rows.title: Election Commission of India - composition, appointment (2023 Act), powers and functions
sub: Group-II M1-B-48: Election Commission of India - composition, powers and functions

secs.t: Composition and status - number, CEC vs EC powers, decision rule, tenure, salary, removal

x: Article 324 occurs in
Part XV
, which deals with elections; Part XV comprises Articles 324 to 329.
The present Commission is a
three
-member body comprising the CEC and two Election Commissioners.
The CEC and the other Election Commissioners have equal powers, and differences are resolved by majority decision.
Although two Election Commissioners were added in 1989, the multi-member form has operated continuously since 1993.
The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge for proven misbehaviour or incapacity.
The CEC may be removed like a Supreme Court judge, requiring an address supported by
a special majority in both Houses of Parliament

secs.t: Powers of Election Commission - Article 324, elections, parties and symbols, disqualification advice

x: Party recognition and symbol allotment are governed by the
Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
, issued under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Article 324.
The Commission can cancel polls in cases such as
rigging or booth capturing
to protect the integrity of the electoral process.
The Model Code of Conduct is not a statute; it rests on Article 324 and applies from the announcement of the election schedule, as recognised in Harbans Singh Jalal (1997).
Electoral-roll revision concerns voter lists, scrutiny concerns nomination papers, expense regulation concerns election expenditure, and delimitation concerns territorial boundaries.
The official designation is
District Election Officer
, although the APPSC usage may refer to the Collector as the District Returning Officer.

secs.t: Chief Election Commissioners - FIRST, FIRST woman, reform era; National Voters' Day

x: T.N. Seshan
, the tenth CEC, is associated with major election reforms, enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and Elector Photo Identity Cards.
The India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM), New Delhi, is the training arm of the Election Commission of India.
The Election Commission was established in 1950, its Golden Jubilee was in 2001, Diamond Jubilee in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.

secs.t: Post-retirement restrictions - constitutional position

x: The Constitution does not expressly bar retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointment.
The Constitution prescribes neither qualifications nor a term of office for the Election Commissioners; these matters are dealt with through the applicable legal framework.

secs.t: CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions

x: The 2023 law is Act No. 49 of 2023 and replaced the 1991 Act.
The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank or above members, and shortlists five names.
The Selection Committee may choose names outside the shortlist prepared by the Search Committee.
An eligible person must hold or have held a post equivalent to Secretary to the Government of India and possess election-management experience.
The CEC and ECs receive equal salaries on a par with a Supreme Court judge.
Election Commissioners other than the CEC can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.
Article 324(2) vests appointment in the President, subject to the provisions of
a law made by Parliament
The 2023 Act was challenged in
Jaya Thakur v. Union of India
, and the matter remained pending as of May 2026.

secs.t: Anoop Baranwal case - interim selection mechanism

x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.
Before the interim mechanism laid down in Anoop Baranwal, the President appointed the CEC and ECs on the advice of
the Prime Minister alone

secs.t: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

x: Decisions are governed by the majority rule and the CEC does not possess an absolute veto over every decision.
The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
The Seshan-era enforcement included arresting politicians who violated the Model Code of Conduct and removing partisan police officers.

secs.t: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

x: Article 329(a) bars judicial challenge to laws relating to delimitation and allotment of seats, while Article 329(b) requires an election to be challenged only through an election petition.

Article 329(a) concerns the bar on challenges to delimitation and seat allotment, Article 329(b) requires an election petition, and Article 71 covers disputes regarding Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.

secs.t: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the state-level officer under the ECI; the SEC conducts local-body elections; the Collector serves as District Election Officer/District Returning Officer; and the ECI conducts Parliamentary and State Legislative elections.
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and can be removed only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge under Article 243K(2).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The removal motion was moved against CEC
Gyanesh Kumar
and was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.
The Supreme Court described the CJI's place as temporary pending legislation, while the petitions challenge the 2:1 government majority in the Selection Committee.

The Commission's dependence on these ministries and its limited authority over internal party democracy and party finances have generated criticism, including the demand for charging its expenses on the Consolidated Fund.

rows.title: Elections - delimitation, model code of conduct, EVM-VVPAT, NOTA, election petitions
sub: Group-II M1-B-76: Elections in India - the electoral system, first-past-the-post, delimitation and reservation of seats
Group-II M1-B-77: Election Commission's powers; the Model Code of Conduct and election machinery

secs.t: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments

x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘
one person, one vote, one value
’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).
Delimitation Commission orders enjoy finality: they cannot be challenged in court or modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies.
The Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 respectively: N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar, J.L. Kapur, J.L. Kapur and Kuldip Singh.
The 87th Amendment substituted the 2001 Census for boundary redrawing while keeping the total number of seats unchanged.
The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.
Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide the constitutional basis for readjustment of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.

secs.t: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

x: SVEEP promotes voter education and turnout; cVIGIL reports Model Code violations; Saksham assists voters with disabilities; and Voter Helpline provides registration, correction, search and complaint services.
cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos, with action envisaged within 100 minutes.
The Voter Helpline app helps users search the electoral roll and file forms and complaints.
The listed categories—service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and persons in preventive detention—are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
The measures include a 1,200-elector cap, mobile-deposit facilities, colour candidate photographs on EVMs and candidate booths just beyond 100 metres from polling stations.

secs.t: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for ten years, up to 2030, under Article 334.
Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies.
ST seats are concentrated in areas with the highest ST population share, SC seats are spread and rotated at delimitation, and reserved constituencies have a common electorate of all voters.
A general election is held at the normal end of a legislature’s term, a mid-term election follows premature dissolution, and a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.

secs.t: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

x: All four circumstances are recognised grounds under Section 100 for declaring an election void, subject to the statutory requirements concerning their effect on the election result where applicable.
From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation are placed in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Sections 169–177.
Section 80 contains the election-petition bar, Section 80A specifies the High Court, Section 81 prescribes 45 days, and Section 100 lists grounds for declaring an election void.

secs.t: National and state party recognition - criteria, number of national parties

x: Recognition is governed by the Election Symbols Order, 1968, whereas registration of political parties is under
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
All four listed conditions are alternative criteria for recognition as a State Party, including the Assembly, Lok Sabha, seat-share and 8% vote conditions.

secs.t: Model Code of Conduct - legal status, authority, enforcement

x: The sequence is 1960 drafting by Kerala, 1968 formalisation by the ECI, 1974 revision, and 1979 addition of Part VII.
Part VII restricts combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport for campaigning, and introducing new schemes or grants after polls are announced.
Part VII, added in 1979, contains provisions concerning
the party in power
and the use of governmental machinery during elections.
The Election Commission may censure a party and may suspend or withdraw recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Symbols Order in appropriate cases.

secs.t: Right to vote - Article 326, nature, first-past-the-post

x: Under the territorial single-member first-past-the-post system, the candidate with the highest plurality of votes wins; an absolute majority is not required.
Difficulty for voters, fragmentation, unstable governments, expense, absence of by-elections and a weaker voter–MP link are cited concerns.
The security deposit is forfeited if the candidate obtains less than
one-sixth of the valid votes

secs.t: NOTA - PUCL case, year, effect on result

x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.
The NOTA symbol is a ballot with a black cross, designed by the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.

secs.t: Universal adult franchise - Article 326, voting age

x: Article 326 permits voting by citizens aged 18 or above subject to disqualifications such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime and corrupt or illegal practice.
The 61st Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

secs.t: Lok Sabha general elections - number, Lok Sabha to year, FIRST election

x: India's first general election was held in
The 1st, 9th, 11th and 16th Lok Sabhas correspond respectively to 1952, 1989, 1996 and 2014.
There have been 18 Lok Sabha general elections so far, and the 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; the 18th was elected in 2024.

secs.t: Electoral provisions in the Constitution - Part XV, Articles 324-329

x: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll and prohibits exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
Article 324
vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
Article 329 bars courts from questioning delimitation laws and provides that an election may be challenged only through an election petition.

secs.t: Electoral rolls - qualifying dates, overseas electors, revisions

x: The qualifying dates are
1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October
Under Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the address given in the Indian passport.
A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.

secs.t: Exit polls and opinion polls - Section 126A

x: Section 126A prohibits conducting or publishing exit polls from the commencement of polling in the first phase until half an hour after polling closes in the last phase.
Opinion polls are barred during the 48 hours before the close of poll under Section 126, while Section 126A governs the longer phase-to-phase restriction on exit polls.

secs.t: Indelible ink - manufacturer, finger, composition

x: The formula for the indelible ink comes from the
National Physical Laboratory
, while Mysore Paints and Varnish Limited manufactures it.
Election indelible ink is applied to the
left forefinger
Silver nitrate
is the key chemical in election indelible ink.
Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election.

secs.t: Commencement of the election process - Sections 14 and 15 RPA

x: Under Section 14 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the President issues the notification for a Lok Sabha election on the Election Commission's recommendation.
The Election Commission
fixes the election schedule and nomination dates, while the President or Governor issues the formal notification as applicable.
The exceptions are where the remaining term is less than one year or the Election Commission, after consulting the Central Government, certifies difficulty in holding the election.

secs.t: Postal ballot and home voting - eligible categories and age

x: The senior-citizen threshold for the absentee-voter postal ballot category is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.

The listed categories include senior citizens aged 85 or above, persons with benchmark disability of 40 per cent or more, essential-service staff on duty, service voters, election-duty electors and persons under preventive detention.

secs.t: Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers

x: The Returning Officer conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result.
At the district level, the District Election Officer is usually the Collector.
The
District Election Officer
receives election expense accounts within 30 days under Section 78.
The Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.

secs.t: RPA 1950 vs RPA 1951 - subjects

x: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 deals with allocation of seats, delimitation and electoral rolls.
Section 29A, concerning registration of political parties, belongs to the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
All four pairs are correctly matched: Sections 19 and 21 belong to the 1950 Act, while Sections 8 and 77–78 belong to the 1951 Act.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly asked for a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and proposed a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
The Bill proposed increasing the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and conducting delimitation on the 2011 Census.
Southern States fear that population-based delimitation would transfer political representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
The EAC-PM proposal envisaged splitting 170 oversized constituencies in order to reach a total of 824 Lok Sabha seats.
The Election Commission was constituted in 1950, is a permanent independent constitutional body, and its IIIDEM provides training to election managers.

rows.title: Electoral reforms - state funding, electoral bonds, criminalisation of politics, RPA 1951 provisions
sub: Group-II M1-B-78: Electoral reforms - committee recommendations, criminalisation of politics, money power
Group-II M1-B-79: Electoral reforms - state funding, electoral bonds, EVM-VVPAT and proposals such as simultaneous elections

secs.t: Committees on electoral reform → subject

x: Exam angle: match committee → subject (APPSC 2025: Indrajit Gupta = electoral reforms; G2 2023 matching Vohra/Gupta/Goswami/Verma).
Exam angle: match-the-committee; Vohra = crime-politics nexus is the most repeated pair.
Exam angle: "Which is NOT on Centre-State relations?" The answer is the
Indrajit Gupta Committee
The J.S. Verma Committee dealt with
criminal-law reform concerning sexual offences
and also urged restrictions on candidates charged with such offences.
The correct sequence is Vohra Committee (1993), Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998), Law Commission 170th Report (1999), and J.S. Verma Committee (2013).

secs.t: One Nation One Election - committee, 129th Amendment Bill

x: All three statements are correct: both the 170th Report and the 2018 draft report supported simultaneous elections, and simultaneous Lok Sabha–Assembly polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967.
Former Chief Justice of India
B.R. Gavai
told the Joint Parliamentary Committee that the Bill did not violate the Basic Structure.
U.U. Lalit and Sanjiv Khanna
raised Basic Structure doubts, whereas B.R. Gavai stated that the Bill did not violate the Basic Structure.

secs.t: Electoral bonds - features, ADR judgment

x: All three statements are correct: a five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.
₹19,083 crore was the amount corresponding to the reported 60% of party
funds from undisclosed sources during 2004–2023
The cited ADR assessment states that 60 per cent of party funds, amounting to ₹19,083 crore, came from undisclosed sources during 2004–23.

secs.t: Election expenditure limits

x: The current limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State or Union Territory is
₹95 lakh
The current Lok Sabha expenditure limit in a smaller State or Union Territory is
₹75 lakh
; the earlier limit was ₹54 lakh.
The limits concern candidates, exclude the travel expenses of 20 star campaigners, and are fixed under Rule 90.

secs.t: RPA 1951 sections → content

x: Section 8 concerns disqualification on conviction, Section 29A registration of political parties, Section 33A criminal-antecedent disclosure, and Section 123 corrupt practices.
The Lok Sabha security deposit is ₹25,000 for general-category candidates, and half of that amount—
—for SC/ST candidates.
The correct sequence is Section 29A (registration), Section 33A (criminal antecedents), Section 81 (election petition), and Section 123 (corrupt practices).

secs.t: Criminalisation of politics

x: A PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending, while 12 special courts have been established for cases involving MPs and MLAs.
Ramesh Dalal v. Union of India held that a sitting MP or MLA convicted and sentenced to imprisonment of two years or more is barred from contesting elections.
The Speaker or Chairman decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, but the decision remains subject to judicial review, as recognised by the Supreme Court in 1992.

secs.t: State funding of elections

x: The Law Commission considered full state funding desirable only if political parties were barred from receiving funds from other sources.
The listed reform ideas include a National Election Fund, democracy vouchers, a zero-cash rule and bringing parties under CAG audits.
The proposed National Election Fund would pool corporate donations and distribute them according to the
vote share
of political parties.

secs.t: Electoral reforms chronology

x: The correct sequence is 61st Amendment and voting-age reduction in 1988, EPIC in 1993, nationwide EVM use in 2004, and VVPAT/NOTA in 2013.
A remote EVM prototype intended for domestic migrants was demonstrated to political parties in
In 2022, the expenditure ceiling for a Lok Sabha candidate in bigger States was raised to
₹95 lakh
ECINET, 100 per cent webcasting and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls are identified with 2025.

secs.t: Contesting from more than one constituency - Section 33(7)

x: Under Section 70 of the Representation of the People Act, the candidate must vacate one seat within
14 days
after being elected from both constituencies.
The Law Commission proposed the principle of one candidate, one seat, while the Election Commission proposed that a candidate vacating a seat should bear the cost of the by-election.

secs.t: RP (Amendment) Act 1996 - nominations, deposits, poll day

x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits, and required more proposers for independents and unrecognised parties.
The poll is countermanded only when
a candidate of a recognised political party
dies.
Section 151A concerns holding a by-election within six months.
All four statements describe provisions associated with election regulation and disqualification under the relevant law.

secs.t: Money power - party expenditure ceiling debate, cash donation limits

x: The perceived loophole is that Section 77 caps candidate expenditure while not imposing a comparable ceiling on the parties’ own election spending.
Evasion may occur by splitting large gifts into amounts below ₹20,000 and by diverting money through surrogate digital advertisements and paid news.
The electoral bonds scheme was struck down by the Supreme Court in Association for Democratic Reforms v Union of India in February 2024.

secs.t: NOTA - case and FIRST use

x: PUCL v Union of India led to the provision of a ‘None of the Above’ option on ballot papers and EVMs.
The first use of NOTA was in the 2013 Assembly elections in
Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi
NOTA was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014, after its initial use in the 2013 Assembly elections.

secs.t: EVMs - FIRST use, capacity, manufacturers, NOTA

x: Exam angle: "first" statements. Parur 1982 = first use; Goa 1999 = first whole State; 2004 = all-India.
M2 EVMs support four ballot units and 64 candidates; an M3 control unit can take up to 24 ballot units and accommodate 384 candidates including NOTA.
The NOTA symbol, depicting a ballot paper with a black cross, was designed by the National Institute of Design at Ahmedabad.

secs.t: VVPAT - FIRST use, versions, court-ordered verification

x: Electronic Voting Machines and VVPATs are manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) and Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL).
Candidates placed second and third may seek verification of 5 per cent of EVMs' burnt memory per Assembly segment within seven days of the result.
The Supreme Court directed counting of VVPAT slips from
five
randomly selected EVMs in each Assembly segment.
In
Subramanian Swamy v ECI
(2013), the Supreme Court held that VVPAT was needed for free and fair polls and required phased introduction.
The 2019 decision raised the random VVPAT-EVM tally from
one to five polling stations per Assembly segment

secs.t: EVM credibility debate - SC rulings, paper-ballot demand

x: The Supreme Court refused to order a return to paper ballots in ADR v ECI (2024).
The Election Commission has stated that EVMs are
still a subject of frequent public questioning

secs.t: Remote voting machine and totaliser proposals

x: The ECI's RVM prototype is intended to enable domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station.

The ECI objected that neither the RPA nor the Conduct of Election Rules provides a legal framework, and that pooling would make booth- and machine-wise checks involving EVMs, VVPATs and Form 17C harder.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Election Commission delisted 808 RUPPs and capped the number of electors per polling station at 1,200.
The Supreme Court made
curbing electoral black money
a core duty of the Election Commission in the 2026 case.
State funding, disqualification on framing of charges and a party spending cap are identified as unfinished agendas.
ASR district
in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of SIR enumeration forms.

rows.title: Indian political parties - evolution, ideology and classification
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-55

secs.t: Party → founder and year of founding (INC, CPI, Jana Sangh, BJP, DMK, BSP, SP, AAP, Republican Party of India, Swatantra)

x: Exam angle: the party founded by Ambedkar is the
Republican Party of India
. BSP was founded in
by
Kanshi Ram
, and AAP in
Although the CPI dates its initial association with M.N. Roy and others at Tashkent in 1920, it was formally established at the
Kanpur conference

secs.t: Leaders → party (national presidents, FIRST presidents, founders, regional leaders)

x: Madduri Annapurnayya
was the first Andhra leader in Bose’s Forward Bloc in 1939.
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and others were associated with the
Andhra Swaraj Party
Annapurnaiah joined the CSP after the Salt Satyagraha, became the first Andhra leader in the Forward Bloc in 1939, and spent four years in jail during the Second World War.

secs.t: Chronological order of party formation

x: The DMK was formed in 1949, the Jana Sangh in 1951, the Swatantra Party in 1959 and the Republican Party of India in 1956–57.
The Indian National Congress was formed in 1885, the CPI in 1925, the Forward Bloc in 1939 and the DMK in 1949.
The Janata Party was formed in 1977, the BJP in 1980, the TDP in 1982 and the BSP in 1984.

secs.t: Splits and mergers → parent party and year (CPI and CPI(M), NCP, Congress splits, Janata Party, Janata Dal family)

x: The Janata Party was formed in 1977 through the merger of Congress (O), Jana Sangh, the Bharatiya Lok Dal and the Socialists.
Congress for Democracy was associated with
Jagjivan Ram, H.N. Bahuguna and Nandini Satpathy
The Janata Dal was formed on 11 October 1988 through the merger of
Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal

secs.t: Party concepts - inner-party democracy, party system, social bases of parties, Kamaraj Plan

x: The TDP rapidly gained power by mobilising the sentiment of “
Telugu atma gauravam
”, or Telugu self-respect.
The Vohra Committee report of 1993 dealt with the
criminalisation of politics
and the nexus between criminals and political actors.
Pressure groups
are referred to as the “Anonymous Empire” because they seek influence without directly seeking governmental power.

secs.t: Classification - national, state, registered unrecognised parties, ideology spectrum

x: The Election Commission recognises political parties under the
Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968
The free symbols list contained 184 symbols in May 2025.
The six listed national parties are BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP.
Indian parties span the left, centre and right, although most parties tend to cluster near the centre.

secs.t: Legal framework - Section 29A RPA registration, party constitution, internal democracy debate

x: The party constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity.
Political parties entered the constitutional framework through the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment in 1985.
The decision restricted the Election Commission's deregistration power, while recognising exceptions involving fraud, loss of allegiance and a party being declared unlawful.

secs.t: Party funding - disclosure rules, electoral bonds ruling, contribution reports

x: Annual disclosure is required for donors contributing more than
The electoral-bond scheme was struck down in ADR v. Union of India on 15 February 2024.
The Indrajit Gupta Committee proposed partial State funding in kind; the 170th Report addressed spending and transparency; and the 255th Report supported limited deregistration power.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Janata Party was formed in 1977, the TDP in 1982, the multi-party coalition era began with the 1989 election, and the YSRCP was formed in 2011.
The Congress system covered 1952–77, the transition and first alternation 1977–89, the coalition era 1989–2014 and the BJP majority phase began in 2014.

rows.title: Party system in India - one-party dominance, multi-party and coalition eras
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-55

secs.t: FIRST non-Congress government at the Centre - year, party, PM

x: Exam angle: "first non-Congress government" = 1977 (not 1989, which was the first non-Congress *coalition of the multi-party era*).
The Janata Party formed the first non-Congress government at the Centre in 1977, with Morarji Desai as Prime Minister.
The Janata Party government of 1977 was the first non-Congress government at the Centre and was stable initially because it possessed a Lok Sabha majority.

secs.t: One-party dominance - 'Congress system', scholars, election that ended it

x: Exam angle: match the election to the claim - 1967 (States), 1971, 1977 (Centre), 1989 (end of Congress system, multi-party era).
Kothari is associated with the Congress system, Morris-Jones with one-party dominance alongside competition, and Weiner with Party Building in a New Nation.
The
1989 Lok Sabha election
marked the end of the Congress system; Congress lost power, remained the single largest party, and chose to sit in opposition.

secs.t: Coalition governments at the Centre - PMs, fronts, minority governments

x: Chandra Shekhar
headed the Samajwadi Janata Party minority government from 1990 to 1991, with outside support from Congress.
The United Front governments during 1996–98 were headed successively by Deve Gowda and Gujral and received outside support from Congress.
The NDA government led by A.B. Vajpayee governed from 1998 to 2004 and involved parties that had no prior experience of working together; it governed for about six years.

secs.t: Consequences of coalition politics - stability, federalism, role of parties

x: Coalition politics may promote consensus, but the need for compromise can slow decisions, cause policy reversals or delays, and dilute strong measures.
Coalition politics creates checks and balances because no single party ordinarily holds absolute power, while regional parties gain representation in national policy.
Defections and horse-trading led to the anti-defection law, introduced through the Tenth Schedule by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.

secs.t: Lok Sabha results - seats of major parties (9th, 11th, 13th, 14th)

x: In the Ninth Lok Sabha of 1989, INC won 197 seats, Janata Dal 143 and BJP 85; INC was the largest party.
The BJP was the largest party in the Eleventh Lok Sabha of 1996 with 161 seats, while Congress had 140.
In 2014, BJP won 282 of the 543 Lok Sabha seats, marking the first single-party majority since 1984.

secs.t: Coalition governments in states - after the fourth general election

x: The coalition governments formed in several States after the fourth general election were commonly known as
Samyukta Vidhayak Dal governments
Except
Tamil Nadu
, where the DMK governed alone, almost every opposition-ruled State had a coalition after the 1967 elections.
Kerala’s coalition politics is principally organised around the Congress-led UDF and CPI(M)-led LDF, with the leading party’s legislature leader becoming Chief Minister.

secs.t: Nature of the Indian party system - multi-party character, fragmentation

x: Regional, linguistic, caste, religious and class divisions together account for the multi-party character of Indian politics.
A two-party system generally presumes one dominant axis of political or social division, unlike India’s multiple cleavages.
Cadre parties are centred more on organised leadership, while mass parties seek extensive popular participation and membership.

secs.t: Common Minimum Programme and coordination committees

x: The United Front adopted its Common Minimum Programme in 1996, the NDA its National Agenda for Governance in 1998, and the UPA its National Common Minimum Programme in 2004.
Coalition partners generally govern through a Common Minimum Programme and a coordination committee representing the constituents.

secs.t: Party systems in states - bipolar vs multipolar, Andhra Pradesh pattern

x: Congress dominance continued until 1983; thereafter the principal contest was between Congress and the Telugu Desam Party, and since 2014 it has been between the Telugu Desam Party and the YSR Congress Party.
The arrangement is a coalition in which a regional party is the dominant partner and the Bharatiya Janata Party supports it.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated distribution records the Bharatiya Janata Party as ruling alone in 11 States.
The multi-party era of 1989–2014 ended when the BJP won a majority on its own in the 2014 general election.
The Justice Party-era awakening of
non-Brahmin agrarian castes
laid the social base for regional parties in Andhra.

rows.title: Regional parties in India and in Andhra Pradesh - rise, role and impact
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-55

secs.t: AP regional parties - founder and founding year

x: The Lok Satta Party was founded by Jayaprakash Narayan in 2006.
Praja Shanti Party was founded by K. A. Paul.

secs.t: TDP - founding, first victory, Lok Sabha opposition status, National Front

x: The TDP won power in the January 1983 Assembly election, roughly
nine months
after its formation, marking one of the fastest rises of a political party.
With 30 seats in 1984, the TDP became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha and was the first regional party to attain that position.

secs.t: Regional parties across India - state and founder

x: All three statements are correct: AIADMK–M. G. Ramachandran–1972, Shiv Sena–Bal Thackeray–1966, and JJP–Dushyant Chautala–2018.
The DMK began with anti-Brahmin, anti-North and anti-Hindi positions and demanded
Dravidanadu
; it later scaled back these demands and formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under Annadurai.
Shiv Sena mobilised around the idea of “Bombay for Maharashtrians” and the demand for jobs for the sons of the soil.

secs.t: Regional parties in chronological order of founding

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 keyed order
DMK, TDP, BSP, SP
The correct order is DMK (1949), Shiv Sena (1966), TDP (1982) and BSP (1984).
The sequence is AGP (1985), Samajwadi Party (1992), BJD and RJD (1997), TRS (2001), and YSRCP (2011).

secs.t: End of continuous Congress rule in AP - year and party

x: 1983 Assembly election
: the
TDP
ended Congress's unbroken rule in Andhra Pradesh since the State's formation (1956).

secs.t: Regional vs national parties - identify, states ruled

x: The
Telugu Desam Party
is included among the State or unrecognised parties in the cited list, whereas AAP, BSP and NPP are listed as national parties.
The cited sequence states that the BJP defeated BJD in Odisha in 2024, AAP in Delhi in 2025 and Trinamool Congress in West Bengal in 2026.

secs.t: Rise of regional parties - linguistic, caste and regional bases

x: The identified causes include linguistic and cultural identity, regional economic neglect, and the failure of national parties to accommodate State leaders.
After 1989, coalition arithmetic increased the national importance of regional parties because their parliamentary support could determine government formation and survival.
The Andhra non-Brahmin agrarian castes identified as becoming politically awakened during the Justice Party era were
Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas

secs.t: Impact - coalition politics, federal bargaining, special category demands

x: Regional parties have acted as coalition kingmakers, supplied Speakers and Union Ministers, and provided votes necessary for government survival.
The material links more genuine federal bargaining to the period after 1989, when coalition politics increased the negotiating power of regional parties.
Regional parties can improve representation of backward regions and promote balanced development, but may also encourage parochialism and instability.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The developments mentioned were the Trinamool Congress defeat in West Bengal, defections involving the specified parties, and the emphasis on vote share as an indicator of regional support.
Vote share
is considered an important indicator of the extent of regional support, whereas seats alone may not fully reflect that support.

rows.title: Recognition of national and state parties - criteria and the Symbols Order
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-55

secs.t: National party criteria - paragraph 6B of the Symbols Order

x: Exam angle: distractors use "2 or more States", "4% / 10% / 15% of votes" - all wrong; APPSC-G2 2025: every listed condition was valid, so the key was "None of the above".
The second route requires at least 6% of valid votes in four or more States at the last Lok Sabha or Assembly elections and at least four Lok Sabha seats.

secs.t: National parties - present number and list, recognitions and derecognitions

x: The April 2023 review derecognised CPI, NCP and AITC and recognised AAP as a National Party.
The National People's Party (
NPP
), based in Meghalaya, was the first North-Eastern party to obtain National Party status.
DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party
are not National Parties in the classification referred to here.

secs.t: Recognising vs registering authority - Symbols Order vs Section 29A RPA

x: Registration is under Section 29A; recognition is under the Symbols Order; symbol reservation and allotment are governed by the 1968 Order; Article 324 provides the constitutional basis of the ECI.
The ECI's deregistration power is limited and may arise in cases such as fraud, ceasing allegiance or an unlawful declaration.

secs.t: State party criteria - vote share and seat combinations

x: A party can qualify through at least 6% of valid Lok Sabha votes in the State combined with one Lok Sabha seat from that State.
A party may qualify by winning one Lok Sabha seat for every 25 Lok Sabha seats allotted to the State.
The later-added 8% route requires 8% of valid votes in the State and does not require the party to win a seat.

secs.t: Election Symbols Order 1968 - reserved vs free symbols, split disputes (Sadiq Ali)

x: Free symbols are allotted from a notified list to RUPPs and independent candidates, subject to the applicable conditions.
An RUPP can obtain a common symbol when it contests two Lok Sabha seats or 5% of the Assembly seats, subject to the applicable rules.
Paragraph 16A empowers the ECI to suspend or withdraw recognition for defiance of the Model Code of Conduct.

secs.t: Recognition benefits - symbol, broadcast, star campaigners, proposers

x: Recognised parties receive two free sets of electoral rolls, broadcast or telecast time on Akashvani and Doordarshan, and consultation by the ECI.

The stated rules provide tax exemption on donations under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, require disclosure of donors contributing above Rs 20,000, and require donations above Rs 2,000 to be made through cheque or bank transfer.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Trinamool rebel MPs chose a merger rather than pursuing a paragraph 15 symbol claim before the Election Commission.
Criticisms include prolonged factional litigation, allegations of bias, rising RUPP numbers and voter confusion arising from similar symbols.
The stated figure was
about 750
contestants out of more than 2,800 registered but unrecognised political parties in 2024.

rows.title: Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions - composition, functions, removal
sub: Group-II M1-B-49: Union and State Public Service Commissions - composition, functions and removal

secs.t: Appointment and removal of UPSC and SPSC members (Art. 316-317)

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2019 - SPSC chairman
appointed by Governor, removed by President
Exam angle: "Governor appoints, President removes" for SPSC chairman is the favourite trap.
The strength of UPSC is not constitutionally fixed, but it usually consists of about
9–11 members
including the Chairman.
UPSC members retire at 65 years and SPSC members at 62 years, subject in both cases to the six-year term.
Misbehaviour includes
being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit
under Article 317(4).
The
President
appoints an Acting Chairman during a vacancy in the office of the Chairman or during the Chairman's absence or inability to function.

secs.t: Functions of UPSC - consulted and not consulted (Art. 320, 321)

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2022 - "manner of reservation" is
not
a UPSC function.
The disciplinary consultation of UPSC may cover censure, withholding of increments, demotion and removal, among other disciplinary penalties.
UPSC is consulted on claims for pension in respect of injuries sustained in government service and claims for reimbursement of legal expenses incurred in defending official actions.
Non-acceptance of UPSC advice requires the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; a Ministry cannot reject it alone.
Article 321 permits extension of UPSC functions to personnel systems of local bodies, corporations and public institutions.
The President may exclude posts from consultation with UPSC, while the Governor may exclude posts from consultation with the SPSC through regulations.

secs.t: APPSC - establishment, headquarters, composition

x: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission came into existence on
1 November 1956
, with the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
After bifurcation, APPSC continued for residuary Andhra Pradesh, Telangana constituted TSPSC, and the Governor appoints APPSC members.
The APPSC conducts recruitment examinations for State services and examinations for the lower judicial service under Article 234.

secs.t: Joint State Public Service Commission

x: Although Public Service Commissions are constitutionally recognised, a Joint State Public Service Commission is established by a Parliamentary Act and is therefore statutory.
The Joint State Public Service Commission submits its report to each concerned Governor, who lays it before the relevant State Legislature.
Punjab and Haryana had a Joint State Public Service Commission briefly after the reorganisation associated with 1966.

secs.t: Articles 315-323 → content

x: Article 318
empowers the competent authority to make regulations regarding conditions of service and staff of a Public Service Commission.
Article 319
provides the post-office restrictions applicable to the Chairman and members of Public Service Commissions.
Article 322 provides that the expenses of Public Service Commissions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or the State, as applicable.

secs.t: SPSC members - term, age, strength, post-retirement eligibility

x: A former SPSC member may become UPSC Chairman or member, or Chairman of the same or another SPSC, but cannot accept any other government employment.
The age limit is 65 years for UPSC members and 62 years for SPSC and Joint State Public Service Commission members, subject in each case to the six-year term.

secs.t: UPSC history

x: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a
Public Service Commission
; the Federal Public Service Commission came later under the Government of India Act, 1935.
The Federal Public Service Commission became the UPSC on
26 January 1950
, and its members continued under Article 378.
ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the
Montagu-Chelmsford reforms

secs.t: Annual report and non-acceptance of advice

x: The UPSC annual report is accompanied by a memorandum explaining cases in which its advice was not accepted.
Every case of non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by
the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
; an individual ministry cannot reject the advice on its own.
The UPSC report follows the President-Parliament route, while an SPSC report follows the Governor-State Legislature route.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Paper leaks, flawed evaluation, delays and litigation are identified as major concerns, with the Telangana 2023 and Bihar 2024 examinations cited as examples.
Satyendranath Tagore was selected in 1863 and is recorded as the first Indian to clear the ICS in 1864.
The Indian Civil Services Act, 1861 permitted only limited Indian entry, and Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian to clear the ICS examination in 1864.

rows.title: Finance Commission - composition, terms of reference, functions; 15th and 16th Finance Commission
sub: Group-II M1-B-47: Finance Commission - composition, functions and recent recommendations

secs.t: Statement-based - nature, composition, qualifications, advisory

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 incorrect statement - "
Article 290
provides for the FC" (it is Art. 280; Art. 290 deals with pensions ).
Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the
Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951
, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
The reporting arrangement includes annual or need-based reports, transmission of State-related reports to the Governor and laying before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.

The reports are submitted to the President, laid before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum, and State-related portions go to the concerned Governor; major policy matters require consultation with the commissions.

secs.t: Finance Commission number → award period and key recommendations

x: The 14th Finance Commission made tax devolution the main route instead of grants and ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction.
The 15th Finance Commission retained the 41% share and added
demographic performance and tax effort
as considerations.
Area and demographic performance received lower weights, forest and ecology remained unchanged, and tax and fiscal effort was dropped.
Heatwaves and lightning
were added as notified disasters on the advice of the 16th Finance Commission.
The Fourteenth Finance Commission shifted the emphasis from Plan grants to tax devolution, and State Plan grants of about 3 per cent of the divisible pool were discontinued.

secs.t: Finance Commission and AP

x: Andhra Pradesh sought higher vertical devolution and criteria addressing capital-city and infrastructure costs resulting from post-bifurcation imbalances.

The Sixteenth Finance Commission period is associated with ₹7.91 lakh crore for local bodies, approximately ₹4.4 lakh crore for rural bodies, ₹3.6 lakh crore for urban bodies, and an urban share raised to 45 per cent.

The stated allocations are ₹16,627 crore for rural local bodies, ₹12,158 crore for urban local bodies, ₹6,125 crore for disaster purposes and up to ₹5,000 crore each for wastewater projects in Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: 16th Finance Commission - constitution, terms, award

x: The Terms of Reference of the 16th Finance Commission were approved by the Cabinet on
29 November 2023
The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023, had constitution-based Terms of Reference, and was the first to use Contribution to GDP as a criterion.
The 14th Finance Commission's increase of the States' share to 42 per cent was
the largest increase ever
The 14th Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions retained or recommended 41 per cent.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 15th Finance Commission was the first to reduce the vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent, largely in the context of the change in Jammu and Kashmir's status.
Cesses and surcharges are not generally part of the divisible pool, so their increasing use shrinks the pool available for devolution.
Kerala
was identified as facing fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission gave it neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants.

rows.title: Comptroller and Auditor General - appointment, duties, types of audit, audit reports and PAC linkage
sub: Group-II M1-B-50: Comptroller and Auditor General of India - appointment, duties and audit reports

secs.t: CAG appointment and removal

x: V. Narahari Rao
was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
The CAG takes the oath before the President, in the form prescribed in the
Third Schedule
The CAG receives a salary equal to that of a Supreme Court judge.
Salary, leave, pension and retirement age cannot be varied to the CAG’s disadvantage after appointment.
No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament
K. Sanjay Murthy
is mentioned as the CAG of India for 2026.

secs.t: CAG duties - Art. 149, 1971 Act; what he does not control

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2017 wrong statement - "CAG controls the entire financial system of the country".
The CAG’s duties, powers and conditions of service are governed by the Comptroller and Auditor General’s Act of 1971, made under Articles 148 and 149.
The CAG audits public finances but does not control the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund.
In the case of secret service expenditure, the CAG must
accept the certificate of the competent authority
and cannot audit the expenditure in the ordinary manner.

secs.t: Articles 148-151 → content

x: Article 150 provides that the form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG.

secs.t: Audit reports - Art. 151 and the PAC

x: Article 151
deals with the submission and laying of the CAG’s audit reports before the appropriate legislature.
Reports relating to public sector undertakings are referred to the
Committee on Public Undertakings
, while the PAC examines the other relevant CAG reports.
The CAG acts as the PAC’s
friend, philosopher and guide
by assisting it in examining audit findings.

secs.t: Types of audit

x: A legal and regulatory audit is obligatory and examines whether money was legally available and spent in accordance with applicable rules.
Financial attest audit is an obligatory audit concerned with the truthfulness of accounts and their conformity with the reporting framework.
Propriety audit
is discretionary and examines wisdom, faithfulness and economy, including possible extravagance in expenditure.

secs.t: CAG and accounts - separation, state audits, charged expenditure

x: Although Union accounts were separated from audit in 1976,
the CAG continues to keep most State accounts
The salary and office expenses of the CAG
are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to vote.
Under Article 151(2), State audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature.

secs.t: CAG's audit of PSUs, local bodies - limits

x: LIC
and RBI are cited as examples of entities subject to wholly private audit.
Central Warehousing Corporation and IFCI
are examples where private auditors are appointed on the CAG's advice and the CAG carries out a supplementary audit.
The CAG cannot audit secret service expenditure and instead accepts a certificate from the competent authority.

secs.t: Criticisms and landmark reports

x: The 2010 2G spectrum report, prepared during Vinod Rai's tenure, referred to a presumptive loss of
₹1.76 lakh crore
The coal block allocation report of 2012 referred to a presumptive loss of
₹1.86 lakh crore
All three are identified as debates concerning CAG auditing: the presumptive-loss method, the boundary between policy and execution, and delayed reports.
Former CAG
Vinod Rai
authored “When Audit Matters.”.

secs.t: Term compared with other constitutional posts

x: Exam angle: "whose term is longest - President, LS member, CAG, VP?" →
CAG
The CAG, CEC and UPSC member have a term of six years or until 65, while the President, Vice-President and ordinarily a Lok Sabha member have five-year terms.

secs.t: Official full name

x: The official name is
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

secs.t: CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

x: The Act provides for
compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators
The 1976 amendment separated accounts from audit and relieved the CAG of compiling Union Government accounts through departmentalisation.

secs.t: CAGs by number - FIRST and present

x: V. Narahari Rao was the first CAG, in 1948.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The PAC was under
K.C. Venugopal
when it pulled up the Railways over the bio-toilet findings.
The CAG was
auditing 101 cities for ease of living
, including urban-mobility concerns.
The 5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit hosted by India in 2026 was associated with the theme of
ease of living and urban mobility
The CAG is using AI/ML-based audits to detect fraud in welfare schemes and is expanding remote audits.

rows.title: Attorney General and Advocate General; Solicitor General
sub: Group-II M1-B-51: Attorney General of India and the Advocate General of the State

secs.t: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - "qualified to be an SC judge" and "advises GoI" are correct; a "fixed term" statement is wrong (LENS Oct 2025 practice question also tests "fixed five-year term" - false).
Article 76 requires the Attorney General to satisfy the qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge, including the stated judicial, advocacy or eminent-jurist qualifications.

secs.t: Highest law officer of India

x: Exam angle: "Who is the highest law officer?" → AG (not CJI, not Law Minister).

The Solicitor General is the second law officer, assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union; the Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, while the Attorney General and Solicitor General occupy the first and second positions among Union law officers respectively.

secs.t: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

x: Article 165 requires the Advocate General to be qualified for appointment as a
Judge of a High Court
Article 177 permits the Advocate General to speak and take part in either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
Additional Advocates General
assist the office of the Advocate General
in discharging its legal responsibilities.

secs.t: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

x: The correct matching is Attorney General—Article 76, Advocate General—Article 165, Attorney General's parliamentary rights—Article 88, and Advocate General's State Legislature rights—Article 177.
The Attorney General's remuneration is determined by the President, while the Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the Governor.

secs.t: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

x: M.C. Setalvad was the first, followed by Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal and R. Venkataramani in the sequence represented here.
R. Venkataramani
is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026.
R. Venkataramani was first appointed Attorney General of India in 2022 and was subsequently reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.

secs.t: Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General

x: References concerning the Attorney General go through the Ministry of Law; law officers conventionally resign after a change of government; and only the Attorney General is constitutionally created, under Article 76.
The five reappointed Additional Solicitors General were Vikramjit Banerjee, K.M. Nataraj, S.V. Raju, N. Venkataraman and Aishwarya Bhati.
Under the Advocates Act, 1961, the Attorney General and Solicitor General are ex officio members of the
Bar Council of India
Section 98 amended
Section 15A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
in relation to the Telangana Legislative Council.

secs.t: Advocates General of AP → current holder

x: The Advocate General is a constitutional office under Article 165, appointed by the Governor and holding office at the Governor’s pleasure.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The convention is criticised because the resignation of all law officers after a change of government can make the offices appear tied to the ruling party rather than being institutionally independent.
The Supreme Court asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to communicate directions to all Advocates General concerning
facilities for senior citizens

secs.t: Commission → article and amendment

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2022 - NCBC got constitutional status by the
102nd
Amendment.
NCST was established on 19 February 2004 under
Article 338A
, inserted through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
All four statements correctly describe the NCST: its constitutional basis is Article 338A, created by the 89th Amendment, operational from 19 February 2004, with civil-court powers.

secs.t: Functions and powers

x: All the listed powers are available to the Commission while inquiring into matters, including summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavit evidence, requisitioning records and issuing witness commissions.
The NCSC, NCST and NCBC exercise civil-court powers during investigations and inquiries, including summoning persons, examining them on oath, calling for documents and requisitioning public records.
The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.
The NHRC has civil-court powers in inquiries, while the NCM’s inquiry powers arise from its statutory framework and should not be described as automatic or unrestricted constitutional powers.

secs.t: Composition of NCSC and NCST

x: The NCST was set up with effect from
19 February 2004
following the bifurcation authorised by the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
The 65th Amendment, 1990 replaced the earlier Special Officer arrangement with a constitutional, multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members are appointed by the President by warrant under the President's hand and seal.

secs.t: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC

x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.

The Kalelkar Commission was established in 1953, the statutory NCBC was created in 1993, constitutional status came through the 102nd Amendment in 2018, and State power was restored by the 105th Amendment in 2021.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Niranjan Jyoti
headed the National Commission for Backward Classes in 2026.
Harjit Singh Grewal
headed the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026.
The criticism identified is that recommendations are advisory only and that the National Commission for Minorities has experienced long vacancies, a matter noted by the Delhi High Court in 2026.

secs.t: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

x: Exam angle: match-the-Act-with-year pairs; "which of these is NOT a constitutional body".
Exam angle: a list-matching question on bodies and Articles; "NHRC is constitutional" is a trap.
NCW, NCPCR and CARA are the three statutory bodies under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
The NCBC acquired constitutional status under the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018, and Article 338B.
Before receiving constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment, the NCBC functioned as a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.

secs.t: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

x: The NCW may review laws, suggest amendments, take suo motu notice and commission special studies.
The five-day Jan Sunwai was held from 9 to 13 March 2026 in five zones, including Nellore, Guntur, Vijayawada and Rajamahendravaram, on directions from the NCW.
All four statements correctly describe functions or responsibilities associated with the NCW, including review, suo motu action, inspection and consultation on relevant policy matters.

secs.t: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

x: After the NCSK Act lapsed in 2004, the Commission continued as a non-statutory body through
periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.
Hardeep Singh Gill
was the Vice-Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis as reported in 2026.

secs.t: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee

x: The Paris Principles were adopted in October 1991, the Ordinance was promulgated on 28 September 1993, the NHRC was established on 12 October 1993, and UNGA endorsement followed on 20 December 1993.
Jains
are among the six notified minority communities, along with Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis.
All four statements are correct: the UDHR dates to 1948, the ICCPR and ICESCR to 1966, CEDAW to 1979 and the Convention against Torture to 1984.
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson; the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Union Home Minister and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha are members.
The 2019 amendment broadened eligibility for the NHRC chairperson and included the specified commission chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as deemed members.

secs.t: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment

x: During inquiries, the NHRC has the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, calling for documents and receiving evidence on affidavit.
The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to matters in the State List and Concurrent List, but it cannot inquire into a matter already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.

secs.t: NCPCR - CPCR Act 2005, POCSO and RTE monitoring

x: The NCPCR was established under the
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
, although it monitors the implementation of several other child-related laws.
Section
of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 concerns the 25 per cent reservation of seats for children in specified private unaided schools.

secs.t: AP State Human Rights Commission and AP State Commission for Women - establishment, location

x: K.S. Jawahar
was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes while reviewing SC/ST welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore.
The Commission investigated 281 abortion registrations in the Eluru Agency areas, including allegations of fake-abortion registrations.
Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.

secs.t: Chairpersons of national commissions - present and first holders

x: Vijaya Rahatkar chairs NCW, Justice V. Ramasubramanian chairs NHRC, Kishor Makwana chairs NCSC and Antar Singh Arya chairs NCST.
Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson, Justice Ranganath Misra the first NHRC Chairperson, Suraj Bhan the first separate NCSC Chairperson and Kunwar Singh the first NCST Chairperson.
Harjit Singh Grewal
was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term in 2026.

secs.t: State counterparts - State Minority Commissions, SCPCR, SHRC, State Commissions for Women

x: SCPCRs operate under the CPCR Act, 2005, alongside the NCPCR, and address child-rights directions including school menstrual-hygiene measures.
After the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson may be
a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
The issue was raised in the context of States having few appeals under the Right to Information framework.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The NHRC sought reports in connection with the alleged custodial death of
Gade Sai Krishna
A long vacancy affected the NCM, and an adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026; the NHRC was not dissolved.
Reports were sought from the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police, Chief Secretary and State Human Rights Commission in relation to the alleged custodial death.

secs.t: Lokpal Bill history - first introduction, attempts, year passed, Anna Hazare movement

x: Exam angle: "first Lokpal Bill introduced in" =
Exam angle: the options mix 1968 (first introduced) with 1969 (first passed by the Lok Sabha) - read the verb.
The correct order is introduction in 1968, passage by the Lok Sabha in 1969, re-introduction in 2008, and passage by Parliament in December 2013.

secs.t: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 - assent, commencement, composition, selection committee, jurisdiction

x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on
27 March 2019
after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
The
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
The Search Committee is constituted by the Selection Committee, prepares a panel, has at least seven persons and must satisfy the specified representation requirement.
The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal.
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
The Prime Minister’s excluded areas include international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space.
An inquiry against the Prime Minister requires approval of the full Bench by at least a two-thirds majority, and the inquiry is held in camera.
The selection committee comprises the Prime Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and an eminent jurist.
A complaint under the Lokpal framework must be filed within
seven years
of the offence.
The Lokpal’s inquiry wing under Section 11 and its prosecution wing were reported as still not fully staffed.
The Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019, Justice Ghose left office on 27 May 2022, and Justice Khanwilkar became Chairperson on 10 March 2024.

secs.t: Lokayukta - first state, appointing authority, tenure changes, CM within ambit

x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the
Governor
Lokayuktas generally rely on State investigating agencies, and their recommendations are advisory in many States.
Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta; Punjab has officials designated as Lokpal; Maharashtra has a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.
Lokayuktas are established under the respective State Acts, and there is no uniformity among States regarding jurisdiction, coverage of the Chief Minister or judicial qualifications.

secs.t: Lokpal working - first Lokpal, chairpersons, complaints, prosecution wing

x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.
Justice Lingappa Narayana Swamy is a judicial member, while Sushil Chandra and Pankaj Kumar are non-judicial members.
After Justice Ghose left office on 27 May 2022, the post remained vacant for about two years and functioned under an acting Chairperson until the next Chairperson assumed office in March 2024.
The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal's 12 November 2025 order sanctioning a chargesheet in the Mahua Moitra matter and held that the law had been 'mutilated'.
Following criticism, the Lokpal cancelled a tender for seven BMW cars valued at approximately ₹5 crore through a full-bench resolution.
The listed criticisms are the absence of power of prior sanction, practical exclusion of Group C and D matters in favour of the CVC, and dependence on the CBI.
Following the Delhi High Court’s decision in the Mahua Moitra case, the Supreme Court agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure in March 2026.

secs.t: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP

x: The Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta have differentiated functions, and the stated coverage includes the Chief Minister and MLAs.
Governor S. Abdul Nazeer
appointed Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao under Section 3(1), on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.
All four figures are reported for the 2025 annual report: 7,431 cases handled, 3,654 disposed, ₹15.29 crore recovered and 148 RTI applications processed.
The total consisted of
3,106 fresh cases and 4,325 backlog cases
The full-time post was vacant for most of 2025, P. Rajani performed the functions, and the stated order concerned EPF/ESI dues of outsourced staff in 32 KGBVs in Srikakulam.

secs.t: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee

x: The First ARC recommended two tiers: Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for the States, in its 1966 interim report on the Problems of Redressal of Citizens’ Grievances.
The First ARC’s recommendation dates to 1966, the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007, and the Santhanam Committee operated during 1962–64.
The correct sequence is Santhanam Committee (1962–64), First ARC recommendation (1966), Vineet Narain judgment (1997), and CVC Act (2003).

secs.t: Civil society pressure - India Against Corruption, Anna Hazare, Jan Lokpal drafting panel

x: India Against Corruption was led by
Anna Hazare
and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.
The fasts were held at Jantar Mantar in April 2011 and at Ramlila Maidan in August 2011.
All four statements correctly identify the chairpersons and members of the Government and civil society sides of the April 2011 Joint Drafting Committee.

secs.t: Ombudsman idea - Sweden, Indian equivalent; who coined 'Lokpal'

x: The Ombudsman institution was first set up in
Sweden
Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.
Maharashtra
was the first State to establish a Lokayukta, in 1971.

secs.t: Lokpal and Lokayuktas (Amendment) Act 2016 - asset declaration

x: The 2016 amendment provided that the form and manner would be prescribed by the Central Government; it did not place the prescription in the Constitution.
The 2016 amendment retained the obligation to declare assets and liabilities but authorised the Central Government to prescribe the form and manner of declaration.

secs.t: Mandate on states to set up Lokayuktas - time limit

x: There is no uniform model under which every State has identical jurisdiction, Chief Minister coverage or qualifications.
Odisha
was the first State to pass a Lokayukta law, in 1970.
The years are Rajasthan—1973, Bihar—1974, Uttar Pradesh—1975 and Andhra Pradesh—1983.
Odisha enacted its law in 1970, Maharashtra in 1971, Madhya Pradesh in 1981 and Karnataka in 1984.

secs.t: Powers - inquiry wing, prosecution wing, CBI superintendence, attachment of property

x: The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the
Prevention of Corruption Act
The Lokpal’s framework includes prosecution before the Special Court, specified CBI superintendence, civil-court powers and attachment or confiscation of tainted property during pending prosecution.
The three SP-level areas are general matters, economic and banking matters, and cyber matters.
Conducting elections to State Legislative Assemblies
is not a Lokpal function.

secs.t: Time limits for inquiry and investigation

x: The Inquiry Wing is required to submit its report within
60 days
after a reference.
A preliminary inquiry ordinarily has a 90-day limit and may be extended by another 90 days.
Investigation is to be completed within six months and may be extended by a further six months.
The Special Court trial is to be completed within one year, with extension permitted up to two years.

secs.t: Lokayukta's jurisdiction over CM, ministers, legislators - state-wise

x: The Chief Minister is included within the Lokayukta’s jurisdiction in
Himachal Pradesh
, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
MLAs are listed as covered in Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Assam.
Sexual harassment, caste discrimination and violence are not among the investigation subjects listed under the stated Rajasthan provision.

secs.t: Origin - body that first recommended state Lokayuktas

x: The First Administrative Reforms Commission, chaired by Morarji Desai, recommended
a Lokayukta in every State and a Lokpal at the Centre
The First Administrative Reforms Commission functioned from 1966 to 1970 and was chaired by Morarji Desai.

secs.t: Karnataka Lokayukta model and its major reports

x: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under
Justice N. Santosh Hegde
The report led to the Chief Minister’s resignation, the arrest of former minister G. Janardhana Reddy, cancellation of mining leases and recovery of thousands of crores.
Chandru Lamani was trapped by the Karnataka Lokayukta Police while taking a
₹5 lakh
bribe.

secs.t: AP Lokayukta seat after bifurcation
Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.
Many Lokayuktas lack an independent investigating wing and therefore depend on the State police or the Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation.
The
Lokayukta
receives citizens’ complaints, conducts inquiries, makes recommendations and reports to the Governor.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
The inquiry and prosecution wings have not remained fully staffed; their continuing staffing problems are among the criticisms.
The parliamentary standing committee noted that the Director of Inquiry and inquiry-wing staffing were
still in process more than a decade after the Act
The split verdict dealt with prior approval under Section 17A, including the binding-opinion qualification and the contrary view that the provision is unconstitutional.
Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if it was based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal or Lokayukta.
Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants.

secs.t: Appointing authority pairing (CIC, SIC, CVC, Lokpal and others)

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025 keyed "CIC by President, SIC by Governor" as the correct pairs, and CM + LoP + CM-nominated minister for the SIC panel. The
Chief Justice is not a member

The President appoints the Lokpal Chairperson and members on the recommendation of a committee including the Prime Minister, Speaker, Leader of Opposition, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and an eminent jurist.

secs.t: CBI - legal basis, recommending committee, year, first Director, Director's appointment

x: The CBI is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body in its own right; its powers derive from the
Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
The CBI was set up in 1963 following the recommendation of the
Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
, constituted during 1962–64.
The Special Police Establishment originated in 1941, the DSPE Act was enacted in 1946, the CBI was set up in 1963, and the CVC was set up in 1964.

The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha or leader of the largest opposition party, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the CJI.
The
Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
amended the DSPE framework and introduced the present three-member selection committee.
The Supreme Court in Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997) quashed the Single Directive that required prior sanction to investigate senior officers.

secs.t: CBI units and platforms → purpose (OCSAE, BHARATPOL, Interpol)

x: OCSAE deals with online child sexual abuse material; BHARATPOL routes international assistance requests; the CBI is India’s National Central Bureau for Interpol; and the specified cells handle economic offences and bank securities and fraud.
The CBI’s anti-corruption mandate mainly covers
Central Government and Union Territory employees and their public sector undertakings

secs.t: RTI Act 2005 - CIC set up, composition, selection, tenure and salary after the 2019 Amendment

x: All four statements are correct as stated: the CIC has the specified composition, is statutory, has civil-court powers and alone can declare an organisation a public authority.
The ordinary response period is 30 days, while applicants belonging to the Below Poverty Line category are entitled to information free of cost.

secs.t: CBI general consent - States withdrawing, Vineet Narain case

x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires general or specific consent of the State concerned because police is included in Entry 2 of the State List.
Vineet Narain was decided in 1997, the DSPE Act was revised in 2003, Andhra Pradesh withdrew consent in November 2018 and restored it in June 2019.
The 1997 Vineet Narain judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and prescribed a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director.

secs.t: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 amendments to RTI

x: The DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, thereby removing the earlier public-interest override.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 called for re-examination of the RTI Act and floated exemptions for confidential service records and draft policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.

secs.t: Enforcement agencies - function and controlling ministry

x: The Enforcement Directorate enforces PMLA and FEMA, the CBI handles corruption, economic and special crimes, and the DRI deals with anti-smuggling and customs evasion.
The Director of the Enforcement Directorate may
attach property believed to be proceeds of crime
under the PMLA.
The 2021 amendments permit extension of the tenure of the CBI and ED Directors by one year at a time, subject to a maximum tenure of five years.

secs.t: ACB and Vigilance Commission in Andhra Pradesh

x: R. Jayalakshmi is a 2006-batch IPS officer who had previously served as CBI SP and DIG before serving as IGP, AP ACB.
The State Vigilance Commission changed the SPSC's disciplinary role, but the SPSC continues as an independent body.
The disciplinary role of an SPSC is shared with the State Vigilance Commission, just as the UPSC's role is shared with the CVC at the Union level.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Bench considered whether State Human Rights Commission chairpersons could act as Information Commissioners in States with few RTI appeals, in the context of vacancies.
The concerns identified include backlogs and vacancies in Information Commissions, misuse of Section 8 exemptions and attacks on RTI activists.
The CBI has a role in economic offences, and no constitutional prohibition of the stated kind exists.
