rows.title: Citizen-centric administration - Citizens' Charter, Sevottam, grievance redress (CPGRAMS), social audit

secs.t: Citizens' Charter - origin, purpose, elements, adoption in India

x: Exam angle: "main purpose of a Citizen's Charter" - time-bound service delivery and grievance redress.
The original six principles were
quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency
All four are basic elements: service standards, service information, grievance redress arrangements and details of responsible officers.
The
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
, or DARPG, coordinates the formulation of Citizens' Charters.

secs.t: AP grievance platforms - period/government and purpose

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2021 and 2018 both keyed
Spandana
as the AP grievance platform.
Prajavani
was an earlier Andhra Pradesh initiative for online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates.
Meekosam enabled citizens to lodge grievances and suggestions through a single window and track their status.
Spandana was associated with
the YSRCP
Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.

secs.t: Social audit - MGNREGA, first law, AP society

x: Social audit functions as
an accountability tool
under MGNREGA and enables community scrutiny of works and implementation.
SSAAT is an independent society concerned with social audit, accountability and transparency, and Andhra Pradesh pioneered state-wide MGNREGA social audits.
The Second ARC recommended institutionalising social audits in all major welfare schemes, extending the practice beyond MGNREGA alone.

secs.t: Right to Services Acts - origin, order of enactment, first state

x: The Right to Services concept grew out of the Citizens' Charter idea that public services should be delivered according to declared standards and timelines.
Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials.
Andhra Pradesh has laws providing for time-bound delivery of notified services, appeal and penalties for responsible officials in cases of delay.

secs.t: Sevottam model - modules, DARPG role

x: Sevottam is derived from “Seva” and “Uttam”, conveying excellence in service.
The Sevottam model was suggested in the Second Administrative Reforms Commission's 12th report, titled Citizen Centric Administration.
The Citizens' Charter module publishes service standards; Public Grievance Redress receives, tracks and resolves complaints; Service Delivery Capability builds organisational capacity.
Sevottam-compliant certification follows Indian Standard

secs.t: CPGRAMS - department, disposal time limit

x: CPGRAMS is a 24x7 grievance platform accessible through the web, a mobile application and UMANG.
All four statements describe features associated with CPGRAMS: multilingual CPGRAMS 7.0, AI/ML-based IGMS with IIT Kanpur, access through 5.1 lakh CSCs and the “One Nation - One Portal” approach.
GRAI ranks ministries on 11 indicators grouped into four dimensions: efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment.

secs.t: Second ARC 12th report 'Citizen Centric Administration' - key recommendations

x: The 12th report was titled “
Citizen Centric Administration - The Heart of Governance
” and was published in 2009.
Veerappa Moily
chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission associated with the 12th report on Citizen Centric Administration.
The report recommended Sevottam, statutory Citizens' Charters, strong grievance redress, social audits, e-governance and right-to-public-services legislation.

secs.t: Lokpal/Lokayukta and ombudsman - distinguishing features

x: The First Administrative Reforms Commission, associated with Morarji Desai and functioning during 1966–70, recommended Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for the States.

CPGRAMS and State portals deal with service-delivery grievances; Lokpal and Lokayukta deal with corruption allegations against public functionaries; and the classic Ombudsman is an independent officer of the legislature.
Lokpal and Lokayukta are statutory institutions under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013; they are not non-statutory voluntary mediation mechanisms.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism of Citizens’ Charters is that they lack legal force, which can limit enforceability of their commitments.
The grievance-platform progression is Prajavani, followed by Meekosam and then Spandana.
SSAAT is associated with
social audit
in Andhra Pradesh.
The cited figure records more than 71,000 grievances pending on CPGRAMS in September 2025.

rows.title: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
sub: Group-II M1-B-55: Right to Information Act 2005 - features, information commissions, exemptions and amendments
Group-II M1-B-56: Working of the RTI regime - achievements, problems and the transparency debate

secs.t: RTI Act sections and Section 8 exemptions

x: All four pairings are correct: Sections 12 and 15 concern the CIC and SIC respectively, Section 20 concerns penalties, and Section 22 gives overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act.
The CIC ordered disclosure of CBSE
answer-book procurement details
and rejected the plea based on the fiduciary exemption under Section 8(1)(e).
Section 2(f) includes records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models and electronic data.
Section 5 concerns PIOs and APIOs; Section 9 concerns copyright belonging to a person other than the State; Sections 12 and 15 concern the CIC and SIC respectively.
Section 8(2) permits disclosure where
the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests
, including in cases involving the Official Secrets Act.
The twenty-year rule does not apply to cabinet deliberations, information affecting security, strategic or economic interests, foreign relations and incitement to an offence.

Section 24 generally excludes listed intelligence and security organisations, but information concerning corruption and human-rights violations remains subject to disclosure under the specified conditions.
Sections 11, 19, 20 and 22 respectively deal with third-party information, appeals, penalties and the overriding effect of the RTI Act.

secs.t: Time limits - reply, life and liberty, third party, appeals

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2025 - "reply in 45 days" is wrong; first appeal 30 days and life/liberty 48 hours are correct.
Exam angle: "reply in 45 days" is the standard wrong pair (APPSC 2025 key: first appeal 30 days and life/liberty 48 hours correct).
The applicant first approaches the PIO, waits for the decision or expiry of the prescribed period, files the first appeal, and may thereafter file a second appeal before the Information Commission.

secs.t: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology

x: Sweden enacted the
Freedom of the Press Act
in 1766, regarded as the world's first freedom-of-information law.
UDHR Article 19, adopted in 1948, recognises the right to
seek and receive information
The
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan
conducted jan sunwais in Rajasthan to demand access to muster rolls and bills, helping initiate the RTI movement.
The Rajasthan movement was associated with
Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh
Tamil Nadu and Goa enacted laws in 1997, Rajasthan and Karnataka in 2000, Delhi in 2001, and Maharashtra and Assam in 2002.

secs.t: Act milestones and nature

x: The Act creates a statutory right.
Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
The Preamble connects informed citizenship and transparency with containing corruption and ensuring accountability, subject to harmonisation with other public interests.

secs.t: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty

x: The State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioners are appointed by the Governor under Section 15.
A sitting Member of Parliament cannot be appointed as a State Information Commissioner.
The inspection covered 258 offices across 18 districts.
The inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b), which concerns proactive or suo motu disclosure of information.
The CVC comprises one Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.
At both levels, the structure consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
Removal may be connected with insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude, paid employment and other specified grounds.
For proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President may remove a Central Information Commissioner after the Supreme Court conducts the required inquiry.
Eligibility requires eminence in public life and experience in specified fields.
Wajahat Habibullah
was the first Central Information Commissioner.
Originally, the CIC’s tenure was five years or until the age of 65 years, whichever was earlier, and there was no reappointment.

secs.t: Landmark RTI judgements - issue decided

x: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay recognised evaluated answer sheets as information; Girish Deshpande treated service records and tax returns as personal information; Subhash Chandra Agarwal covered the CJI’s office; and Zee Telefilms held that BCCI was not State under Article 12.
The judgment treated the public servant’s service record, disciplinary proceedings, assets and tax returns as personal information protected under Section 8(1)(j).
The political-party decision was in 2013, the CJI-office decision in 2019, the Delhi High Court ruling was in May 2026, and the Supreme Court agreed to examine the DPDP issue in August 2026.
The Delhi High Court treated the income-tax return details as personal information and found no larger public interest justifying disclosure to the estranged wife.

secs.t: RTI (Amendment) Act 2019 and DPDP Act 2023 - provisions changed

x: At the central level, the CIC’s salary was equated with that of the Chief Election Commissioner and an IC’s with that of an Election Commissioner.
The criticism is that executive control over tenure and remuneration may weaken the institutional autonomy of the Information Commissions.

Section 44(3) rewrote Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, dropping the earlier test concerning relationship to public activity, unwarranted invasion of privacy and the public-interest override.
The original provision contained
a public-interest override
, allowing disclosure where the larger public interest justified it.
The Attorney-General opined in January 2026 that the amendment did not dilute the RTI Act.

secs.t: Public authority - political parties, NGOs, courts

x: The CIC declared
six national political parties
to be public authorities in 2013.
The political parties did not comply with the CIC’s declaration; the Bill seeking exclusion lapsed, rather than successfully removing them.
The DAV College Trust decision in 2019 recognised that NGOs substantially financed by the Government can fall within the meaning of public authority under the RTI Act.

secs.t: Issues - pendency, vacancies, RTI activists

x: Chronic vacancies in the Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions, together with a large backlog of appeals, cause long delays.
The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for
confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
, along with a possible ministerial veto.
The 2019 amendment allowed the Central Government to prescribe the
tenure and salaries
of Information Commissioners, raising autonomy concerns.

secs.t: Commencement - assent, enactment and coming into force

x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 May 2005, the Rajya Sabha on 12 May 2005, assent was given on 15 June 2005, and the Act fully came into force on 12 October 2005.
Sections 13, 15, 16 and 24
were among the provisions that came into force immediately, along with Sections 4(1), 5 and 12.

secs.t: Meaning of 'information' and 'right to information'

x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
An RTI request may be made by post, in person or by e-mail in Hindi, English or the local official language.
The Act seeks transparency, accountability, reduced corruption and an informed citizenry while recognising confidentiality needs.

secs.t: Penalties on PIOs and compensation

x: Penalty grounds include refusal to receive an application, delay, mala fide denial, knowingly incorrect or misleading information, destruction of information and obstruction.
The Commission may recommend disciplinary action against the Public Information Officer in addition to imposing the statutory penalty.
Section 19(8)(b) enables the Commission to require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.

secs.t: Achievements vs misuse - transparency gains, frivolous and vexatious applications

x: Exam angle: Assertion-Reason pairs of "purpose of the Act" with "misuse" or "limited impact" - usually both true.
The Act has helped break secrecy, improve accountability, reduce corruption and misuse of public funds, and strengthen participation and service delivery.
Public-authority misuse includes excessive or bad-faith reliance on Section 8 exemptions, along with delayed, incomplete or misleading replies and weak proactive disclosure.
The Economic Survey associated the uniquely broad RTI regime with a possible chilling effect on
honest decision-making
and proposed re-examination of the framework.

secs.t: RTI activists' safety - attacks and whistle-blower protection

x: RTI activists and whistle-blowers face harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks in connection with their disclosures and applications.
The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.
All three statements are correct: the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 exists, has not been operationalised, and a 2015 amendment Bill sought to dilute it.

secs.t: Political parties under RTI - CIC order and compliance

x: The six parties were INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP.
All three statements describe the reasons advanced by activists for bringing political parties under RTI.
The 2005 Act did not expressly name political parties.
The 2026 demand was to bring recognised national parties under RTI along with
a transparent and auditable electoral-funding system

secs.t: Proactive disclosure compliance - Section 4 audits

x: Section 4 mandates proactive or
suo motu disclosure by public authorities
, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.
From 22 June 2026, the AP Secretariat published Action Taken Reports on seven sector white papers as an example of disclosure in the spirit of Section 4.
MPLADS works are subject to RTI and are tracked through the eSAKSHI portal.

secs.t: Online RTI portals - central and Andhra Pradesh

x: The central RTI Online portal, rtionline.gov.in, was launched in 2013 by the Department of Personnel and Training.
The portal at rtionline.gov.in enables filing of RTI applications and first appeals to central public authorities and provides online fee payment.
The e-governance approach supports mandatory digital disclosure to make information easily accessible to citizens.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements reflect the current debates concerning the interaction of data-protection law, RTI and possible changes to disclosure of policy and service-related records.
The CIC ordered the CBSE to disclose
answer-book procurement data
after the CBSE had invoked the exemption under Section 8(1)(e).
The sequence is Sweden in 1766, Tamil Nadu in 1997, the central RTI Online portal in 2013 and the CIC order in June 2013; in the ordering used here, the portal launch preceded the June 2013 order.
Sweden enacted the first RTI law in 1766, Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997, and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.

rows.title: Civil services in India - role, neutrality, generalist-specialist debate; Second ARC recommendations

secs.t: Second Administrative Reforms Commission - chairman, reports

x: The Commission submitted 15 reports during 2006–2009 and is described as the “Bible” of administrative reform.
The
First Report
was titled “Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance.”.
The Fourth Report concerned Ethics in Governance; the Tenth, Refurbishing of Personnel Administration; the Eleventh, Promoting e-Governance; and the Fifteenth, State and District Administration.

secs.t: Committees on civil service reform - year and focus

x: The D.S. Kothari Committee was associated with the three-stage examination system; Satish Chandra reviewed that scheme and introduced the essay paper; Y.K. Alagh reviewed the CSE system; and P.C. Hota dealt with civil service reforms.
The committees belong respectively to 1974–76, 1989, 2000–01, 2004 and 2016, giving the order D.S. Kothari, Satish Chandra, Y.K. Alagh, P.C. Hota and B.S. Baswan.

secs.t: Constitutional provisions for services - Articles 308-323

x: Article 310
embodies the Doctrine of Pleasure.
Article 309 concerns recruitment and conditions of service; Article 311 provides safeguards; Article 312 concerns All India Services; and Article 320 specifies PSC functions.
Removal for misbehaviour requires an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

secs.t: Bureaucracy - characteristics, typologies, thinkers

x: Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy is based on hierarchy, rules, impersonality, specialisation, merit and written files.
F. Morstein Marx identified
guardian, caste, patronage and merit
bureaucracies in The Administrative State.
The stated conception of Indian bureaucracy includes All India Services, State services, local government employees and PSU managers.

secs.t: Civil Services Day - date and origin

x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”.
The 17th Civil Services Day took place at Vigyan Bhawan on 21 April 2025 with the stated theme, after the event was not held in 2024 because of elections.

secs.t: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

x: Satyendranath Tagore entered the ICS in 1864, the Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, the Federal PSC followed under the 1935 Act, and the UPSC was established in 1950.
The split system separates policy functions performed by the Secretariat from implementation carried out by field agencies.

secs.t: Civil service neutrality and anonymity - conduct rules, debates

x: The
AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964
require political neutrality and integrity.
Chhattisgarh issued a circular barring employees from membership of any political party or organisation and quickly withdrew it, reopening the neutrality debate.
Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards were associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian case and the Second Administrative Reforms Commission in the context of insulating civil servants.

secs.t: Generalist vs specialist debate - lateral entry, domain expertise

x: The generalist design is recognised as having served nation-building, but the contemporary debate supports dedicated scientific cadres and separate scientific service rules in appropriate fields.
Both the Second Administrative Reforms Commission and the P.C. Hota Committee supported lateral entry.

secs.t: Mission Karmayogi - iGOT, Capacity Building Commission

x: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building was launched in 2020 with the
iGOT Karmayogi
online platform.
The
Capacity Building Commission
is the custodian of Mission Karmayogi.
The Global Digital Capacity Building Alliance was launched in New Delhi on 20 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: the Alliance completed six months, and an annual summit and a State of Capacity Building Report are planned.
The Andhra Pradesh angle concerns disciplinary action under the AP CCA Rules, 1991, reported on 21 April 2026.
Civil servants serve as policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers in public administration; therefore, all three statements are correct.

rows.title: Accountability and transparency mechanisms - Whistle Blowers Protection Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, citizens' oversight
sub: Group-II M1-B-61: Whistle Blowers Protection Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act

secs.t: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 - who, competent authority, protection, amendment issues

x: A whistleblower is a person who discloses information regarding corruption, wilful misuse of power or discretion, or a criminal offence by a public servant to the public or a higher authority.

Central Government employees are covered by the CVC; Union Ministers by the Prime Minister; State Ministers by the Chief Minister; and MPs by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or Speaker of the Lok Sabha, as applicable.
For an MP who is not a Minister, the competent authority is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, depending on the House concerned.

secs.t: Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index - measure, scale, India's trend

x: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by
Transparency International
, headquartered in Berlin.
The CPI measures the perceived level of public-sector corruption on a 0-100 scale.
The CPI reflects perceived public-sector corruption and uses expert and business surveys as important sources.
The Corruption Perceptions Index ranges from 0, meaning highly corrupt, to 100, meaning very clean.

secs.t: Anti-corruption and anti-money-laundering agencies - parent Act/ministry, powers

x: The key powers stated for the ED in relation to proceeds of crime are to
trace, attach and confiscate
them, subject to the applicable legal process.
They respectively identify the legal basis of the CBI, the laws governing the ED, the function of State ACBs and the CVC’s supervisory role over the CBI in corruption cases.

secs.t: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 and 2018 amendment - changes

x: The
Santhanam Committee
on Prevention of Corruption was constituted in 1962 and its recommendations contributed to stronger anti-bribery laws, eventually consolidated in the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
The 2018 amendment made bribe-giving a direct offence, protected a coerced giver reporting within seven days, and imposed liability on commercial organisations for bribes offered on their behalf.
Section 17A requires prior government approval before an inquiry or investigation into a public servant concerning decisions taken in the discharge of official functions.
Vineet Narain was decided in 1997, Subramanian Swamy in 2014, and Centre for PIL v. Union of India produced the noted split verdict in 2026.

secs.t: AP Lokayukta - Act, appointment, jurisdiction

x: The Lokayukta has jurisdiction over higher functionaries, whereas the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the remaining categories covered by the state law.

secs.t: Santhanam Committee - recommendations and outcomes

x: Outcomes:
, tougher bribery laws leading to
PCA 1988

secs.t: Citizens' oversight - social audit, report cards, public hearings

x: Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.
Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.

secs.t: WBP (Amendment) Bill 2015 - status and notification

x: The Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015, was passed by the Lok Sabha in
May 2015
The Bill proposed restrictions on disclosures in Section 8(1)-type categories, including sovereignty, security and Cabinet papers, and lapsed with the 16th Lok Sabha in 2019.

secs.t: Sanction for prosecution - PC Act and CrPC/BNSS

x: Exam angle: 17A (approval before investigation) and 19 (sanction before prosecution) are often swapped in statements.
Section 17A requires government approval before inquiry or investigation in specified cases, while Section 19 requires prior sanction before a court takes cognizance of an offence.

Section 17A relates to approval before inquiry or investigation; Section 19 to prior sanction before cognizance; Section 218 BNSS gives general protection; and Section 197 CrPC was its earlier counterpart.

secs.t: Related laws - Benami, PMLA, FEOA

x: The Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 bans proxy holdings and provides for confiscation and imprisonment up to seven years' rigorous imprisonment.

All four conditions are associated with the FEOA framework: an arrest warrant, an offence value of at least ₹100 crore, flight from India, and an application by the ED to a Special Court empowered to confiscate before conviction.

secs.t: UN Convention against Corruption - India's ratification

x: The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005, and India ratified it in 2011.
India ratified the United Nations Convention against Corruption in 2011.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements reflect the reported criticism and debate concerning transparency and legislative scrutiny: over four lakh RTI cases were pending, committee referrals fell from 71% to 16%, and more than 100 RTI activists had been killed.
The CVC report on CBI pendency and related trial outcomes was reported on
2 September 2026

units.title: Impact of Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization on Governance; Statutory, Regulatory and Quasi-Judicial Bodies

rows.title: Liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation - meaning, the 1991 reforms, sequencing

secs.t: 1991 crisis and New Economic Policy - trigger, PM and FM, stabilisation vs structural adjustment

x: The 1991 crisis was triggered by the Gulf War, higher oil prices, reduced remittances, NRI deposit flight and political instability.
By June 1991, India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about
$975 million
, sufficient for roughly two weeks of imports.
India pledged about 67 tonnes of gold, sought approximately $7 billion from the IMF and accepted structural-adjustment conditions.

secs.t: LPG - definitions and distinctions

x: Liberalisation involved removing or reducing licences, quotas and controls and thereby reducing the direct role of the state in economic activity.
Privatisation means withdrawal of government from ownership or management and may involve outright sale of public sector undertakings.
A private stake exceeding 51 per cent transfers
ownership and management
of the public sector undertaking.
The New PSE Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat, 2021, favours
strategic disinvestment

secs.t: Reform measures - part of LPG or not

x: Industrial licensing was largely abolished, but it was retained for
alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence, and drugs
The 1991 reforms provided automatic approval for foreign direct investment up to 51 per cent in 34 priority industries.
The reform material lists defence, atomic energy and railways among reserved areas, while the present position stated is limited to atomic energy and railway operations.

secs.t: Industrial Policy Resolutions/Statements - year and thrust

x: The 1948 Industrial Policy Resolution adopted the mixed-economy approach and classified industries into four categories.
The 1980 Industrial Policy Statement focused on technology upgrading, export orientation and development of backward areas.
The 1991 Industrial Policy Statement emphasised de-licensing, restructuring of MRTP provisions, foreign direct investment and autonomy for PSUs through Memoranda of Understanding.

secs.t: Sequencing debate - first- vs second-generation reforms

x: First-generation reforms, broadly covering 1991–2000, included trade and industrial de-licensing, tariff reduction, automatic FDI and financial-sector reform.
Second-generation reforms focused on factor markets such as labour, land and power, along with fiscal rules, PSU disinvestment and governance.
Reforms 2.0 are framed as reforms from 2014 onwards, including digital public infrastructure, Aadhaar, UPI, Jan Dhan and direct benefit transfer.

secs.t: Licence Raj and MRTP Act - fate and successor law

x: The Licence Raj involved licensing for starting, closing or expanding firms, reservation for small-scale industries and price controls.
The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act was enacted in 1969, relaxed in 1980 and later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, administered by the CCI.
In 1991, asset limits and pre-entry curbs relating to expansion, mergers and acquisitions under the MRTP framework were abolished.

secs.t: Trade reforms - devaluation, tariffs, EXIM changes

x: Import licensing was abolished except for hazardous or environmentally sensitive items
Although import licensing was substantially abolished earlier, quantitative restrictions were fully removed in
April 2001
The WTO replaced GATT in 1995; GATT had been established in 1948.
The 1991 trade reforms initiated a move towards
a market-determined rupee
, with the market-determined exchange rate operating from 1993.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Protection of property rights was one of the prescriptions associated with the Washington Consensus.
LENS (July 2026) describes LPG as ‘Reforms 1.0’ and argues for a third wave of reforms.
The one-size-fits-all character of the Washington Consensus is specifically questioned, and the framework is regarded as outdated.
The term Washington Consensus was coined by
John Williamson

rows.title: Impact of LPG on the role of the State - from provider to regulator and enabler

secs.t: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

x: Exam angle: match the role (provider/regulator/enabler) to the reform or institution.
The 1991 crisis and the LPG reforms under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh shifted the economy from a state-controlled orientation to a market-oriented one.
Public-private partnerships, Direct Benefit Transfer, Government e-Marketplace and UMANG are instruments through which the State enables delivery by private or civil-society actors.

secs.t: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

x: The exempted categories included
alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace and drugs or pharmaceuticals
Abolition of MRTP asset limits removed curbs on
concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions
₹21,082 crore
had been raised in 2026–27 through stake sales in seven PSUs together with SUUTI remittances, as of August 2026.

secs.t: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

x: The TV Ratings Policy 2026 made the
Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
the sole authority over television rating agencies, ending the overlap with TRAI.

The Economic Survey made all four recommendations or observations: regulators exercise multiple kinds of powers, independence must be balanced with accountability, younger professionals should have dedicated regulatory careers, and delayed clearances should attract penalties.

secs.t: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

x: The expression refers to a leaner State that performs fewer activities directly but governs more effectively through rules, technology and accountability.
Aadhaar, DBT and GeM are e-governance instruments that can reduce discretion and middlemen.
Capacity building and right-sizing of the bureaucracy
are administrative measures intended to support leaner and more effective governance.

secs.t: Market failure vs government failure debate

x: Public choice theory, associated here with James Buchanan, supplied the intellectual basis for the government-failure critique of the pre-1991 system.
The criticisms included declining agricultural infrastructure investment, shrinking welfare revenue due to tax incentives and curtailed social-sector spending.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 links State capability with reducing uncertainty and enabling coordination beyond
kinship and caste networks
, including in the auto and pharmaceutical sectors.

secs.t: Washington Consensus - policy prescriptions list

x: All four were included: privatisation, deregulation, secure property rights and reordering public expenditure priorities.
Interest-rate deregulation was associated with the Narasimham Committee, tax reforms with the Chelliah Committee, the market-determined exchange rate with 1993, and FEMA replaced FERA in 1999.
The package involved export promotion, removal of import quotas and a market-determined exchange rate in 1993.

secs.t: State capacity debates - 'flailing state' and developmental state → author

x: Chalmers Johnson’s developmental-state concept describes a strong, autonomous bureaucracy steering industrialisation, particularly in the East Asian experience.
Peter Evans associated embedded autonomy, in 1995, with a bureaucracy that is protected from capture while remaining connected to business.

The Economic Survey 2025-26 describes Indian corporates as neither purely East Asian developmental partners nor purely Western rules-bound firms; they occupy a hybrid equilibrium where political mediation substitutes for market discipline.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: Chapter 3 is titled “Refining the Regulatory Touch”, dated 31 January 2026, and is cited for the current regulatory role of the State.
The Swarna Andhra KPI monitoring framework tracks indicators at the
mandal, district and state levels
By supporting BPL families through DBT for LPG cylinders, Deepam-2 illustrates a shift from the State as direct provider to the State as enabler.

rows.title: Impact of LPG on administration - downsizing, contractualisation, New Public Management

secs.t: Downsizing and governance reform measures; Pay Commissions on staff strength (Fifth, Sixth, Seventh)

x: Exam angle: "which of these are governance/downsizing measures" statement questions.
Public-sector employment fell from 19.6 million in 1991 to 17.5 million in 2008 as
uncompetitive public-sector enterprises closed or downsized
The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed a definition under which the State could hold
less than 51%
, indicating a new paradigm for disinvestment.

secs.t: New Public Management - originators, core principles, pioneering countries

x: New Public Management brought private-sector techniques into government, including performance auditing, contracting out and customer-oriented service delivery.
NPM promotes performance auditing, contracting out non-core services and a customer-oriented view of citizens.
NPM includes hands-on management, explicit performance standards, output controls and competition in the public sector.
These are among Christopher Hood’s stated NPM doctrines, along with professional management, performance measures and output controls.

secs.t: Reinventing Government - authors and ten principles

x: Reinventing Government, published in 1992, was authored by
David Osborne and Ted Gaebler
Reinventing Government uses the catchphrase “
steering, not rowing
,” signifying that government should guide rather than directly perform every service function.
Catalytic government steers rather than rows; community-owned government empowers; competitive government injects competition; mission-driven government moves from rules to mission.

secs.t: New Public Service and Public Value theory → author, as critiques of NPM

x: New Public Service emphasises democratic citizenship, community building, public interest and serving rather than steering.
Mark Moore
wrote Creating Public Value in 1995 and developed the Public Value perspective.
Public Value theory holds that managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust, and not merely efficiency.
Both approaches critique NPM’s reduction of the citizen to a customer and of the State to a service seller.

secs.t: Contractualisation and outsourcing - contract employees in government, APCOS

x: Outsourcing involves hiring external sources for services such as legal, IT, advertising and security work previously performed in-house.
APCOS was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in 2020 to recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly, thereby cutting out contractor middlemen.
About 8,000 outsourced APSRTC employees are paid through contractors and face irregularities involving wages, provident fund and ESI; they have demanded equal pay.

secs.t: Lateral entry - joint secretary level recruitment, debates

x: Joint Secretary and Director posts at the Centre are otherwise filled through tenure deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme of the Department of Personnel and Training.
The debates include the benefits of domain expertise and fresh ideas, as well as concerns about single posts without reservation, conflict of interest and demotivation of career officers.

secs.t: Performance management tools - RFD, PMS, Key Result Areas

x: An RFD requires each ministry to specify objectives, success indicators and targets; these serve as Key Result Areas.

NeSDA assesses digital services for G2C and G2B; the Good Governance Index provides a uniform framework for States and UTs; GRAI ranks central ministries on CPGRAMS disposal; and the RFD lists objectives, indicators and targets.

secs.t: Citizen as customer - business-like administration and its criticisms

x: The criticisms emphasise citizenship rights, the importance of equity and accountability, and the New Public Service formulation ‘serve, not steer’.
Registration Service Kendras are based on the Passport Seva Kendra model, but statutory powers remain with Sub-Registrars.
Registration Service Kendras followed the Passport Seva model, but Sub-Registrar Offices were not privatised.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The upper age limit was raised to 44 years for direct recruitment to non-uniform services until
30 September 2027
under G.O. Ms.
The decision was reported ahead of APPSC recruitment for
892 posts
, of which 163 were Group-I posts.
Contractualisation is criticised for lowering job security and weakening unions; it may also adversely affect productivity rather than automatically improving it.

rows.title: Impact of LPG on federalism, welfare and social sector spending

secs.t: Competitive federalism - investment competition, ease of doing business ranking of states

x: The Centre’s planning-era allocation role associated with the Planning Commission gave way to

the Net Borrowing Ceiling
imposed on the State.

for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

The May 2026 revisions permitted
sovereign wealth funds, pension and infrastructure funds, and private equity
to bid for BOT projects; previously they could bid only for TOT.

The Kelkar Committee examined ways to revisit and revitalise the public-private partnership model.

x: OFS was widely used from 2012, IPP refers to placement only with Qualified Institutional Buyers, and CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 ETF are disinvestment instruments.
An IPO is the first public offer by an unlisted PSE, an FPO is a further offer by a listed PSE, OFS is a promoter share sale, and a strategic sale transfers management control.

Modern Foods was the first strategic sale, undertaken in 2000, with Hindustan Lever acquiring 74 per cent.

secs.t: AP PPP projects - AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, ports and airports under PPP

x: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 provides the legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh and includes Swiss-challenge proposals.
The draft policy covers transport, logistics, ports, airports, healthcare, education, renewables, tourism and urban infrastructure.
The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks
₹1,500 crore
for Viability Gap Funding and proposes a bridge fund.

secs.t: PPP issues - renegotiation, aggressive bidding, stalled projects, Swiss challenge method

x: Aggressive bidding, often producing the winner's curse, traffic and revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays can leave PPP projects stalled.
Because unforeseen financial and implementation problems can arise, the Kelkar Committee wanted
a built-in mechanism for renegotiation
of PPP contracts.
The Infrastructure Projects Arbitration Tribunal (IPAT) and the Infrastructure Projects Review Committee (IPRC) were proposed to speed up dispute resolution and project review.

₹16.72 lakh crore
Current PPP developments include
revised BOT and HAM norms in May 2026
, NMP 2.0 for FY26–30, and the AP PPP Policy-2026 with ₹1,500 crore VGF.
Criticisms include possible undervaluation of assets and the perception that monetisation is a sale by another name.

rows.title: Constitutional, statutory, executive, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies - definitions and how to distinguish them

secs.t: Constitutional bodies → Article

x: The Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body created by executive resolution in March 1950; Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
The Election Commission is under Article 324, the Finance Commission under Article 280, the CAG under Article 148 and the NCBC under Article 338B.
Articles 315–323 concern the public service commissions, Article 338 concerns the NCSC and Article 338A concerns the NCST.

secs.t: Constitutional vs extra-constitutional status - spotting the odd one out

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a constitutional body" and "how many are constitutional" counts.
The NCBC, CAG and Finance Commission are constitutional bodies.
The NCB​​C is a constitutional body under Article 338B, not a body created by executive resolution.
Linguistic minorities are not notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act; safeguards for them are covered through the officer provided under Article 350B.

secs.t: Statutory bodies → parent Act and ministry

x: The NCW, NCM, NGT and UIDAI are respectively governed by the NCW Act 1990, NCM Act 1992, NGT Act 2010 and Aadhaar Act 2016.
The CBI Director is selected by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India or a nominee, and the Leader of the Opposition.

secs.t: Executive/non-statutory bodies - resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2024 keyed "All incorrect" for statements calling the Law Commission a quasi-judicial body that advises the President.
These bodies are not created as constitutional bodies by the Constitution; they arise through resolutions or executive notifications and perform advisory or coordinating functions.
NITI Aayog is a think tank with the Prime Minister as Chairperson, and its Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

secs.t: Bodies → year of establishment

x: The predecessor of the UPSC, the Public Service Commission, was established in 1926.
All four pairs are correctly matched.
The Inter-State Council was established in 1990, the NCM in 1992 and the NHRC in 1993.

secs.t: Quasi-judicial bodies - defining features, civil court powers

x: A quasi-judicial body is not a court, but it can interpret and apply law, examine matters, summon persons and impose sanctions under authority granted by a statute.
NITI Aayog
is an advisory body and is not quasi-judicial.
The NCBC has powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses and requisitioning records, particularly after it received constitutional status in 2018.

secs.t: State counterparts → Article/Act

x: State SC and ST Commissions are established under State laws.
K. S. Jawahar, Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State SC Commission, reviewed SC/ST schemes in Nellore.

secs.t: Reports of constitutional bodies → to whom submitted and where laid

x: Under Article 323, the UPSC submits its annual report to the President.
Under Article 350B, the report of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is submitted to the President, laid before Parliament and also sent to the concerned States.
Both Houses of Parliament consider the annual reports of bodies such as the CAG, Finance Commission and UPSC.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Chairperson of the UPSC, the Chief Election Commissioner and the CAG are placed at rank 9A in the order of precedence.
The Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST are placed at rank 17.
Withdrawals of general consent for CBI investigations remain a federal flashpoint because they concern the relationship between the Union investigative agency and State governments.

rows.title: Financial regulators - RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, IBBI, IFSCA - mandate and powers

secs.t: IRDAI - statutory basis, recommending committee, year, sector regulated, expert panels

x: Exam angle: "which statement is NOT correct about IRDAI": the Gadgil Committee trap.
The IRDAI expert panel on a standard cyber liability insurance product was chaired by
P. Umesh
The package made an authorised salesperson mandatory for each policy, introduced perpetual licensing with an annual fee for intermediaries, and revised actuarial and investment rules.
Ind AS 117 and Ind AS 109 replaced IGAAP for insurers, and IRDAI enforces their adoption.

secs.t: Regulator → establishing Act and date set up

x: RBI is established under the RBI Act, 1934; IRDAI under the IRDA Act, 1999; IBBI under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; and IFSCA under the IFSCA Act, 2019.
The correct sequence is RBI in 1935, SEBI as a non-statutory body in 1988, IBBI in 2016 and IFSCA in 2020.

secs.t: Regulator → headquarters and parent ministry

x: SEBI
is headquartered in Mumbai and has regional offices in New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Ahmedabad.
The Ministry of Finance nominates representatives to the boards of SEBI, IRDAI and RBI; IBBI belongs to Corporate Affairs, while IFSCA belongs to Finance.
IFSCA promotes FinTech as well as regulatory and innovation sandboxes.

secs.t: RBI - Monetary Policy Committee, banker/regulator functions, inflation-targeting mandate

x: Headline CPI
, with base year 2024, is the nominal anchor for the inflation-targeting framework.
Section 45ZN requires the RBI to report to the Centre when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters.
The Public Debt Management Cell was established to reduce the RBI's conflict of interest between conducting monetary policy and managing public debt.

secs.t: SEBI - powers over capital markets, quasi-judicial orders, appeal forum

x: SEBI exercises quasi-judicial powers; it investigates, summons persons and passes orders and penalties.
Appeals against SEBI orders lie first to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and thereafter to the Supreme Court.
Since 2014, orders of
IRDAI and PFRDA
have also been appealable to SAT.
SEBI revised derivative settlement pricing after the introduction of the new
Closing Auction Session

secs.t: Mergers and shifted mandates (FMC, NBFCs, HFCs) - which regulator now

x: All three statements are correct: HFC regulation shifted to the RBI in 2019, NHB remains the apex housing refinancer, and the Centre took full ownership of NHB in 2019.
BIFR, constituted under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016; its cases moved to NCLT/NCLAT under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
NABARD is associated with agricultural and rural development credit, NHB with housing finance, Exim Bank with export-import finance and SIDBI with small industries development.

secs.t: Financial Stability and Development Council - chair and role

x: FSDC was set up in 2010 as a non-statutory apex body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
All four listed functions fall within the role of the FSDC.
The FSDC sub-committee is chaired by the
RBI Governor
, whereas the main council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

secs.t: Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission - chair and key proposals

x: The Commission was set up in 2011, its report came in 2013, FMC merged into SEBI in September 2015, and BIFR was dissolved in 2016.
The Commission proposed a single Indian Financial Code, a Unified Financial Agency, a Public Debt Management Agency and other reforms, but not a separate constitutional court.
The proposed Unified Financial Agency was to merge SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA.
The Commission proposed expanding SAT into a
Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal

secs.t: Investor/depositor protection bodies (DICGC, IEPF) → parent

x: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the
RBI
and was established in 1978.
The Policyholders’ Education and Protection Fund is associated with IRDAI under
Section 16A of the IRDA Act
, following the 2025 amendment.
The National Financial Reporting Authority oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013.

anticipatory regulation
NPS e-Shramik extends pension coverage to
informal workers
IRDAI is headquartered in
Hyderabad
, which was the shared capital with Telangana until 2024.
The debates include overlapping mandates and mixed evidence on the effect of a decade of inflation targeting on output and jobs.

abuse of dominant position

was among the eight laws and orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
From 1 July 2019, recycled plastics and newspaper may not be used to wrap food.
Eat Right India is FSSAI’s movement for safe, healthy and sustainable food and was launched in 2018.

x: TRAI performs regulatory functions relating to tariffs, interconnection and quality of service.
TDSAT was set up in May 2000 and also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.
Anil Kumar Lahoti
is the chairperson of TRAI.

secs.t: Electricity regulators - CERC, SERCs, APERC formation, APTEL

x: CERC handles inter-State matters, while SERCs handle intra-State tariffs and consumer protection and coordinate with CERC.
The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 retained APERC as a joint regulator for
not more than six months
, until separate SERCs were formed.
CEA performs technical planning, CERC and APERC deal with central/inter-State and State tariffs respectively, and APTEL hears relevant appeals.

secs.t: Data Protection Board of India - composition, powers, appellate forum

x: Created under the
DPDP Act, 2023 (Sections 18-22)
as an independent adjudicatory body.
Appeal: to
TDSAT within 60 days
, then to the Supreme Court.
Data protection - DPDP Act 2023
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

x: Regulatory chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government, usually on committee recommendations.
Removal is by the Central Government, but only on grounds specified in the parent Act and after the concerned person has been given a hearing.
The usual grounds include insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, incapacity and abuse of position.

secs.t: Proposed regulators and bills - HECI and others

x: The proposal for the Higher Education Commission of India has taken the form of the
Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025
The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025, referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament and proposes repeal of all three specified higher-education laws.
The CCI set up a Digital Markets Division to address competition issues arising in digital markets.

abuse of dominance
NCLAT upheld the abuse-of-dominance finding, the appeal is before a Supreme Court Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant, and the CCI penalty was ₹213.14 crore.
The criticism concerns the amendment of

A SAT decision can be appealed to the Supreme Court on points of law.

rows.title: Regulatory governance issues - independence, capacity, accountability, regulatory capture, appellate structures

secs.t: Regulatory independence - appointment/removal safeguards, post-retirement jobs, funding autonomy

x: Regulators are described as “mini-states” because they combine rule-making, investigation and adjudication, corresponding broadly to
legislative, executive and judicial functions
The NGT is funded and administered by the MoEFCC, the Railway Claims Tribunal depends on Zonal Railways for its budget, and the AERB works under the DAE through the Atomic Energy Commission.

secs.t: Regulatory capture - meaning, theorist, Indian illustrations

x: Regulatory capture occurs when a regulator comes to serve the interests of the regulated industry instead of the public.
The theory of regulatory capture is associated with
George Stigler
, particularly through his 1971 work.

secs.t: Accountability of regulators to Parliament - reports laid, standing committees

x: Regulators’ annual reports and accounts are laid before Parliament and examined by the
Departmentally Related Standing Committees
All three measures are part of the accountability framework: parliamentary review and published orders, board oversight of executive management, and proportionate sanctions.
The Joint Committee on the VBSA Bill warned against excessive concentration of power in one central regulator.

secs.t: Appellate structures → regulator and further appeal forum

x: SAT hears appeals from SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA; APTEL hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB; and NCLAT hears appeals from NCLT, IBBI, CCI and NFRA.
APTEL was established in 2004, NCLAT in 2016, NCLAT began hearing CCI appeals in 2017, and NFRA appeals in 2018.
L. Chandra Kumar held that
High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure
of the Constitution.

secs.t: Regulatory overlap and conflicts - SEBI-IRDAI on ULIPs, CCI vs sector regulators

x: The CCI penalised WhatsApp for abuse of dominance through
data sharing
, while the DPDP Act separately restricts cross-use of data.
The
DPDP Act
separately restricts cross-use of data, creating an interaction between competition regulation and data-protection regulation.
The TV Ratings Policy, 2026 ended the overlap by making the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting the sole regulator of rating agencies.

secs.t: Reform proposals - FSLRC Indian Financial Code, Regulatory Reform Bill, common framework

x: The FSLRC proposed a Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal for appeals; it did not propose abolishing such a tribunal.
The Regulatory Reform Bill, 2013 was a
Planning Commission
draft intended to provide a common framework for infrastructure regulators.
The VBSA Bill, 2025 proposes one higher-education regulator with three councils, replacing the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.

secs.t: Regulatory capacity - staffing, technical expertise, tribunal vacancies

x: The lack of a dedicated regulatory cadre and reliance on retired administrators are among the reasons for proposing a School for Regulations.
Legal aid is available at only 9 of the Railway Claims Tribunal’s 23 benches, while the NGT has no IT division; statements 3 and 4 reverse these facts.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Both statements are true, and the State’s interface with the economy through regulation explains why regulatory capacity forms part of overall State capacity.
The Joint Committee’s draft report on the VBSA Bill flagged risks to
institutional autonomy

secs.t: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques

x: FICCI is a business group, AITUC is a trade union, the Indian Medical Association is a professional group, and Bharatiya Kisan Union is a peasant organisation.
Almond and Powell classify pressure groups as
institutional, associational, non-associational and anomic
Anomic
pressure-group activity is characterised by spontaneous riots, demonstrations and agitations.
Pressure groups represent sectional interests and
press the government, legislators and bureaucracy for favourable laws and measures

secs.t: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh - year, legal form, lending model

x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh follows a quasi-wholesale model: it lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which lend onward to poor women and SHGs.
Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was set up under the
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is registered as a society under the
Societies Registration Act, 1860

secs.t: FCRA 2010 and 2020 amendment - restrictions, cancellation grounds, designated bank account

x: The Ministry of Home Affairs administers FCRA, while FEMA, 1999 is administered by the Reserve Bank of India and the Enforcement Directorate.
The retrospective 2016 amendment followed the Delhi High Court's 2014 Vedanta-donations ruling and excluded Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms from the definition of foreign sources.
Cancellation may arise from breach of the law or conditions, non-functioning, or administrative defaults such as non-filing of returns or delayed renewal.
The Rules require utilisation of 75 per cent before seeking the next instalment and prohibit foreign funding for proselytisation; they do not require transfer to another NGO.

secs.t: NGOs - status in development programmes, legal forms and registration laws

x: Civil society organisations are described as the third sector, alongside government and the market, while functioning as development partners and democratic watchdogs.

Societies are registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860; private trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882; public charitable trusts under State laws; and not-for-profit companies under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.

secs.t: Trade unions → party affiliation

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2022 asked a match of unions with parties, e.g. BMS with BJP and INTUC with Congress.
AITUC is affiliated with CPI, INTUC with the Indian National Congress, HMS with the Socialists, and BMS with the BJP/Sangh Parivar.
BMS was founded in 1955, is associated with RSS/BJP, and legal recognition came through the Trade Unions Act, 1926 after five years of pressure.

secs.t: SHG-Bank Linkage Programme - NABARD role, DAY-NRLM

x: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was piloted in 1992 and encourages banks to lend to SHGs of poor women.
DAY-NRLM is community-driven and develops SHG members as community resource persons.
The listed roles are Pashu Sakhi, Krishi Sakhi, Bank Sakhi, Bima Sakhi and Poshan Sakhi.
DAY-NRLM runs the
SVEP
umbrella for village enterprises.
The national campaign focused on
SHG non-farm enterprises and rural women's entrepreneurship

secs.t: Civil society role → examples

x: The MKSS campaign for transparency and public hearings contributed to the
Right to Information Act, 2005
The correct sequence is Chipko (1973), Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985), Anti-arrack movement (1992), and MKSS (1990).
The Narmada Bachao Andolan brought the displacement caused by large dams, particularly the Sardar Sarovar project, into public debate.

secs.t: National Policy on the Voluntary Sector 2007 - objectives, NGO accountability

x: The National Policy on the Voluntary Sector was adopted in 2007 by the Planning Commission.
The policy seeks an enabling environment, easier resource mobilisation and partnership with government.
The policy favours
transparency, self-regulation and codes of conduct
rather than tight government control.

secs.t: Media's role - fourth estate, free press, new media, image-building, paid and fake news

x: Freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes press freedom, while new media has increased participatory communication.
The misuse of
UAPA, IT Rules and defamation law
is identified as a concern affecting media freedom.
India is placed in the '
very serious
' category in the Reporters Without Borders classification mentioned here.

secs.t: Techniques - definitions

x: Petitioning
involves submitting written demands or memoranda to authorities.
Litigation includes PILs and court cases, such as electoral cases filed by ADR.
Strikes, bandhs and dharnas are forms of direct action intended to disrupt normal activity and force public or governmental attention.

secs.t: Press Council of India - legal nature, composition, powers

x: The Press Council was first set up in 1966 under the
Press Council Act, 1965
The composition of the Press Council of India is a Chairman plus 28 members.
The Press Council can warn, admonish or censure newspapers and journalists and covers print media only.
The Press Council may warn, admonish or censure, but it lacks punitive powers to impose criminal penalties.

secs.t: Pressure groups vs political parties

x: Political parties seek to capture power and govern.
Pressure groups generally do not contest elections, are answerable to their members and represent sectional interests.
Pressure groups are described as the '
Anonymous Empire
' because they influence public policy without directly seeking governmental office.

secs.t: Civil society movements - leader and demand

x: The Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar dam and the displacement associated with it.
MKSS raised issues of minimum wages and the right to information, using the public hearing or jan sunwai process.
The Chipko Movement is associated with Uttarakhand, then part of Uttar Pradesh, and with Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi in 1973.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh examples

x: Farmers involved in land pooling in Amaravati protested from December 2019 against
the three-capitals plan
The AP NGOs' Association and farmers' associations, including rythu sanghams, are examples of pressure groups.
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet asked the police for a task force to address fake news and defamatory content on social media.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The opposition letters were written by
K.C. Venugopal and John Brittas
, seeking withdrawal of the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026.
FCRA curbs and NGO funding regulations are specifically debated in relation to shrinking civic space.
An AP social-media task force was associated with civil-society and governance developments in July 2026.
The NEET paper-leak protests drew solidarity from
Sri Lanka
n civil society in July 2026.

rows.title: Globalisation and society - culture, migration, labour, inequality; the anti-globalisation critique

secs.t: Cultural change terms → meaning

x: Glocalisation adapts global influences locally, homogenisation produces cultural convergence, and hybridisation creates blended global-local forms.
McDonaldisation
refers to the spread of fast-food principles such as efficiency, calculability, predictability and control across society.
Glocalisation means local adaptation, homogenisation means convergence, hybridisation means blending, and McDonaldisation means the spread of fast-food principles.

secs.t: Globalisation theorists → concept

x: Castells developed the ideas of network society and space of flows, while Appadurai identified five scapes including ethnoscapes, mediascapes and technoscapes.
Appadurai’s five scapes are ethnoscapes, mediascapes, technoscapes, financescapes and ideoscapes. ‘
Politiscapes
’ is not included in this list.
Wallerstein’s world-systems theory divides the global system into
core, semi-periphery and periphery

secs.t: Migration - international migrants, remittances rank, Gulf migration from AP/Telugu states

x: The
Ministry of External Affairs
signs Migration and Mobility Partnerships and runs Pre-Departure Orientation Training under the Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana.
The Pre-Departure Orientation Training programme under the Pravasi Kaushal Vikas Yojana began in
January 2018
Remittances and services exports offset pressures arising from the
trade deficit
and help keep the current account deficit stable.

secs.t: Labour concepts → sociologist; gig and platform workers

x: Keith Hart
coined the term ‘informal sector’ during 1971–73.
Jan Breman is associated with footloose labour and the concepts of circular and casual labour.
The number of gig workers was projected to rise to
2.35 crore
by 2029–30, equivalent to 4.1% of the workforce.
The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Bill, 2025 replaced
MGNREGA

secs.t: Inequality - Gini trends, World Inequality Report, Oxfam reports

x: The World Inequality Report 2026 estimates that the top 1% in India hold about
of total wealth.
The official view is that inequality matters less than it did in the early 2010s, while the comparability of data remains contested in the HCES 2023–24 debate.
In 2023–24, median earnings of the top 10 percent were
13 times
those of the bottom 10 percent.

secs.t: Anti-globalisation critique → proponents and movements

x: The World Social Forum is associated with the slogan ‘Another world is possible’; the Seattle protests opposed the WTO Ministerial; Vandana Shiva advocates seed sovereignty; and Joseph Stiglitz criticised IMF policy conditions.
The ‘Battle of Seattle’ refers to protests against the WTO Ministerial in 1999.
Mahendra Singh Tikait opposed the Dunkel Draft, GATT and WTO.

secs.t: Impact on women, tribals, farmers and traditional artisans

x: The concerns include cheap imports under WTO rules, while debt- and crop-failure-related farmer suicides were especially marked in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
Small farmers constitute about 98% of coffee growers and face global price swings as well as competition from Brazil and Vietnam.
MNC competition can squeeze artisans and domestic firms, causing shutdowns and layoffs.

secs.t: Consumerism, media and youth culture changes

x: Global integration is associated with wider consumer choice, global brands, media expansion and cultural fusion.
‘Mindless aping’ refers to the uncritical imitation of Western lifestyles, identified as a cultural risk accompanying global integration.
About
of tertiary-educated youth were unemployed in 2023–24, reflecting a skills-job mismatch.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism is that globalisation can widen disparities between rich and poor people and between nations, and can develop into ‘commercial imperialism’.
The stated current-relevance references are the World Migration Report 2026, World Inequality Report 2026 and the MoSPI migration survey of July 2026.
Gulf-dependent remittance households face uncertainty arising from
the 2026 West Asia war

rows.title: Indian society - salient features, unity in diversity, continuity and change
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Features of Indian society - pluralism, hierarchy, rural base, joint family, caste, religion

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2014 listed
excess population in villages, various religions, various castes
as main features of Indian social structure; poverty was the option left out.
Indian social life has historically been centred on
castes, ethnic groups and extended families
The movement towards nuclear households does not mean rejection of the joint-family ideal.

secs.t: Unity in diversity and national integration - bases of diversity, bonds of unity, threats

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2025 A-R. National integration has
political, economic, social, cultural and psychological
dimensions (keyed: A true, R false).
The stated framework identifies six major religions, notes Hindu minorities in eight States or Union Territories, and treats religion as a basis of diversity.
Shankaracharya is associated with sending priests from the south to temples in the north and vice versa, thereby strengthening cultural links.

secs.t: Indological study of Indian society - Ghurye, Dumont, Maine

x: Homo Hierarchicus, published in 1966, discusses hierarchy through
purity-pollution and the encompassing power of the Brahmin
Louis Dumont
and D. Pocock founded Contributions to Indian Sociology in 1957.
Ancient Law was published in 1861, Village Communities in the East and West in 1871, Caste and Race in India in 1932, and Homo Hierarchicus in 1966.

secs.t: Sociologists - statements on Indian society (Srinivas, Yogendra Singh, A.R. Desai, Karve)

x: Srinivas is associated with Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste.
Srinivas viewed the joint family as modified rather than eliminated by social change.
Yogendra Singh discussed
orthogenetic and heterogenetic sources
of change.
The observation that poverty is transferred and transmitted rather than cured is attributed to
A.R. Desai
Yogendra Singh
authored Modernization of Indian Tradition, published in 1973.

secs.t: Continuity and change - traditional institutions vs forces of change

x: Double cropping, the plough at Kalibangan, zebu cattle and binary weights are all cited as evidence of continuity from Harappan times.
Courtyard houses and bangles
are cited, along with other features, as evidence of continuity from Harappan times.
The evidence is limited by the urban collapse around 1900 BCE and the fact that the Harappan script remains undeciphered.

secs.t: Terms → originator + meaning (Great/Little Tradition, universalisation, parochialisation, cultural lag)

x: McKim Marriott associated universalisation with the upward movement of local elements into the Great Tradition, illustrated by the integration of local Jagannath with Vishnu.
McKim Marriott discussed universalisation in
Village India
, published in 1955.
Robert Redfield originated the concept, and
Milton Singer and McKim Marriott
applied it to India.
Redfield’s little community is characterised by distinctiveness, smallness, homogeneity and self-sufficiency.

secs.t: Founders of sociology → key concepts and books (Comte, Durkheim, Weber, Marx)

x: Durkheim is associated with social facts, Weber with class-status-power, Marx with alienation, and Comte with positivism.
Durkheim’s works appeared in the order Division of Labour (1893), Rules of Sociological Method (1895), Suicide (1897), and Elementary Forms of Religious Life (1912).
Marx linked class struggle with dialectical materialism, discussed alienation, and authored The Communist Manifesto (1848) and Das Kapital (1867).

secs.t: Terms → coined by (sociological imagination, network society, social facts, verstehen)

x: C.
Wright Mills
coined the term sociological imagination in 1959.
Manuel Castells
is associated with the term network society and wrote The Rise of the Network Society in 1996.
Sociological imagination was coined by C. Wright Mills, network society by Manuel Castells, social facts by Durkheim, and verstehen by Weber.
Verstehen, associated with Max Weber, means
interpretive understanding
of social action.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Education Minister released 55 volumes of classical-literature translations, including Sangam works and selected Telugu and Odia texts.
All four were included among the mentioned classical-literature translations: Sangam works, a Telugu Silappathikaram, and the Odia works Charyapada and Madalapanji.
The report proposing a National Mission for Mother-Tongue-Based Multilingual Education was mentioned on
Mother Language Day
, 21 February 2026.

rows.title: Family - types, functions and changing structure in India
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Changing structure and urban families - factors of disintegration, urban family typologies (T.K. Oommen)

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2014 asked how T.K. Oommen distinguished urban families. Answer:
all of
mode of earning and value pattern, structure of authority, and urban milieu and social ecology.
Milton Singer and Orenstein
are associated with the view that industrial urbanisation had not dissolved the joint family.
Ramkrishna Mukherjee observed that joint families were over-represented in
trade and higher occupations

secs.t: Family types - by structure, residence, descent, authority

x: A
neo-local
family residence is established independently by the married couple.
In a duo-local arrangement, spouses stay with their respective natal families.
The
family of orientation
is the family into which a person is born, whereas the family of procreation is established after marriage.
MacIver defined the family as a group based on sex relationships precise and enduring enough for procreation and upbringing.

secs.t: Family - functions (Ogburn, Murdock, Parsons) and loss of functions

x: Ogburn stated that all the listed functions except
affectional function
were passing to outside agencies; affection remained within the family.
Parsons identified primary socialisation of children and stabilisation of the adult personality as the two irreducible functions of the family.
Dysfunction
refers to persistent failure of family functions, such as failure caused by abuse or alcoholism.

secs.t: Joint family - features and definitions (Karve, I.P. Desai, A.M. Shah)

x: Karve emphasised functional unity and obligations more than co-residence; she also described the joint family as a residential unit holding common property.
All four statements correctly represent I.P. Desai’s findings: five degrees of jointness, 61 per cent nuclear households, 39 per cent joint households and only 5 per cent not joint at all.
A.M. Shah distinguished family from household and explained that households may move between nuclear and joint forms through a developmental cycle.

secs.t: Matrilineal family systems → community + region

x: Among Tiyans, some Moplas and Bants, the tharawad consists of a woman, her siblings and her sisters’ children; the husband is not part of the unit.
Among the Garo, Machong is the matrilineage and the heiress’s husband, called
nokma
, heads the household.
The Khasi of Meghalaya are matrilocal, organised into exogamous clans, and follow inheritance by the youngest daughter.

secs.t: Inheritance and succession - Mitakshara vs Dayabhaga, Hindu Succession Act and amendment

x: Mitakshara is Vijnaneshwara’s commentary on the
Yajnavalkya Smriti
, composed in the Kalyani Chalukya court.
*Vineeta Sharma* (2020) held that daughters’ coparcenary rights by birth apply irrespective of whether the father was alive in 2005.
The 2005 amendment made daughters
coparceners by birth
and gave them rights equal to those of sons in coparcenary property.

secs.t: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

x: Widowhood, marital instability and male migration are identified as causes of rising single-parent and female-headed households.
Elderly care is linked to filial piety, while nuclearisation and migration weaken traditional support systems and create a need for alternative care.
The maintenance provisions under the BNSS, 2023 cover wives, children, indigent parents and divorced wives.

secs.t: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

x: NFHS-6 was released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with the
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
, as the nodal agency.
NFHS-6 covered 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts.
NFHS-5 reported urban and rural fertility rates of 1.6 and 2.1 respectively, while NFHS-6 reported an overall rate of 2.0.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: N. Chandrababu Naidu urged a return to the joint family and incentives for having two or more children in the context of declining fertility.
Srinivas, Shah and Desai are associated with the debate; Srinivas and Shah emphasised continuity, while Marxist sociologist I.P. Desai linked nuclear households to capitalism.
The Andhra Pradesh succession amendment was in 1985, followed by the Family Courts Act in 1984?.

src: Sources: CDX (Indian Society Part 1 pp.12-14, 19-20; Part 2 pp.2-4, 22-25; AP History p.589); APP (Society > Family: Definition, Household Dimensions, Desai's Mahuwa study, Urban Family, Shift to Nuclear); CDI (Block03 Kalyani Chalukyas; Block05 Family Courts); UPSC (Indian Society p.94; Social Justice p.113; Post-Independence p.97); IYB 2026 pp.81, 84; LENSD 1 Jun 2026; LENS Aug 2025; TH 12 Jun 2026, 29 Jun 2026

rows.title: Marriage - forms, rules of endogamy and exogamy, changing trends and legislation
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-89

secs.t: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

x: Adultery, bigamy and conversion are among the stated grounds, and mutual consent was added in 2001.
The Hindu Marriage Act applies to
Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs
All three statements are correct: the second marriage is void under Section 11 and may constitute bigamy punishable under Section 494 of the IPC.

secs.t: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

x: Anuloma
, or hypergamy, refers to the marriage of an upper-caste man with a lower-caste woman.
Niyoga permitted a wife to cohabit with a designated man for begetting a child when her husband was impotent or dead.
The Later Vedic period saw the emergence of child marriage, decline of Swayamvara, discouragement of widow remarriage and prohibition of marriage within the same gotra.

secs.t: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

x: Capture marriage is associated with the
Naga, Ho, Bhil and Gond
communities.
Among the Gonds, the groom may work at the bride's home as a form of service associated with acquiring a mate.
In the trial form, the prospective groom demonstrates prowess in a dance game.
Youth dormitories gave young people
a wide choice of mates through mutual consent

secs.t: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

x: Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground, but the Supreme Court can use Article 142, and Naveen Kohli urged legislative recognition of the ground.
The Supreme Court held instant triple talaq unconstitutional in
Shayara Bano
The 2019 Act makes instant triple talaq void and illegal and provides for imprisonment of up to three years along with fine.

secs.t: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

x: Exam angle: the Delhi HC upheld
HMA Sec. 5(v)
(the sapinda bar).
Endogamy operates at the varna, caste and sub-caste levels and requires marriage within the specified group.
The stated North Indian pattern is
caste endogamy, clan or gotra exogamy and village exogamy
The Delhi High Court upheld
Section 5(v)
, which concerns the sapinda restriction, subject to the statutory framework regarding custom.

secs.t: Changing trends - inter-caste, love marriage, live-in, same-sex unions

x: Companionate marriage, rising age at marriage, serial monogamy and increasing divorce are identified trends.
Honour killings are most common where existing
caste hierarchy is being challenged
, particularly through inter-caste relationships or unions.
Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala
are identified as States where empowered Dalits show both more inter-caste unions and more honour killings.

secs.t: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, data sources (NFHS, NCRB), district initiatives

x: Under the PCMA, the marriage is
voidable at the option of the child
; it is not automatically void in every case.
On 1 July 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA
overrides the personal-law puberty rule for all religions
Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat aims to cut child marriage by 10% by 2026 and eliminate it by 2030.

secs.t: Marriage offences and solemnisation - IPC/BNS, self-respect marriages, who can solemnise

x: IPC Chapter XX, Sections 493–498, became BNS
Sections 81–84
in the stated reorganisation.
Bigamy is placed under
BNS Section 82
, corresponding to old IPC Sections 494–495.
Self-respect marriages were institutionalised by Periyar and validated through
Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act
by a Tamil Nadu amendment in 1967.
A Kazi conducts Nikah, Anand Karaj takes place in a gurdwara, and a Marriage Officer solemnises a marriage under the Special Marriage Act.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated target is to cover all 21 NDA States by 2029.
Uttarakhand's UCC has been in force since January 2025.
The Andhra Pradesh adolescent-education programme covers child marriage in 9,675 schools.
