rows.title: Custodial violence, encounter deaths, prison reforms, death penalty debate

secs.t: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials

x: Prisons continue to be governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals; BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.
The Model Prisons Act, 2023 was prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs as a guide for States to replace the colonial 1894 Act.
BNSS Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, reduced to one-third for first-time offenders, subject to the statutory conditions.

secs.t: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings

x: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab
(1980) established the ‘rarest of rare’ doctrine, under which life is the rule and death is the exception.
Machhi Singh developed categories of rarest cases and required balancing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.
Capital offences formerly in the IPC now appear in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; murder is cited under Section 103.

secs.t: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

x: Nilabati Behera concerns compensation, Joginder Kumar concerns justified arrest and informing relatives, D.K. Basu concerns arrest safeguards, and Arnesh Kumar restricts automatic arrest for offences up to seven years.
Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
(1993) recognised compensation under Articles 32 and 226 for custodial death and rejected sovereign immunity as a defence.

secs.t: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

x: The guidelines require recording the tip-off, registering an FIR and an independent investigation by the CID or another police station.
The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations and requires mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
Body-worn cameras by the Delhi Police, Kerala’s Janamaithri Suraksha and Tamil Nadu’s Friends of Police were identified as way-forward measures, along with stronger forensic capacity.

secs.t: UN Convention against Torture - India's status, Prevention of Torture Bill

x: The Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010 was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed.
The 273rd Law Commission Report (2017) recommended ratification of UNCAT and proposed a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.
The proposed way forward includes ratifying UNCAT, passing a standalone anti-torture law and adopting the PEACE model of interviewing.

secs.t: Prison reform committees → focus (Mulla, Krishna Iyer, Justice Amitava Roy)

x: The Mulla Committee focused on comprehensive jail reforms, the Krishna Iyer Committee on women prisoners and women in police, and the Justice Amitava Roy Committee on overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial.
The Supreme Court-appointed Justice Amitava Roy Committee (2018) focused on
overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial

secs.t: Law Commission reports → subject (262nd, 273rd)

x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

secs.t: Mercy petitions - Arts 72 and 161, Shatrughan Chauhan

x: In
Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India
(2014), the Supreme Court recognised inordinate and unexplained delay in deciding a mercy petition as a ground for commuting death to life imprisonment.

All three statements reflect the safeguards recognised in Shatrughan Chauhan (2014): unexplained delay may support commutation, pre-rejection solitary confinement is illegal, and 14 days should separate rejection from execution.

secs.t: Police reforms linked to custodial abuse - Prakash Singh directives, Police Complaints Authority

x: All four are among the police-reform measures associated with Prakash Singh (2006): the State Security Commission, UPSC-panel selection of the DGP with a two-year tenure, two-year tenure for field officers and Police Establishment Boards.
The State Police Complaints Authority, headed by a retired judge, deals with serious misconduct including custodial death, rape and grievous hurt.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The NHRC sought reports in June 2026, and subsequently the Supreme Court gave the SIT seven-day custody of suspended CI Nagaraju.
The Supreme Court gave the SIT, headed by
IGP M. Ravi Prakash
, seven-day custody of suspended CI Nagaraju.
Retributive justice emphasises punishment or retaliation for wrongdoing, whereas reformative justice focuses on rehabilitation and reform of the offender.

rows.title: Women's rights - constitutional provisions and the legal framework
sub: Group-II S3-11: Women in Indian society - status through history, patriarchy and the women's movement
Group-II S3-37: Constitutional and legal provisions for women - Articles 15(3), 39, 42, 51A(e), 243D; key legislations

secs.t: Landmark judgements on women's rights → issue

x: The
Shayara Bano
judgment was followed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, which made instant triple talaq punishable.
The Shah Bano judgment recognised the entitlement of a divorced Muslim woman to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC and also urged the adoption of a Uniform Civil Code.

secs.t: National Policy for Empowerment of Women 2001 and draft 2016 policy - objectives

x: The Eighth Plan marked a shift in policy emphasis from development of women to empowerment of women.
The policy objectives included advancement and empowerment, equal access to health, education and employment, ending discrimination and violence, and gender mainstreaming.

The 2016 draft policy identified health, food security and nutrition, education, economy, governance and decision-making, violence against women, enabling environment, and environment and climate change as priority areas.

secs.t: Reproductive rights laws - Surrogacy Act 2021, ART Act 2021, MTP (Amendment) Act 2021

x: The Act permits altruistic surrogacy, under which medical costs and insurance are allowed.
A
State Medical Board
decides cases involving substantial foetal abnormality beyond 24 weeks; in such cases no gestational limit applies.
The PCPNDT Act bans
sex selection and prenatal sex determination
The Supreme Court in 2022 removed marital-status distinctions in access to abortion, invoking Article 14.

secs.t: Institutions for women's justice - NCW, AP State Commission for Women, Family Courts, first women's court

x: The Chairperson, five members and Member-Secretary of the NCW are nominated by
the Centre

secs.t: Gender concepts → meaning

x: Matrilineal tribes
are identified as an exception to the general pattern in which men hold primary power and status.
Amartya Sen
coined the term ‘missing women’ to refer to the consequences of discrimination against women, including intra-household discrimination.
Gender mainstreaming builds a gender perspective into policy-making by assessing the impact of policies on women and men.

secs.t: International commitments - CEDAW, Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action

x: India made a reservation regarding Article 29(1), which concerns arbitration or reference of disputes to the International Court of Justice.
The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action emerged from the Fourth World Conference on Women held in 1995.
The Beijing Platform for Action identifies 12 critical areas, including poverty, education, health, violence, economy, decision-making, media, environment and the girl child.

secs.t: Constitutional provisions for women → content

x: Article 42
directs the State to make provisions for securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
The stated implementation date for the 33 per cent quota in the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies is
17 April 2026
Article 41 covers work, education and public assistance; Article 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief; Article 43 living wage; and Article 47 nutrition, public health and prohibition.

secs.t: Personal law reforms - Hindu Succession (Amendment) 2005 and AP amendment, Special Marriage Act, Hindu Marriage Act

x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate.
Vineeta Sharma held that the daughter’s coparcenary right is by birth and does not depend on whether the father was alive on 9 September 2005.
The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.

secs.t: Equal pay and work rights - Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Code on Wages, night shifts

x: The Code on Wages prohibits gender-based wage discrimination and includes
transgender persons
within its protection.
Apart from prohibiting gender discrimination in wages and recruitment, the Code on Wages provides for a
statutory floor wage
Contract and fellowship researchers
are noted as categories that often fall outside the coverage of the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017.

secs.t: Statements on women's status and progress → leader

x: This observation is associated with
Swami Vivekananda
The statement was made by
Mahatma Gandhi

secs.t: Status of women by period, customs and colonial laws

x: The later Vedic and medieval periods witnessed a decline in women’s status, increasing domestic confinement, purdah and social evils.
Niyoga did not mean prohibition of widow remarriage; it involved a childless widow or wife bearing a son by the husband’s brother or kinsman.
The practice was banned by the Madras Act of 1947 and, in Andhra Pradesh, by the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988.

secs.t: Women's movement - WIA, AIWC, NCWI; post-1970s; Towards Equality

x: The nineteenth-century phase focused mainly on social reform issues such as sati, widow remarriage and education.
The WIA, associated with Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins, worked for
votes for women and the right to sit in councils
The Women’s Indian Association was established in Madras in 1917 by
Annie Besant and Margaret Cousins

secs.t: Women and religion cases - Sabarimala, Shayara Bano, Haji Ali

x: The Sabarimala entry restriction was struck down by a 4:1 majority, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting.
The case concerned the prohibition on women entering the inner sanctum of Haji Ali Dargah; entry was ultimately allowed.
The petition was filed by the
Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan
, associated with Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz.

secs.t: UN milestones on women

x: The Commission on the Status of Women was established under the
Economic and Social Council
, or ECOSOC.
The International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women were held in Mexico City in 1975.
CEDAW was adopted in 1979, and India ratified it in 1993.
SDG 5, adopted in 2015, concerns
gender equality

secs.t: Sex ratio and gender indices - causes, GDI, GII, GGGI

x: Son preference, female foeticide or infanticide, dowry and neglect of girls are stated causes of a low sex ratio.
The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the
Gender Inequality Index
, not the GDI.
Haryana and Punjab are identified as the most male-skewed region, whereas Kerala and the North-East, including Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Mizoram, have the best sex-ratio balance.

secs.t: Social reformers and inspirations → reform

x: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj; Vidyasagar was associated with the Widow Remarriage Act; the Phules founded the Satyashodhak Samaj; and Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj.
Vidyasagar supported female education, opposed child marriage and polygamy, and played a major role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

secs.t: Andhra women's movements - Anti-Arrack, Chalam, Durgabai Deshmukh, Andhra Mahila Sabha

x: The movement began at Dubagunta in 1992, led to the arrack ban in 1993, and was followed by prohibition in 1995.
Chalam wrote Stree and advocated women's personal and sexual freedom, while Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha in 1937.
Kandukuri Veeresalingam performed the first widow remarriage in Telugu society at
Rajahmundry in 1881

secs.t: Laws and policies on women - year and provisions (Indecent Representation Act, National Policy for Empowerment of Women)

x: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 provides for imprisonment up to five years and a fine of at least
Rs 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is greater
The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act dates to 1956, the Dowry Prohibition Act to 1961, the PCPNDT Act to 1994 and the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act to 2019.

secs.t: Maternity Benefit Act 1961 and Amendment Act 2017 - leave weeks, creche, work from home

x: The 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid maternity leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.
A crèche is compulsory in establishments with 50 or more employees, and the woman employee is permitted four visits a day, including rest intervals.
The 2017 position provides
12 weeks
of maternity benefit for the third child onwards.

secs.t: Women's reservation in local bodies - AP share, AP reservation in nominated posts and jobs

x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50% reservation for women in panchayats and municipalities, which is above the one-third floor.
Andhra Pradesh provides
reservation for women in nominated posts and work contracts.
Andhra Pradesh provides
horizontal reservation for women in direct recruitment.
Women constitute
about 46%
of Panchayati Raj Institution representatives nationally.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court hearing concerned challenges to the marital rape exception contained in Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The expression ‘proxy’ women heads refers to situations in which elected women representatives are effectively controlled by others in local governance.
The Andhra Pradesh-specific measures cited are the
daughters' property law of 1985 and 50% quotas in local bodies and nominated posts

rows.title: Laws for women - Dowry Prohibition Act, Domestic Violence Act 2005, POSH Act 2013, Maternity Benefit Amendment
sub: Group-II S3-23: Dowry, domestic violence, sexual harassment and trafficking

secs.t: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 - commencement, definition, penalties, Dowry Prohibition Officers, IPC/BNS sections

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - the Act came into force on
1 July 1961
Section 4 deals with demanding dowry and prescribes imprisonment from six months to two years, along with a fine up to ₹10,000.
BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs
within seven years
of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.
The 1986 changes introduced dowry death under IPC Section 304B and the presumption under Evidence Act Section 113B.

secs.t: Other women-specific laws → year

x: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1956 after being known as SITA and was amended in 1986.
The law was enacted in 1994 as the PNDT Act and was renamed the PCPNDT Act in 2003.
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was passed on
30 July 2019

secs.t: POSH Act 2013 - what it addresses, Vishaka, Internal and Local Committees, time limits

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2018 - the "Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal Act 2013" deals with
sexual harassment of women at the workplace

The Internal Committee applies to workplaces with 10 or more employees; the Local Committee applies to workplaces with fewer than 10 employees; its Presiding Officer is a senior woman employee, and it is set up by the District Officer.
Employer duties include constituting the Internal Committee, displaying the policy, conducting awareness programmes and acting on reports.

secs.t: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 - commencement, definition, Protection Officers, reliefs

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2015 - the PWDVA came into force on
26 October 2006
Multiple reliefs may be sought in one case, including residence, protection, monetary relief, temporary custody and compensation; disposal is contemplated within 60 days.
The reported figures were
55 NGOs as Service Providers, 47,734 petitions, 23,644 Domestic Incident Reports and 7,307 final orders

secs.t: Criminal provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 - cruelty, dowry death, stalking, voyeurism

x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS
Sections 85-86
, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
Rape is covered by Sections 63-64, trafficking by Section 143, selling or buying minors for prostitution by Sections 98-99, and acid attack by Section 124.
BNSS Section 144 provides for maintenance of wives
regardless of religion
; it corresponds to old CrPC Section 125.

secs.t: Legal aid and support institutions - One Stop Centres, Women Helpline, fast track courts

x: One Stop Centres, also known as Sakhi centres, provide
medical, legal, counselling and shelter services under one roof
to women affected by violence.
All three statements are correct: 743 Fast Track Special Courts were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, and 3,39,644 cases had been disposed of by 31 July 2025.

secs.t: Trafficking - UNODC GLOTIP findings, US TIP tiers, forms

x: Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 does not fully meet them but is making significant efforts; Tier 2 Watch List is the watch-list category; and Tier 3 represents countries not making significant efforts.
The listed forms include sex trafficking, forced or bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and servitude, and organ removal.

secs.t: Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956 and the Trafficking in Persons Bill

x: The law originally started as the
Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act
, commonly abbreviated as SITA, and was later renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act gives effect to
the 1950 UN Convention
relating to trafficking and exploitation.
The Victim Protection Plan provides a common protocol for legal aid, education, skills and livelihood support to rescued victims.

secs.t: Prevention, rescue and rehabilitation - Ujjawala, AHTUs

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 - the MHA IT initiative for real-time crime/trafficking information and inter-state coordination is
Cri-MAC
Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
Cri-MAC
is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.

secs.t: Acid attacks - Laxmi case, sale regulation, compensation

x: The Laxmi case directions require photo identification, entry in a sales register and prohibition of sale to anyone below 18 years.
Acid-attack offences were covered by Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC and are now identified as BNS 124 in the cited framework.
BNS Section 124 provides a minimum punishment of ten years extending to life imprisonment for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Poor enforcement, faulty First Information Reports, and presenting dowry-death cases as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.
Mandatory film publicity clearance based on an Internal Complaints Committee report is associated with POSH compliance, not the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The Andhra Pradesh angle refers to APSES and CDI AP SES data concerning PWDVA, POSH committees and Shakti Sadans.

rows.title: Crimes against women - trafficking, honour crimes, acid attacks; Criminal Law Amendments 2013 and 2018
sub: Group-II S3-21: Crime against women - types, magnitude, causes and NCRB data
Group-II S3-22: Legal and institutional response to crimes against women

secs.t: AP initiatives - Disha Bill/Act, Disha police stations and Disha app

x: Exam angle: APPSC-G1 2022 - the SOS app is
Disha
. APPSC-GS 2018 - Chittoor's campaign is
Abhayam
; the Ongole pick-up scheme is
Abhay
The Disha Act provides for a seven-day investigation, a fourteen-day trial, mandatory special courts in every district and mandatory forensic evidence.
Trishul committees are described as state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
The reported decline in crimes against women was
4.4 percent
, with Shakti Teams and Sexual Offender Sheets being associated with the measure.

secs.t: Crime databases and safety IT initiatives → purpose

x: ITSSO tracks investigation timelines; NDSO is the database of convicted sexual offenders; CCTNS links police stations; Cri-MAC enables real-time crime information sharing.
Cri-MAC, or Crime Multi-Agency Centre, facilitates real-time sharing of information on significant crimes, including human trafficking, and supports inter-State coordination.
Safe City Projects and ERSS-112 receive funding from the
Nirbhaya Fund
, which is dedicated to women’s-safety projects.

secs.t: Fast track courts and special courts - Nirbhaya Fund scheme, States' new courts

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2019 - first women's court =
West Bengal
The FTSC scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund for cases involving rape and offences under POCSO.
As on 31 July 2025, 743 FTSCs were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, across 29 States and Union Territories.

secs.t: Trafficking - UNODC report, Palermo Protocol, ITPA, Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018/2021

x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and begar or other similar forms of forced labour; it is a key constitutional provision in human trafficking matters.
The Palermo Protocol is the
UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children
The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.

secs.t: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013 - committee, new offences

x: Section 326A concerns acid attack, Section 326B attempt to acid attack, Section 354C voyeurism and Section 376E death for repeat rapists.
The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, and raised the minimum punishment to seven years.
The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape, opposed the death penalty for rape and recommended retaining the age of consent at 16.

secs.t: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2018 - context, punishment changes

x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the
Kathua and Unnao cases
and was associated with the fast-track court response.
The stated timelines were two months for investigation, two months for trial and six months for appeals.
The 2018 amendment barred anticipatory bail in cases involving rape of a girl
below 16 years

secs.t: Honour crimes - Supreme Court guidelines, Law Commission report

x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, which respectively protect equality, prohibit discrimination, protect freedoms and safeguard life and personal liberty.
Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under
Section 103
of the BNS.

secs.t: NCRB Crime in India - States with highest crimes against women, AP data

x: The 2024 report recorded 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes, incorporated BNS data for the first time alongside IPC data, was released in May 2026, and reported Odisha as having the highest violent-crime rate.
Andhra Pradesh recorded
trafficking victims per ten lakh population in the APSES 2024–25 SDG-16 table.
Cybercrime reached 1,01,928 cases, with fraud forming 72.6% and sexual exploitation forming 3.1%, or 3,190 cases.
The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline operate under the Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).

secs.t: NCRB data on child marriage and dowry deaths → state rankings

x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
accounted for most dowry-death cases in the cited data.
NFHS-5 reported that
of women were married before the age of 18.
The figures were 26.8% in NFHS-4, 23.3% in NFHS-5 and 20.1% in NFHS-6.

secs.t: Types - IPC/BNS crimes vs Special and Local Laws (SLL) crimes

x: Of the 58.86 lakh cognisable crimes in 2024, 35.44 lakh were under IPC/BNS and 23.41 lakh were under SLL.
The
Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956
is an SLL head.
Cruelty by husband or relatives and kidnapping or abduction of women are IPC/BNS heads.
Foeticide, sati and eve-teasing are classified as social violence.

secs.t: Crime heads ranked by share

x: Cruelty by husband or relatives
was the largest category, accounting for 29.8% of crimes against women in 2023.
The descending order is cruelty by husband or relatives at 29.8%, kidnapping and abduction at 19.8%, and assault with intent to outrage modesty at 18.7%.
Trafficking cases under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act rose by about
between 2022 and 2023.

secs.t: Causes - patriarchy, son preference, dowry, alcoholism, low reporting, weak conviction

x: Marital rape is not captured well in NCRB data because such incidents are substantially under-reported and remain insufficiently visible in official reporting systems.
The cited weaknesses are that women constitute only 11.7% of the police, rape conviction rates are low, and pendency in courts for crimes against women is over 90%.

secs.t: Female foeticide and sex ratio - CSR (Census 2011), SRB (NFHS-5), PCPNDT enforcement

x: The PCPNDT Act permits diagnostic procedures for detecting
genetic abnormalities
, while prohibiting sex selection and prenatal sex determination.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 to address the declining
Child Sex Ratio
and related discrimination against girls.
The PCPNDT law bans
advertising sex determination
as part of the legal response to sex-selective practices.

secs.t: NFHS data on spousal violence

x: NFHS-5 reported that
of ever-married women had faced spousal violence.
NFHS-5 reported that
of women aged 18–49 had faced physical violence.
All three statements are correct: the NFHS-4 figure was 5.4%, the exception remains, and the Delhi High Court delivered a split verdict on it.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh - district-wise crimes against women and conviction rate

x: The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women’s Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets.
APSES 2024–25 aims for one of the lowest crime rates and provides for special courts for atrocity cases.

secs.t: Institutional mechanisms - OSC, 181, 112, Nirbhaya Fund, CVCF - funding source

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2019 - OSCs are set up with grants from the
Nirbhaya Fund
. ERSS for women's safety =
The Nirbhaya Fund was created after the 2012 case through the
Union Budget, 2013
, as a non-lapsable corpus.
Women Helpline 181 provides emergency help and counselling, ERSS 112 is the single emergency number, and Women Help Desks operate in police stations.

secs.t: BNS provisions on offences against women - new offences

x: Section 69 of the BNS addresses sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud.
Consent is immaterial for the trafficking offence under Section 143.

secs.t: Nirbhaya case and its policy outcomes

x: The principal listed outcomes were the Justice Verma Committee, the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013, the Nirbhaya Fund and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for
heinous crimes
, subject to the statutory process.
Nirbhay Raho is a Ministry of Panchayati Raj initiative with the Ministry of Women and Child Development and NLSIU, under the Nirbhaya Fund.

secs.t: Gender sensitisation of police - women police stations, AHTUs

x: Women Help Desks and Mahila Police Volunteers are listed as gender-sensitisation measures, with the latter associated with MWCD and MHA.
AHTUs are district-level task forces funded by the Ministry of Home Affairs for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution.
The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 operates under Article 141 until
Parliament enacts a law
on the subject.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Disha model is associated with a 21-day verdict, the Nirbhaya Act with a two-month probe, Shakti Teams with the current Andhra Pradesh policing model, and SHe-Box 2.0 with the workplace-harassment complaint portal.
The measures included Trishul committees, a police response time of 30 minutes, and an emphasis on improving conviction rates.
The current Andhra Pradesh model is described through
Shakti Teams, Sexual Offender Sheets and Trishul committees

rows.title: Women's political participation - 73rd/74th Amendment reservation, 106th Amendment; gender indices (GII, GGGI)
sub: Group-II M1-B-101: Women and weaker sections in local governance - reservation and its social outcomes

secs.t: Gender indices - publisher, sub-indices, India's rank, top countries

x: Exam angle: publisher-index matching; India's rank in a named year; which dimension is in which index.
GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.

All four pairs are correctly matched: the World Economic Forum releases the Global Risks Report 2026, ILO the World Social Protection Report, UNU-EHS the World Risk Index, and QS the World Future Skills Index 2027.

secs.t: 73rd/74th Amendments - women's reservation Articles, seats and chairpersons, states at 50%

x: Exam angle: "one-third at which level?" is answered by PRIs. "How many seats in AP?" is answered by
one-half
. 243D(3) is the Article for women's seats.
Article 243D provides for reservation for SCs and STs in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area, at every level.
Article 243T(3)
provides for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats in Municipalities for women.
SC/ST reservation is proportionate to population, and chairperson offices are arranged under State law and rotation.
Article 243D(5) links the duration of SC/ST reservation in Panchayats to the period specified under
Article 334

secs.t: Grassroots empowerment initiatives - state and purpose; NCW and SHGs

x: The Abhiyan provides leadership, legal-awareness and gender-justice training, including modules on gender-based violence, for Women Elected Representatives.
Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to be established at least one per district, promote safe spaces and gender-responsive governance, and align with SHGs.
Nirbhay Chetna involves training about 17.5 lakh male representatives through 28,500 master trainers.

secs.t: Constitution (106th Amendment) Act 2023 - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam

x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the
106th Constitutional Amendment
Act, receiving assent in 2023.
The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, also associated with the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, was passed on
21 September 2023
The one-third reservation extends to
the Delhi Legislative Assembly
, in addition to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
Because commencement depends on the Census and subsequent delimitation, the quota is linked to the 2027 Census and is not expected to be enforceable before 2034 under the current law.

secs.t: Women's Reservation Bill history - earlier attempts

x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
The 108th Amendment Bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2008, passed there on 9 March 2010, and lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha in 2014.

secs.t: Women voters - turnout trends

x: Articles 84 and 173 relate to qualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, respectively, and thereby permit women to contest elections when the qualifications are met.
Women's turnout first exceeded men's in 2019, did so again in 2024, and women voters are among the targets of the ECI's SVEEP programme.

secs.t: FIRST women - post

x: Pratibha Patil was the first woman President, Meira Kumar the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister, and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor.
All four pairs are correctly matched.

secs.t: Studies on women sarpanches - Chattopadhyay-Duflo, proxy representation

x: Chattopadhyay and Duflo used the
random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan
to study the effects of women’s political leadership.
Women leaders invested more in public goods that women specifically requested, notably drinking water and roads.
“Sarpanch-pati” denotes proxy representation in which a male relative exercises the office formally held by an elected woman.

secs.t: Dalit and tribal representatives - discrimination and atrocities

x: The relevant legal safeguards identified are
the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in 1989.

secs.t: AP examples - women-led panchayats, Mahila Sabhas

x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
Andhra Pradesh provides
50 per cent
reservation for women in local bodies.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements are correct: local bodies have a one-third floor, half reservation operates in 19 States and Union Territories, and legislative reservation is linked to post-delimitation operation.
The existing experience of local-body quotas is described as the working model for the
106th Amendment
concerning women’s representation in legislatures.
The criticisms include delay of the women’s quota until post-Census delimitation, proxy representation, and the absence of an OBC-women sub-quota.

rows.title: Women's welfare schemes - Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Mission Shakti, PMMVY, Ujjwala

secs.t: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao - launch, ministries, objectives, CSR districts

x: The scheme is fully centrally funded, began in 100 districts with low Child Sex Ratio, and has subsequently expanded to all districts.
The scheme focuses on Child Sex Ratio, prevention of gender-biased sex selection, and the survival, protection and education of girls.
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is included under the
Sambal
vertical, which deals with women’s safety.

secs.t: Women's economic empowerment schemes

x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh lends to intermediary NGOs and micro-finance institutions, which in turn provide micro-credit to poor women.
For a non-individual enterprise, at least
of the shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST person or a woman entrepreneur.
Under DAY-NRLM, an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh annually is termed a
Lakhpati Didi

secs.t: Maternal schemes - PMMVY, IGMSY, PMSMA

x: IGMSY was the pilot maternity-benefit scheme; PMMVY provides partial wage-loss compensation; PMSMA provides monthly antenatal check-ups; and JSY supports institutional delivery.
IGMSY was introduced in 2010 as a pilot conditional maternity-benefit scheme and later served as the forerunner of PMMVY.
PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on
the ninth day of every month

secs.t: Mission Shakti and the MWCD umbrella missions

x: Exam angle: "Which is a sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?" Swadhar and Ujjawala no longer exist under their own names.
From 1 April 2022, MWCD schemes were organised under
three
umbrella missions: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya, and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0.
Swadhar Greh and Ujjwala were merged as Shakti Sadan; Working Women Hostel became Sakhi Niwas; National Creche became Palna; and Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan became MY Bharat (IYB).

secs.t: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana

x: All four particulars are correct: PMUY is under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, was launched on 1 May 2016 at Ballia, and provides LPG connections to women of BPL households.
Ujjwala 2.0 provided a free first refill and hotplate.
Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana has reached
over 10.5 crore households

secs.t: Girl child schemes - objective

x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 2015 under BBBP as a small-savings account scheme for girls below 10 years, primarily supporting education and marriage expenses.
Balika Samriddhi Yojana provides a post-birth grant and annual scholarships to girls from families living below the poverty line.
Dhanalakshmi was introduced in 2008 as a conditional cash-transfer scheme linked to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and delaying marriage beyond 18 years.

secs.t: AP women's welfare schemes - benefit

x: Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 per year to mothers of pupils in
Classes 1 to 10
, subject to 75 per cent attendance.
Talliki Vandanam provides ₹15,000 annually to eligible mothers, with a 75 per cent attendance condition, and was described as a restructured form of Amma Vodi.
YSR Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa was introduced in 2022 and provides marriage assistance to poor brides belonging to SC, ST, BC and minority communities.

secs.t: Shelter, livelihood and income schemes - target group

x: Swadhar Greh is meant for
women in difficult circumstances
and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.
STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.
DWCRA
, or Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas, was introduced in 1982–83 and provided group-based credit to rural poor women.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The rape conviction rate is reported to have remained around
27–28 per cent
, prompting demands for more fast-track courts and stronger standards.
The stated demands include extending fast-track courts and establishing national minimum standards for One Stop Centres and shelters.
Talliki Vandanam is described as a conditional cash transfer, while Andhra Pradesh’s total fertility rate is approximately 1.7.

rows.title: SC/ST rights - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 164, 244, 330, 332, 335; abolition of untouchability
sub: Group-II S3-16: Untouchability and caste-based atrocities; the legal response
Group-II S3-31: Constitutional provisions for Scheduled Castes - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 330, 332, 335, 338

secs.t: SC/ST Articles number game → subject

x: Exam angle: straight "which Article" questions (Art. 46 asked three times; Art. 17 twice).
Exam angle: "educational and economic interests of SCs/STs" =
Art. 46
(G2/GS 2018, 2019); "untouchability abolished" =
Art. 17
Article 46, a Directive Principle of State Policy, directs the State
to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, especially SCs and STs, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation

Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, 2005, covers admissions in private aided or unaided educational institutions for SEBCs, SCs and STs, but excludes minority institutions under Article 30.

Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, permits special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admission to educational institutions, including private aided and unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.

Article 15(4) concerns special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs; Article 16(4A) concerns promotion for SCs and STs; Article 16(4B) concerns backlog vacancies; and Article 340 concerns a commission on SEBC conditions.

secs.t: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

x: B.R. Ambedkar
ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
The judicial interpretation excludes the
social boycott of a few individuals
from the meaning of untouchability under Article 17.
The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities.
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
Untouchability involves both the stigma of ritual pollution attached to people and the practices adopted by the rest of society to protect itself from that supposed pollution.

secs.t: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

x: Exam angle: G2 2024 asked which amendment allows relaxation of qualifying marks in promotions - the correct answer is the
82nd
; the key circulated for that paper says 89th, which is the NCSC-NCST bifurcation amendment.
The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.

secs.t: Articles 341 and 342 - SC/ST lists

x: Exam angle: CDX AP History (p.424) credits "Article 344" with adding castes to the list - that is wrong; Art. 344 is the Official Language Commission. The power is
Art. 341
(and 342 for STs).

The term was first used by the Simon Commission, received statutory shape in the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first official list was issued in 1936. 'Depressed Classes' was the earlier terminology.

secs.t: National Commissions for SCs and STs

x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.
The 89th Constitutional Amendment created the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A, and it began functioning from
19 February 2004
The Chairperson of the NCST has the rank of a Union Cabinet Minister, the Vice-Chairperson has the rank of a Minister of State, and the members have Secretary rank.

secs.t: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

x: Madiga Dandora, led by Manda Krishna Madiga through MRPS, demanded A-B-C-D categorisation and a separate share within the Scheduled Caste quota in Andhra Pradesh.

Indra Sawhney dealt principally with reservation under Article 16(4), the 50 per cent ceiling and reservation at initial appointment; it did not uphold Andhra Pradesh’s Scheduled Caste sub-classification.

M. Nagaraj upheld the 77th, 81st and 85th Amendments and required the State to show quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequacy of representation and administrative efficiency under Article 335.

secs.t: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

x: Bhagya Reddy Varma established
Jagan Mitra Mandali
in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.
The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
V.R. Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission, Bhagya Reddy Varma founded Jagan Mitra Mandali, and Ambedkar founded Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha.

secs.t: Literature against untouchability → author

x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.
Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, Annihilation of Caste by B.R. Ambedkar, Gulamgiri by Jyotiba Phule and Jatimimamsa by Sree Narayana Guru.
Jyotiba Phule wrote
Gulamgiri
, published in 1873, in which caste oppression was compared with American slavery.

secs.t: Statements on caste and outcastes → leader

x: B.
R. Ambedkar
described caste as a division of labourers and rejected the term ‘Harijan’ for Dalits.
Gandhi is associated with reform from within, whereas Ambedkar advocated legal-constitutional rights and annihilation of caste.
The Poona Pact took place in 1932, the Yeola declaration in 1935, Karamchedu in 1985 and Tsundur in 1991.

secs.t: Caste atrocities - causes (NCSC&ST reports), major incidents → state, social boycott

x: The Karamchedu incident of 1985, in which Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords, sparked the independent Dalit movement.

The PoA Act was enacted in 1989 and the Rules were framed in 1995; the framework includes special courts and State and district vigilance and monitoring committees, with a 60-day limit for police investigation.

secs.t: Measures against untouchability - legislation, education, awareness, economic empowerment

x: NSFDC, NSKFDC, PM-DAKSH and VCF-SC are all listed among economic empowerment measures, with the associations stated in the question.
Only 24 cases were registered nationwide under the PCR Act in 2023, while pendency stood at 97%; vigilance committees also met irregularly.
Andhra Pradesh provides enhanced monetary relief and free legal aid to victims of atrocities.

secs.t: Manual scavenging - MS Act 2013, surveys, rehabilitation

x: The 2013 Act prohibits manual scavenging, unsafe cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and requires identification and rehabilitation.
All four statements correctly describe NAMASTE: its two ministries, zero sanitation deaths goal, allocation of ₹349.70 crore, and the stated stipend and health coverage.
The reported figures were 90,915 sewer/septic workers and 1.3 lakh waste pickers profiled, with 58,000 manual scavengers identified.

secs.t: Part XVI (Articles 330-342) - special provisions for certain classes

x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the list of Scheduled Tribes, and Article 342A concerns socially and educationally backward classes.
After the 2008 delimitation based on Census 2001, 84 Lok Sabha seats were reserved for SCs and 47 for STs.
The post-2008 delimitation used Census 2001, and the reserved seats rose from 79 to 84 for SCs and from 41 to 47 for STs.

secs.t: SC population data - India and AP (Census 2011)

x: Scheduled Castes constituted 16.6% of India's population according to Census 2011 data.
In Andhra Pradesh,
the SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population
The Scheduled Caste literacy rate in Andhra Pradesh is given as
Alluri Sitharama Raju had the lowest Scheduled Caste population share at 2.49%, whereas Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema had the highest at 24.85%.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Madiga Dandora movement and the 2000 Andhra Pradesh Act initiated the sub-classification debate within the Scheduled Castes, which culminated in the Davinder Singh judgment of 2024.
A major criticism is that untouchability is not constitutionally defined, allowing newer indirect forms to potentially escape effective penal consequences.
The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and stated that any change would require a holistic empirical review.

rows.title: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and amendments; Civil Rights Protection Act 1955
sub: Group-II S3-32: Statutory provisions for SCs - PoA Act 1989, Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955

secs.t: Atrocities Act - dilution case, 2018 amendment, Prithvi Raj Chauhan

x: Exam angle: G2 2024 - the case "alleged to have diluted" the Act =
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan
In
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
, decided on 20 March 2018, the Supreme Court issued directions concerning preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest.
The power to grant relief or quash proceedings is available where no prima facie case exists; statement 3 reverses this condition.
The Supreme Court cancelled the High Court's anticipatory bail, held that Section 18 applies where a prima facie case exists and stated that a mini-trial is impermissible at the bail stage.

secs.t: Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955

x: Exam angle: Untouchability (Offences) Act "extends to the whole of India"; MPPSC accepted both "cognizable and triable summarily" and "cognizable and non-compoundable".
The Act was enacted to give effect to
Article 17
of the Constitution, which abolishes untouchability.
Section 3 deals with religious disabilities, including barring entry to or worship in public places of worship.
Section 6
deals with refusal to sell goods or render services on the ground of untouchability.
Section 15A provides for State duties such as legal aid, special courts, surveys of untouchability-prone areas, awareness measures and related implementation duties.
For a first offence, the stated punishment is imprisonment of one to six months and a fine of ₹100 to ₹500.
The
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
is the nodal ministry, with the Ministry of Home Affairs also associated with implementation.
The rules made for carrying out the purposes of the Act are known as the Protection of Civil Rights Rules, 1977, commonly called the
PCR Rules, 1977

secs.t: Atrocities Act provisions → section

x: The Act covers specified offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons, treats them as cognizable, permits arrest without warrant, and has applied to Jammu and Kashmir since 2019.
The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants.
Since 1 July 2024, references to the IPC and CrPC in the Act are read as references to the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
The Act was enacted in 1989, commenced in 1990, amended in 2015, Section 18A was inserted in 2018, and its application extended to Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

secs.t: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

x: The PoA Rules require investigation by an officer not below the rank of DSP and completion with charge-sheet filing in the Special Court within 60 days.
Investigation and filing of the charge-sheet are subject to 60-day timelines, while the Special Court should, as far as possible, complete the trial within two months of the charge-sheet.

secs.t: Atrocities Act 2015 amendment - changes

x: Garlanding an SC/ST person with footwear was included among the new or rephrased atrocities under the 2015 amendment.
Tonsuring, forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass and dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi are recognised acts under the amended framework.
The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.

secs.t: Enforcement data - NCRB and AP

x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a crime rate of
per lakh Scheduled Caste population in the cited SDG India Index.

Crimes against Scheduled Tribes declined by 23.1%, crimes against Scheduled Castes by 3.6%, and Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar were the leading States mentioned for crimes against Scheduled Castes.
Uttar Pradesh
accounted for 173 of the 180 cases recorded nationally in 2023.
The 26-month duration, compared with the 60-day limit, illustrates chronic pendency and delay in investigation.
The Director of Prosecutions
conducted the State-level review in Vijayawada and issued the guidelines.

secs.t: Institutional machinery

x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional machinery: State-level chairmanship by the Chief Minister, district-level chairmanship by the Collector, a Secretary-level nodal officer, and Protection Cells under an IG or ADGP.
SC/ST Protection Cells function under an Inspector General or Additional Director General of Police, not under a District Judge.

secs.t: Manual scavenging laws

x: The 1993 Act prohibited employing manual scavengers and constructing dry latrines.
Local authorities are required to conduct surveys and build sanitary latrines within
three years
NSKFDC was established in 1997 and is the nodal agency for the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers.
The offences are cognizable and non-bailable, with the stated penalties for first contravention and hazardous sewer cleaning.
NAMASTE formalises sewer and septic-tank workers, subsumed the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers, and aims at zero sanitation fatalities.

secs.t: PoA Act procedure sections → content

x: Section 4A requires immediate registration of the FIR and does not permit a preliminary inquiry as a prerequisite.
States must ensure legal aid, travel and maintenance for victims and witnesses, and identification of atrocity-prone areas.
The 2015 amendment defined economic boycott and social boycott and made them offences amounting to atrocities under the Act.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The task force report proposed higher relief, counselling, State relief cells, and transmission of FIRs and charge-sheets to the authorities within 24 hours.
The Sukanya Shantha decision held that
Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma
, expanding the understanding of untouchability beyond narrow physical exclusion.
The post-rally 'shuddhikaran' ritual revived the debate over whether caste-based purity stigma falls within the prohibition of untouchability under Article 17.

rows.title: Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation
sub: Group-II S3-35: Constitutional and statutory provisions for Backward Classes - Articles 15(4), 16(4), 338B; commissions

secs.t: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

x: Exam angle: match amendment to clause; "which article was added to overcome Champakam Dorairajan" → 15(4).
The
77th Constitutional Amendment Act
, 1995 inserted Article 16(4A) to provide reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, in response to the Indra Sawhney judgment.
The 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A), the 81st dealt with backlog vacancies, the 82nd inserted the proviso to Article 335, and the 85th provided consequential seniority.

secs.t: Backward Classes Commissions - Article 340

x: Exam angle: "commission on reservation in government employment" =
Mandal
The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, and the recommendation was implemented by the
V.P. Singh government
Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and recommend remedial measures.
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission did not accept
caste
as the criterion, although its broader criteria included educational and occupational disadvantage and inadequate representation.
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission's report listed about 2,399 castes, while the Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population.

secs.t: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus

x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.
The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
The Muralidhara Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation, examined minority inclusion and contributed to a higher total quota.
No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 concerns urban local-body polls under
the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965

secs.t: EWS reservation - 103rd Amendment

x: The 103rd Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6), introduced EWS reservation of 10 percent outside the existing SC, ST and OBC quotas, and originated as the 124th Constitutional Amendment Bill.
A five-judge Constitution Bench upheld the 103rd Amendment by a
majority in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022).
The 124th Amendment Bill, 2019, became the 103rd Constitutional Amendment and provided for
reservation for economically weaker sections

secs.t: Backward Classes in the Constitution

x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5), enabling special provisions for admission of SEBCs, SCs and STs, including in private educational institutions other than minority institutions.

secs.t: Indra Sawhney - rulings

x: Indra Sawhney accepted caste as a possible main criterion, prescribed the general 50 per cent ceiling and excluded the creamy layer.
The judgment laid down that total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent, though extraordinary circumstances may justify an exception.
The judgment confined the reservation policy under consideration to initial appointments and held that it did not apply to promotions.

secs.t: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through
the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee
The 11 March 2026 verdict held that parental salary alone cannot determine creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts.

The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in October 2017, received 14 extensions, examined sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes, and submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023.

secs.t: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists

x: Article 342A provided for the
President
to notify the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes.
The 105th Amendment restored the power of the States to identify and maintain their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes.
The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand
are identified as live reservation issues in Andhra Pradesh.
APSES residential school admissions for 2024–25 continue to use BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E carrying 4 per cent.
The reserved Supreme Court verdict concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota in relation to persons who converted to Islam.

rows.title: Scheduled Tribes - Forest Rights Act 2006, Fifth and Sixth Schedules, TSP, Eklavya schools
sub: Group-II S3-8: Tribal problems and tribal development approaches - isolation, assimilation, integration
Group-II S3-34: Statutory provisions for STs - Forest Rights Act 2006, PESA Act 1996
Group-II S3-41: Welfare programmes for SCs and STs - scholarships, hostels, special component plan, TSP

secs.t: Forest Rights Act 2006

x: Exam angle: the right to fell and transport
bamboo
comes from the
FRA
, not the IFA amendment.
The
Gram Sabha
initiates the determination process and passes resolutions on claims under Section 6 of the Forest Rights Act.
The Gram Sabha initiates and resolves claims, while six-member Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees examine claims and issue titles.
The Act’s full title concerns recognition of forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional
Forest Dwellers
, and its stated objective was to undo historical injustice to forest dwellers.
Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before
13 December 2005
for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.
Bharia of Madhya Pradesh
was the first PVTG mentioned as receiving habitat rights; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.

secs.t: ST identification - criteria, procedure, religion

x: The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.
The stated sequence is proposal by the State, examination by the Registrar General of India and NCST, consideration by the Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).
Article 366(25)
defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to the tribes or tribal communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes under Article 342.

secs.t: Tribal Sub-Plan

x: TSP funds are to be at least proportional to the ST population and additional to normal plan flows or general benefits.
The Tribal Sub-Plan is now referred to as the
Scheduled Tribe Component or Development Action Plan for STs
(DAPST).
The Tribal Sub-Plan originated in 1972 and was adopted in the Fifth Plan; the Special Component Plan became SCSP and later DAPSC; DAPST is the present ST-focused form.

secs.t: Eklavya Model Residential Schools

x: The tribal residential schools in Andhra Pradesh are run by the Andhra Pradesh Tribal Welfare Residential Educational Institutions Society (
APTWREIS
), known as Gurukulam.
All four statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh has 734 pre-matric and 300 post-matric SC hostels, 17 Ananda Nilayams, and 371 Tribal Welfare Ashram schools with 1.65 lakh students.
Social Welfare residential schools recorded an SSC pass percentage of

secs.t: Tribal welfare institutions

x: All three are objectives of TADP/ITDA: agricultural improvement, fruit-bearing plantations and other income-generating activities in tribal areas.
The Tribal Sub-Plan strategy emerged from an expert committee of the
Ministry of Education and Social Welfare
TSP monitoring was shifted from the Planning Commission to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in
January 2017
The monitoring shift occurred in January 2017, online monitoring covers 41 ministries, and Andhra Pradesh enacted a 2013 law binding proportional allocation.

secs.t: Scheduled Tribes in AP

x: In PESA areas, at least 50 per cent of seats go to Scheduled Tribes and all chairpersons are Scheduled Tribes.
All three statements are correct: the AP PESA Rules were issued in 2011, 2,038 PESA Gram Sabhas are notified, and the stated individual and community FRA titles have been issued.

secs.t: Tribal land and displacement in AP

x: The Samatha judgment held that land in Scheduled Areas cannot be transferred or leased to non-tribals or private companies, including private mining companies.
The case arose against the background of mining leases in the
Visakhapatnam Agency
, where the AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation was enforced.
Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas can prevent alienation and restore illegally alienated land belonging to Scheduled Tribes.

secs.t: Tribal terms for outsiders and exploiters (Diku) - meaning

x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
Birsa’s Ulgulan was aimed at British land-grabbing and the exploitative dikus.

secs.t: Tribal problems - land alienation, indebtedness, displacement, shifting cultivation, bonded labour

x: Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation
All three statements correctly identify problems associated with tribal communities: loss of habitat, educational and linguistic disadvantages, malnutrition, forced labour and displacement.
The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.

secs.t: Approaches → proponent (isolation, assimilation, integration)

x: Isolation seeks to keep tribes apart for cultural protection; assimilation seeks their absorption as ‘backward Hindus’; integration combines development with retention of identity.

Robert Redfield originated the Great and Little Tradition; McKim Marriott proposed Universalisation and Parochialisation; M.N. Srinivas developed dominant caste; N.K. Bose is associated with the Hindu method of tribal absorption.

secs.t: Panchsheel for tribal development - principles and source

x: The fifth principle is to judge development by the quality of human character evolved rather than by the amount of money spent.
Although one listing presents encouragement of tribal languages separately, the standard wording keeps it within the first principle of developing tribal communities along their own genius.
CDX credits Verrier Elwin with formulating Panchsheel under Nehru’s influence, while its stated source is Nehru’s foreword to A Philosophy for NEFA.

secs.t: Tribal movements and revolts - issues raised

x: Birsa’s Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, opposed land-grabbing and forced labour, sought Abua Raj, and led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
The correct sequence is Santhal Hul (1855–56), Birsa’s Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa rebellion (1922–24), and Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967–70).
The Srikakulam Girijan movement was led by Vempatapu Satyanarayana and Adibhatla Kailasam, raised issues of land alienation, moneylenders and forest officials, and later turned Naxalite.

secs.t: Displacement and rehabilitation - Polavaram, bauxite in Agency areas

x: The stated concerns of the Koya and Kondh communities include land rights, inadequate compensation and displacement without proper rehabilitation.
The private pumped-storage projects were mentioned in
Koyyuru, Hukumpeta and Ananthagiri
in ASR district.
In 2013, Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining under the Forest Rights Act, after which the project was cancelled.
The
Koya and Kondh
tribes are mentioned as opposing Polavaram over land rights, compensation and rehabilitation.

secs.t: FRA and forest/wildlife law linkages - CWH, MFP and bamboo, Indian Forest Act

x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are areas within national parks and sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, and they are notified after an open process with affected communities.
MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete; this position was repeatedly upheld by the Supreme Court.

secs.t: FRA implementation - claims vs titles, AP data, CFR

x: More than 47,900 CFR/CFRR claims were rejected.
Although RoFR can expand to “Right of First Refusal” in another usage, the Andhra Pradesh usage here is “
Recognition of Forest Rights
There were 1,16,021 RoFR cultivators among Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan beneficiaries in 2025–26.
Statement 3 is not a gap; the identified gap is weak MoTA capacity.

secs.t: Related laws - RFCTLARR 2013 consent and SIA in Scheduled Areas

x: The RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment
mandatory
Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable
Habitats of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups receive legal protection under the RFCTLARR Act.
The District Mineral Foundation uses the definitions of “affected” and “displaced” families contained in the
RFCTLARR Act, 2013

secs.t: Economic empowerment - Stand-Up India, Venture Capital Fund for SCs, NSFDC and NSTFDC loans

x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016 under the Ministry of Finance and targets at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch for a greenfield enterprise.
The Venture Capital Fund for SCs is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, dates from 2014-15 and has a range of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore.

secs.t: Dr Ambedkar Foundation initiatives - Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence, coaching schemes

x: The Dr Ambedkar Foundation runs the Dr Ambedkar National Centre located at Janpath, besides its other schemes.
The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence provide free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.
SHRESHTA places bright SC students in top residential schools through the National Testing Agency’s NETS test.

secs.t: AP SC/ST welfare corporations and schemes - founding year and role, land purchase, self-employment

x: The GCC purchases minor forest produce at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers.
The APSCCFC provides self-employment support, including rehabilitation of Jogin women under the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis Act, 1989.
SC pensions of Rs 4,000 are provided to Dappu artists and cobblers, and SC households receive free power up to 200 units.

secs.t: Sanitation workers' welfare - NAMASTE scheme for sewers and septic tanks

x: NAMASTE, launched in 2022, seeks to end manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks and promote mechanised sanitation.
All four are components of NAMASTE: worker profiling in over 4,800 ULBs, PPE and safety training, a 25% machine subsidy and skilling with a Rs 3,000 stipend.
NAMASTE is backed by the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation was set up in 1997.

secs.t: Skill and livelihood programmes for tribals - Roshni, Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, TRIFED, MSP for MFP

x: TRIFED was established in 1987 and is associated with tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce.
The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission is run by TRIFED and focuses on buying Minor Forest Produce at MSP, value addition and GI tags.
Van Dhan Vikas Kendras generally involve about 15 SHGs, with up to 20 gatherers per group, and at least 60% ST participation.

secs.t: Scholarships for SC/ST students - pre-matric, post-matric, National Overseas, Top Class, fellowships

x: The SC Post-Matric Scholarship is the largest central SC scheme with 60:40 cost sharing, while the specified ST scholarships are classified as stated.
The National Overseas Scholarship provides 20 awards a year, comprising 17 for ST students and 3 for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.
The ST pre-matric scholarship covers Classes IX and X; the post-matric scholarship applies thereafter.

secs.t: Area and habitation programmes - PM-AJAY, PM-JANMAN, Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan

x: PM-JANMAN focuses on houses, roads, water, Mobile Medical Units and hostels;
industrial mining leases
are not among the stated focus areas.
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan has an outlay of
Rs 79,156 crore
The stated Andhra Pradesh coverage comprises 79 PM-JANMAN hostels and 4 Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan hostels.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Parasnath Hills have both Jain pilgrimage significance and Santhal religious significance, and the dispute is discussed in relation to Articles 25, 26, 29, the Fifth Schedule and Article 244.
All three pairings are correct: 4,172 VDVKs were noted, EMRS received a raised allocation in Budget 2026-27, and diversion of sub-plan funds remains a criticism.
The issues concern funding for CFR management, alleged disregard of FRA in Agasthyamalai eviction orders, and the wider development-versus-consent debate.
The issue concerning Parasnath Hills or Marang Buru involves competing Jain and Santhal claims under the Fifth Schedule context.

rows.title: Child rights - Articles 21A, 24, 39(e)(f); UNCRC; Right to Education Act 2009
sub: Group-II S3-39: Provisions for children - Article 21A, RTE Act, JJ Act, POCSO, child labour law

secs.t: RTE Act 2009 - commencement, age group, 25% quota, PTR, teacher qualification, no-detention, SMCs

x: Exam angle: statement pairs - "6-14 years" and "enacted under Art. 21A" are both correct (APPSC answer: both).
Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the
National Council for Teacher Education
(NCTE).
The original no-detention provision extended up to Class VIII, while the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after regular examinations and a re-examination opportunity.

secs.t: Features of RTE Act - what is and is not included

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2017 asked the odd one out - "Central government has sole responsibility for funds" is NOT a feature.

All four are features of the RTE Act: it prohibits screening and capitation fee, physical punishment, mental harassment and private tuition by teachers, and provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children.

secs.t: UNCRC - adoption, articles, India's ratification, rights and principles, protocols, Children's Day

x: The sequence is 1989 adoption of the UNCRC, 1992 Indian accession, 2000 adoption of two Optional Protocols, and 2011 adoption of the Communications Procedure Protocol.
Participation is a broad rights category, while respect for the child’s views is a related core principle; the reason does not by itself explain the complete classification of rights.

secs.t: Child rights Articles number game → subject and amendment

x: Article 45
was substituted by the 86th Amendment to provide for early childhood care and education until children attain six years of age.
Article 39(e)
, a Directive Principle of State Policy, addresses protection of tender age and work unsuitable to age or strength.
Article 39(f) provides for children to develop in freedom and dignity and for childhood and youth to be protected against exploitation.

secs.t: Child helplines and portals → number/purpose

x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24x7 emergency helpline for children.
TrackChild handles tracking of missing and found children, Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting, and CARINGS relates to child adoption information and guidance.
e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights.
CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline and is now integrated with ERSS-112.

secs.t: NCPCR and SCPCR - parent Act, composition, powers, AP SCPCR

x: The NCPCR has powers of a
civil court
while inquiring into complaints.
The specified monitoring mandate includes the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009.
V. Gandhi Babu of the AP SCPCR directed admission-related measures for migrant and fisherfolk children in Kolleru in Eluru district.

secs.t: National Policy for Children 2013 and National Plan of Action for Children - priority areas

x: The four priority areas are survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and participation.
The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 put the National Policy for Children, 2013 into operation.

secs.t: Child rights cases → issue

x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
(2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.
Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act, while Bachpan Bachao Andolan addressed trafficking, circus children and FIRs concerning missing children.
The sequence is Unni Krishnan (1993), the Constitution Amendment Bill (July 1997), the 86th Amendment (December 2002), and Pramati (2014).

secs.t: Child-related indicators - child sex ratio, child labour, AP figures

x: The NFHS-5 figures stated are an infant mortality rate of 35.2, an under-five mortality rate of 41.9 and a total fertility rate of 2.0.
The figures refer to working children aged 5–14 years.
All four indicators are correctly stated for NFHS-5.

secs.t: Adoption - CARA, Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, JJ Act route

x: CARA became a statutory body under the
Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
The Adoption Regulations, 2022 provide a two-month reconsideration period for surrendered children.
HAMA applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, while the adoption route under the Juvenile Justice Act is open to all religions.

secs.t: Universalisation of elementary education - SSA, Samagra Shiksha, no-detention changes

x: The allocation mentioned for Samagra Shiksha for 2026–27 is
Rs 42,100 crore
All three statements are correct: KGBVs are supported up to Class 12, CwSN support is Rs 3,500, and Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.
The 2019 amendment allowed examinations in Classes 5 and 8 and permitted a child to be held back after failing the re-examination.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The DPDP Act, 2023 defines a child as a person below 18 years and requires verifiable parental consent for processing the child's data.
POCSO defines a child as below 18 years, child labour law uses the below-14 threshold stated here, and RTE covers children aged 6–14 years.
All three are identified areas of criticism and debate: the age of consent, arbitrariness in the JJ transfer system and vacant RTE quota seats.
