rows.title: Juvenile Justice Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment 2016
sub: Group-II S3-24: Child abuse - forms, causes, consequences and the legal framework
Group-II S3-25: Child labour - magnitude, causes, legislation and rehabilitation

secs.t: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate

x: Exam angle: APPSC-GS 2022 - the MP High Court asked the Centre to lower the age of consent to 16 because
social-media exposure brings earlier puberty
Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting; Sections 29 and 30 contain presumptions against the accused; and the prescribed timelines are two months for investigation and one year for trial.
The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography.
Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting, Sections 29–30 place the burden of proof on the accused, and Section 22 deals with false complaints, subject to the good-faith exception.
POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.
The Justice Verma Committee supported 16 years, the 2011 parliamentary report rejected minor consent, and BNS Section 63 retains 18 years.
The Supreme Court set aside the ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO; it did not itself create such an exclusion.

secs.t: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986 and 2016 amendment - title, ages, hazardous list, exceptions

x: Exam angle: the year 1986. The "adolescent" category came only in 2016.
The retained hazardous categories are mines, inflammable substances and explosives, and hazardous processes under the Factories Act.
Helping in a family or family enterprise after school hours is a specified exception, provided the conditions relating to schooling are satisfied.
The exception covers a child artist in audio-visual entertainment but excludes circus work and requires that schooling should not be affected.

secs.t: Juvenile courts and boards - body, best-interest principle, AP functioning

x: The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.
Andhra Pradesh had Boards in the erstwhile 13 districts, undertook selection for bodies in the 13 new districts, and its Juvenile Welfare Department also runs the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.

secs.t: JJ (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015 - JJBs, heinous offences, CWCs, CARA, 2021 amendment

x: For a child in the 16–18 age group accused of a heinous offence carrying a minimum punishment of seven years, the Juvenile Justice Board conducts a preliminary assessment.
Juvenile offenders are dealt with under the guiding principle of
the best interests of the child
For a 16–18-year-old accused of a heinous offence, the JJB conducts a preliminary assessment and may transfer the case to the Children’s Court.
Mission Vatsalya covers former child-protection services as well as CWCs, JJBs and DCPUs.
Article 39(e) concerns protection of tender age from abuse, while Article 39(f) concerns protection against exploitation and moral and material abandonment.

secs.t: PENCIL portal and National Child Labour Project - ministry, enforcement

x: PENCIL is the online portal for effective enforcement of
the amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
Special Training Centres cater to rescued children aged
9–14 years
before they join regular school.
The Gurupadswamy Committee identified
poverty
as the root cause of child labour and recommended banning hazardous work while regulating the rest.

secs.t: Missing and exploited children - CHILDLINE, Operation Muskaan/Smile, AHTUs

x: The operations scanned railway stations, bus stands, markets and dhabas.
The widened concept includes sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal.
The widened definition covers the specified forms of trafficking
irrespective of consent
The provision is now referred to as Section 143 of the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

secs.t: International and judicial standards - ILO 138 and 182, M.C. Mehta v. State of TN

x: Exam angle: UPPSC 2003 key "All of the above": the Constitution, the SC judgment of 10 Dec 1996 and the UN Charter.
Convention 138 concerns minimum age for employment, while Convention 182 concerns the worst forms of child labour; India ratified both in 2017.
The 2011 Bachpan Bachao Andolan case emphasised stricter enforcement and the rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers.

secs.t: Earlier juvenile laws and the trigger for 2015

x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 was the first uniform law and prescribed an age of 16 years for boys and 18 years for girls.
The JJ Act, 2000 prescribed a uniform age of
18 years
and was amended in 2006.
The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by
the Delhi gang rape case of 2012

secs.t: NCRB data on crimes against children - top states, child marriage by state

x: Kidnapping and abduction
were reported as the largest categories of crimes against children in 2024.
The reported increase in crimes against children since 2013 was
NCRB 2021 data reported that
of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child.

secs.t: Child helplines and reporting - CHILDLINE, 112, POCSO e-Box

x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.
The cybercrime portal cybercrime.gov.in is used for CSAM and other online abuse, under the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and the Ministry of Home Affairs.

secs.t: Forms of child abuse

x: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary
are identified as forms of social abuse.
Online abuse and CSAM are dealt with under the IT Act, 2000, and the IT Rules, 2021 require large platforms to detect CSAM automatically.
Child labour is recognised as a form of abuse; India is described as having the largest number of child labourers in the world, with debt bondage extending across generations.

secs.t: Causes and consequences

x: Parental alcoholism
is listed as a cause.
Lack of affectionate relationships is a cause, while deviant behaviour such as drug abuse and stealing is a consequence.
Family conflict and unsafe institutions can contribute to trauma, delinquency and later revictimisation, along with other interpersonal and educational problems.

secs.t: Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD) - key findings

x: The 2007 study by the Ministry of Women and Child Development covered 13 states and about 12,447 children.
The study found that
two out of three
children faced physical abuse.
The study reported that
of children experienced one or more forms of sexual abuse.
The study concluded that
boys were as much at risk as girls

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh - child protection mechanisms and POCSO courts

x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli was launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026 to target
sexual offences against children
Operation Chinnari-Thalli includes Sexual Offender Sheets, zero pendency in POCSO cases and chargesheets within 60 days.
The
Women & Child Safety Wing
conducts “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programmes in schools and hostels.

secs.t: ILO core conventions on child labour and India's ratification

x: ILO Convention No. 138 concerns the Minimum Age for Employment, whereas Convention No. 182 concerns the Worst Forms of Child Labour.
The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child treats a child as a person below
18 years
of age.
The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on
12 June

secs.t: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors

x: The 4.35 million figure counts
main workers only
; it is not the total number of child labourers aged 5–14.
Brick kilns, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals and tea stalls are all identified sectors or settings associated with child labour.
The global figure for 2024 was 137.6 million child labourers, of whom 54 million were in hazardous work.

secs.t: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour

x: Employers may obtain more work for less pay by employing children, creating an economic incentive for child labour.
Family disorganisation, lack of awareness, kidnapping and weak enforcement were listed causes.
Debt bondage drives child and bonded labour in farms, brick kilns and domestic work.
Twenty-nine Chenchu and Yanadi tribals from Prakasam were rescued from a coal kiln in
Telangana

secs.t: Factories Act and Mines Act age limits

x: The Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment of children below 14, while the Mines Act, 1952 prohibits anyone below 18 from working in mines.
The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 treats working children as
children in need of care and protection

secs.t: Universal angles

x: In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court flagged misuse of POCSO in consensual adolescent relationships and urged
a “Romeo-Juliet” clause
The Supreme Court held that a minor cannot consent, set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling and invoked Article 142 for sentencing flexibility.
APSES 2024-25 recorded
342 street children rescued and 877 child marriages prevented
The 2012 Standing Committee supported 18 years, the 2023 Law Commission warned against lowering it, and the Supreme Court suggested a Romeo-Juliet clause in January 2026.

rows.title: Child welfare - ICDS, POSHAN Abhiyaan, mid-day meal (PM POSHAN), child marriage, malnutrition
sub: Group-II S3-43: Welfare programmes for women and children - ICDS, POSHAN, Mission Shakti, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

secs.t: Mid-day meal to PM POSHAN - year, renaming, coverage, norms, aims, financing, partners

x: PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools and provides one hot cooked meal.
PM POSHAN aims to address classroom hunger and improve enrolment, attendance, retention and concentration.
All four statements describe features of PM POSHAN: mandatory district-level social audits, school nutrition gardens, additional nutrition in specified districts, and participation of FPOs and SHGs.
The Akshaya Patra Foundation, based in Bengaluru, is identified as the largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme.
In Andhra Pradesh, the Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal was extended to Intermediate Classes XI-XII in 2024-25, covering 27.97 lakh students and providing five eggs, three chikkis and ragi java per week.

secs.t: ICDS - launch, ministry, services, Anganwadi worker, Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, One Nation One Anganwadi

x: Exam angle: "Anganwadi worker is a functionary of which scheme?" → ICDS; count and names of the six services.
Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the Anganwadi Centre, whereas immunisation, health check-up and referral services are delivered through the health system.
Cash maternity benefit
is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.
All four statements correctly describe the Anganwadi Worker, Anganwadi Helper and the joint AWW-ASHAs role in HBYC home visits.
The Scheme for Adolescent Girls covers
girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region
The three verticals are nutrition support including adolescent girls, ECCE for children aged 3-6 years, and Anganwadi infrastructure.
One Nation One Anganwadi enables migrant families to continue receiving benefits for children below six years and pregnant or lactating women after migration to another State.

secs.t: POSHAN Abhiyaan - launch, targets, Poshan Maah, Pakhwada, Tracker, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi

x: POSHAN Abhiyaan targets stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight.
POSHAN Abhiyaan envisages a Suposhit Bharat and a Jan Andolan, with the stated goal of reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.
Poshan Tracker data represents a census of children enrolled or covered at Anganwadi centres, while NFHS data is survey-based; therefore, the two are not strictly comparable.
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi integrates ECCE into Anganwadis and promotes play-based pedagogy, effectively developing them as pre-schools.

Poshan Tracker relates to real-time monitoring, Poshan Vatika to nutrition gardens, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi to ECCE and play-based pedagogy, and Poshan Pakhwada to brain development in the first six years.
The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40, changing to 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir; Union Territories without legislatures receive 100% Central funding.

secs.t: Child marriage - PCMA 2006, Prohibition Officers, age bill, data, district models

x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
The Bill was sent to a Standing Committee and subsequently lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
West Bengal, Bihar and Tripura
were identified among the States with the highest child-marriage levels in the cited NFHS-5 data.

secs.t: Child protection schemes - Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, sponsorship and foster care

x: Mission Vatsalya was introduced in 2021–22 for child protection and the promotion of a happy childhood, in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.
Mission Vatsalya subsumed the
Child Protection Services/Integrated Child Protection Scheme
and is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
PM CARES for Children was launched in 2021 for children who lost parents or specified guardians to COVID-19 and provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at 23, along with education and health support.

secs.t: Early childhood care - ECCE policy, NEP 2020 foundational stage, Anganwadi as pre-school

x: Article 45 concerns early childhood care and education for all children until they complete
six years
of age.
The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.
Bal Vatika was brought under
PM POSHAN
as part of the school nutrition framework.

secs.t: Maternal health schemes - benefit, eligibility, launch year, nodal ministry

x: Exam angle: PMSMA launch year (2016, G2-GS 2022); JSY sits under NHM, while PMMVY sits under MWCD.
JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns with free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
PMMVY provides maternity-related wage-loss compensation, while PMSMA provides free monthly antenatal check-ups on the 9th and identifies high-risk pregnancies.

secs.t: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and girl-child schemes - objectives, ministries, Sukanya Samriddhi, Balika Samriddhi, Dhanalakshmi

x: BBBP is implemented under
Sambal
, the safety component of Mission Shakti.
Balika Samriddhi provides a birth grant and scholarships; Dhanalakshmi is a conditional cash-transfer pilot; BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign; Sukanya Samriddhi matures at 21 years.
Dhanalakshmi was piloted in 2008, BBBP and Sukanya Samriddhi were launched in 2015, and PM Ujjwala followed in 2016.

secs.t: Women's credit, livelihood and welfare - RMK, DWCRA and DAY-NRLM SHGs, Swavalambini, Swayam Siddha, Swadhar, Ujjwala

x: DAY-NRLM
, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
Swavalambini was associated with 2022 and promoted entrepreneurship among women students in the North-East through MSDE and NITI Aayog.
PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched in May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cited figures are 22,692 cases through Sakhi OSCs, 28 Shakti Sadans and 1,02,000 women reached under PMMVY.
The criticism is that the schemes still emphasise survival rather than complete child development, while last-mile gaps persist in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
Tithi Bhojan began in Gujarat, and PMMVY is identified as the only cash maternity benefit written into the National Food Security Act.

rows.title: Rights of persons with disabilities - RPwD Act 2016, UNCRPD, accessibility (Sugamya Bharat)
sub: Group-II S3-38: Provisions for persons with disabilities - RPwD Act 2016 and accessibility measures

secs.t: Disability inclusion initiatives → target group and purpose

x: The Inclusive India initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, associated with the National Trust, seeks to bring persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream.
Divyang Shakti was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2026 and provides 100% free travel for persons with disabilities in APSRTC buses.

secs.t: Disability institutions - Chief Commissioner, State Commissioners, National Trust, RCI, NHFDC

x: The
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
is the statutory authority under the RPwD Act, 2016, responsible for monitoring implementation and taking up complaints.
The National Trust Act, 1999 covers autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities and provides for welfare and legal guardianship.
The RCI regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.

secs.t: International cooperation - MoUs, UNCRPD, ratification, Optional Protocol

x: The UNCRPD was adopted on 13 December 2006, India ratified it in October 2007, the RPwD Act was enacted in 2016, and it came into force on 19 April 2017.
All three statements are correct: adoption took place on 13 December 2006, India ratified the Convention in October 2007, and the RPwD Act, 2016, was enacted to fulfil UNCRPD obligations.

secs.t: RPwD Act 2016 - specified disabilities, benchmark disability, reservation, free education, replaced Act

x: Section 2(s) covers long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full participation in society.
The Act increased specified disabilities from 7 to 21, includes conditions such as autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease, and permits the Central Government to add more disabilities.
After
a Supreme Court interpretation in 2026
, survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the Act.

secs.t: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app

x: The three verticals are accessibility in the
built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem
The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as part of the right to life under
Article 21
and specified a minimum width of 1.8 metres.
From 18 March 2026, free APSRTC bus travel is available in the specified categories to persons with
40 percent
or more disability.

secs.t: Disability observances

x: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in 1981.

secs.t: Schemes for PwDs → benefit

x: UDID is
a single, digitally verifiable national disability card
and certificate.
The
ADIP
scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.
ADIP operates through institutions including National Institutes, Composite Regional Centres, ALIMCO and District Disability Rehabilitation Centres.
SIPDA
provides grants to States, bodies and universities for implementation of the RPwD Act.

secs.t: Disability data and AP welfare

x: India’s Census 2011 figure was 2.21 percent, whereas the approximate global estimate was about 16 percent; the difference suggests under-reporting in India.
The figures are orthopaedic 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.90 lakh, visual 2.03 lakh, multiple 1.96 lakh and mental 1.02 lakh.
The Corporation supplies aids and appliances and runs economic-rehabilitation schemes for persons with disabilities and senior citizens.

secs.t: Disability rights cases → issue

x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned deplaning and dignity; Vikash Kumar recognised a scribe as reasonable accommodation; Rajive Raturi concerned mandatory accessibility standards.
Jeeja Ghosh concerned the deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy by an airline, raising the right to dignity and resulting in compensation.
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC
(2021) recognised the availability of a scribe as reasonable accommodation even without benchmark disability.

secs.t: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups

x: The RCI Act, 1992 established the
Rehabilitation Council of India
, which became statutory from 1993.
The target group for special education is
children with disabilities
, or CwSN; it is not a programme exclusively for gifted groups.
Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities.
The inclusive education component of Samagra Shiksha took over the earlier
IEDSS
programme.

secs.t: Divyangjan entrepreneurship and livelihood - expos and fests, NHFDC, social enterprises employing PwDs

x: All four statements are correct: education loans are at 4 per cent, eligibility requires 40 per cent or more disability and age 18 or above, and the general loan ceiling is Rs 50 lakh.
The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal provides UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for employment opportunities.
ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise established in 1972 and manufactures aids and artificial limbs.

secs.t: Constitutional basis - Article 41, State List entry on relief of disabled, UNCRPD ratification

x: Article 41, among the Directive Principles of State Policy, refers to
public assistance in cases of disablement
, among other situations.
India spends approximately
0.02 per cent
of GDP on disability welfare.
The proposal for a national minimum disability pension of Rs 8,000 per month has been linked with
Article 41
, which refers to public assistance in cases of disablement.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court directed attention to prison accessibility and revision of prison manuals in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
The Supreme Court recognised digital access as part of Article 21 while citing the
United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
The cited Andhra Pradesh update records a disability pension of Rs 6,000 per month and distribution of 52,263 assistive devices.

rows.title: Rights of the elderly - Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007, schemes

secs.t: Elderly schemes → benefit and launch place

x: The scheme provides aids such as walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids and dentures to BPL senior citizens.
AVYAY is an umbrella programme comprising the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line.
IPOP can support up to 90 per cent of project cost for NGOs and covers old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units.
Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana, introduced in April 2021, was renamed from the
National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.

secs.t: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 - obligations, tribunals, cap, appeals, homes, 2019 bill

x: Section 23
permits a transfer of property to be declared void where the transferee neglects the senior citizen despite the condition of care attached to the transfer.
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was enacted in 2007; NPOP was issued in 1999; NPHCE began in 2010–11; and NPSC dates to 2011.

secs.t: National Policy on Older Persons 1999 and National Policy for Senior Citizens 2011

x: The policy includes health care, nutrition, self-provision, family care, NGO support and geriatric training among its 14 principal areas.
The policy addresses financial and food security, health, shelter and protection from abuse;
compulsory military service
is unrelated to it.
The newer draft policy emphasises
ageing in place
, housing, income security and tougher punishment for elder abuse.

secs.t: Elderly helpline - Elder Line

x: Elder Line 14567 is the National Helpline for Senior Citizens and forms part of AVYAY.
Elder Line is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment with State emergency response centres and technical support from
Tata Trusts and NSE Foundation
Elder Line is a National Helpline for Senior Citizens and is not limited merely to pension disbursement.

secs.t: International frameworks

x: The Madrid Plan was adopted in 2002, the International Day of Older Persons is observed from 1 October, World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on 15 June, and the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers 2021–2030.

secs.t: Elderly rights issues - elder abuse surveys, property transfer cancellation

x: HelpAge India
runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.
Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
permits the Tribunal to declare such a property transfer void when the promised care is not provided.
Such victims may approach
the Revenue Divisional Officer
(RDO).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposed floor is specifically intended to be indexed to inflation.
Weekly geriatric OPDs function in 1,684 PHCs and daily geriatric OPDs in 177 CHCs in Andhra Pradesh.
Seven physiotherapy centres treated 87,240 patients under the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens.

rows.title: Population problem, ageing and problems of the elderly
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I B-107

secs.t: Effects of population growth - economic, environmental, land holdings, case for control

x: A large workforce pays off economically only if it is
employed productively
Population growth can lead to
overuse of resources
, creating environmental stress.
Population growth
contributes to repeated subdivision and fragmentation of land holdings.
All four statements reflect the environmental case for population control and the counter-debate concerning the possible demographic and fiscal disadvantage of southern States.

secs.t: Population problem - Census 2011, transition stages, TFR (NFHS-5)

x: The year 1921 is known as the
Great Divide
in India’s demographic history.
The correct sequence is decline during 1911–1921, the Great Divide in 1921, population explosion during 1961–1971, and high but slowing growth during 1981–2011.
The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.

secs.t: Problems of the elderly - health, loneliness, abuse, dependency, feminisation

x: Ageing does not eliminate health expenditure; persons aged 80 and above face chronic disease, insurance may have age caps, and the elderly account for about 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
Ageism and abuse
are recognised social problems faced by elderly persons; loneliness and feminisation of ageing are also important concerns.
Under AVYAY, the SAGE component provides equity support of up to
₹1 crore
for senior-care start-ups.

secs.t: Ageing and family - old age homes, intergenerational support, living alone, rural vs urban

x: Care within joint families is weakening, while over 55% of the elderly live in nuclear households, highlighting changing family support arrangements.
The
Integrated Programme for Older Persons
provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.
Kerala
is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.

secs.t: Population control debates - two-child norms, AP stance, dependency ratio

x: The draft policy provides the stated incentive, removes the two-child norm for local elections and rests on five pillars.
In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003),
the Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm
The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India launched its first national family planning programme in 1952, Javed v. State of Haryana was decided in 2003, SRS 2024 provides the fertility-rate reference, and the Andhra Pradesh draft policy dates to March 2026.

India introduced the first national family planning programme in 1952, Kerala was first with the senior-citizens institutional framework, and Andhra Pradesh is associated with the draft Population Management Policy.

rows.title: Transgender persons - NALSA judgment, Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019
sub: Group-II S3-40: Provisions for the elderly and transgender persons

secs.t: Reservation and state measures - horizontal vs vertical, first service quota, AP pensions, welfare board, ID cards

x: The transgender community has sought horizontal reservation, which would cut across the SC, ST, OBC and General categories.
The measures include Tamil Nadu’s Welfare Board and tailoring cooperative, Kerala’s Sthree Suraksha scheme, and 3,125 certificates issued in Andhra Pradesh.
The Transgender Welfare Board and Thirunangaigal app are Tamil Nadu measures; Sthree Suraksha is a Kerala scheme; and the National Portal certificates relate to Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: FIRST transgender persons → post

x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific region to address the
United Nations General Assembly
The correct sequence is Shabnam Mausi as MLA in 1998, Manabi Bandyopadhyay as college principal in 2015, Joyita Mondal as judge in 2017, and Madhu Bai Kinnar as mayor in 2015.

secs.t: NALSA v. Union of India - year, bench, directions

x: NALSA rejected compulsory biological determination and recognised self-identified gender.
NALSA recognised the third gender, affirmed self-determined gender identity and applied the listed fundamental-rights provisions to transgender persons.
Both statements are true, and the direction to extend reservation in education and employment explains the treatment of transgender persons as socially and educationally backward.

secs.t: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019 - definition, certificate, offences, criticism

x: The 2019 definition includes trans men and women, intersex variations, genderqueer persons and specified socio-cultural identities including kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.
Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation.
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.
The advisory recommended review of the amendment and
separate intersex, transmen and transwomen categories in Census 2027

secs.t: Transgender Persons Rules 2020 and National Council for Transgender Persons

x: The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under
the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
The Council has governmental, expert and community representation and performs advisory and monitoring functions.
The Transgender Persons Rules, 2020 prescribe the application procedure through the national portal for obtaining the certificate of identity.

secs.t: SMILE, Garima Greh and National Portal - ministry, components, services

x: The transgender component includes scholarships, PM-DAKSH skilling and a PM-JAY-linked health package.
SMILE is an umbrella Central Sector Scheme of Rs 365 crore covering transgender welfare and rehabilitation related to begging.
Garima Greh provides
shelter homes for transgender persons
The Mumbai protest concerned
Maharashtra
's reply in proceedings before the Bombay High Court regarding horizontal reservation.

secs.t: Transgender data - Census 2011

x: Census 2011 counted approximately
4.88 lakh
transgender persons in India.
The order was Uttar Pradesh, followed by undivided Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar.
The NHRC Advisory 2.0 recommended Census categories for
intersex persons, trans men and trans women

secs.t: Rights of Transgender Persons Bill 2014 - mover and fate

x: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by
Tiruchi Siva
of the DMK.
The Bill was not passed by the Lok Sabha.

secs.t: Constitutional basis - Article 41 and State List entry on old age pensions

x: Invalidity and old-age pensions are included in
Concurrent List Entry 24

secs.t: AP - senior citizens and transgender welfare schemes, pension categories

x: NTR Bharosa provides
per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.
The cited rates are Rs 6,000 for persons with disabilities, Rs 10,000 for chronic diseases, Rs 15,000 for fully disabled persons and Rs 4,000 for transgender persons.
All three statements are part of the reported current-affairs position: the August 2026 assurance on identity cards, the Rs 200 IGNOAPS amount and the Rs 4,000 NTR Bharosa pension.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 2026 Amendment Act was reported to replace self-identification with medical-board certification and to face a Supreme Court challenge.
The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.
NHRC Advisory 2.0 included admission by self-identified gender, a ban on non-consensual intersex surgery on children and more Garima Grehs.

rows.title: Minority rights - Articles 29 and 30, National Commission for Minorities, Sachar Committee, schemes
sub: Group-II S3-36: Constitutional and statutory provisions for minorities - Articles 29, 30; National Commission for Minorities
Group-II S3-42: Welfare programmes for BCs and minorities - education, skill and credit schemes

secs.t: National Commission for Minorities - Act, notified communities, composition, appointment, powers

x: Exam angle: G1 2022 - "set up under the NCM Act 1992" is correct; the claim that the Ministry of Welfare notified five communities was the rejected statement.
The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
The Commission has seven members, at least five including the Chairperson must belong to minority communities, and the Vice-Chairperson was added by the 1995 amendment.
The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures;
conducting elections to minority educational institutions
is not one of its stated functions.
The milestones are correctly matched as 1978–non-statutory Commission, 1992–statutory NCM Act, 1993–first statutory Commission and 1995–addition of Vice-Chairperson.
The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in
Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B
, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
The five communities notified in 1993 were
Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis
or Zoroastrians.

secs.t: Articles 29 and 30 - scope, 'minority' undefined, unit for status, institution rights

x: The 44th Amendment added
Article 30(1A)
, providing that compulsory acquisition of property of a minority educational institution should not impair the right to establish and administer such institution.

Article 29(1) protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture, while Article 30 protects the rights of religious and linguistic minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.
Article 30(2)
provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.

secs.t: Sachar Committee - chair, year, mandate, Muslim groups, follow-ups

x: Exam angle: the Ashraf/Ajlaf/Arzal classification.
The
Ajlaf
, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.

The Sachar Committee was chaired by Rajinder Sachar, the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities by Justice Ranganath Misra, and the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee by Amitabh Kundu.
The Sachar Committee was the
Prime Minister’s High Level Committee on the social, economic and educational status of Muslims
, chaired by Rajinder Sachar and constituted in March 2005.

secs.t: Minority schemes → benefit

x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan, was introduced in 2022 as a Central Sector scheme, merges five schemes and is intended to run until 2025-26.
PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil.
Naya Savera provides free coaching, while Nai Udaan provides support after candidates clear the preliminary examinations of UPSC, SSC and State PSCs.

secs.t: Linguistic minorities - Articles 347, 350A, 350B, Special Officer

x: Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage, Article 350B creates the Special Officer, and both provisions were inserted by the Seventh Amendment Act, 1956.

Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

secs.t: State Minorities Commissions and AP minority welfare

x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh had six pre-matric and ten post-matric hostels, allocated ₹5 crore to six residential schools, and operated computer training through 36 centres in 26 districts.
All three statements are correct: imams received ₹10,000, muezzins ₹5,000, and the programme covered 4,984 masjids with an expenditure of ₹45 crore.

secs.t: Waqf administration - Waqf Act 1995, amendments, Central Waqf Council

x: The Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013 amended
the Waqf Act, 1995
; it did not replace the parent law.
The 2013 amendment barred
sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer
of waqf property.
The 2025 Act provided for officers
above the rank of Collector
to decide whether disputed land was government property.
The Supreme Court stayed the five-years-practising-Islam condition and the Collector’s power, and accepted the Limitation Act change.

secs.t: Minority rights cases → issue

x: Exam angle: G2 2017 - minority status is decided by the State's demography (true); "minority rights are
absolute
" is the untrue statement (APP's "absolute right" wording for Art. 30 should not be used in MCQs).

In re Kerala Education Bill corresponds to regulation of standards; St. Stephen's permits preference up to 50 per cent; T.M.A. Pai identifies the State as the unit; and P.A. Inamdar rejects such State-imposed reservation in the stated institutions.

secs.t: National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions - Act, powers

x: The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers.
The Commission exercises civil court powers and handles minority status and university-affiliation matters.

secs.t: Notified minority communities - number, names, additions, population

x: Jains
were added on 27 January 2014, increasing the number of nationally notified minority communities from five to six.
The notified communities number
six
after Jains were added to the five communities notified in 1993.
The Census 2011 population figures given are Muslims 172.2 million, Christians 27.8 million, Sikhs 20.8 million and Jains 4.5 million.

secs.t: PM Vishwakarma - target trades, benefits, implementing ministries

x: PM Vishwakarma was launched on
17 September 2023
, coinciding with Vishwakarma Jayanti.
PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades.
The scheme provides collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh initially and an additional Rs 2 lakh, with the credit carrying a 5 percent interest rate.

secs.t: Prime Minister's programme for welfare of minorities - name, focus areas, monitoring

x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 2006, the same year associated with the New 15 Point Programme.

secs.t: Scholarships for OBC/EBC/DNT - PM YASASVI, SHREYAS, minority scholarships

x: PM-YASASVI is a scholarship and educational support scheme for students belonging to OBC, EBC and DNT categories under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
PM-YASASVI includes top-class education and hostel support, reserves 30 percent of slots for girls and follows a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio.
The SHREYAS scheme supports higher education by funding 8,571 SC students studying at IITs and IIMs.

secs.t: Credit institutions - NBCFDC, NMDFC - loan schemes and channelling agencies

x: NBCFDC functions under the
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
New Swarnima is intended for women and Saksham for young professionals.
NMDFC Credit Line-1 has an income ceiling of Rs 3 lakh and Credit Line-2 of Rs 8 lakh.
NMDFC provides education loans, micro-finance and Virasat loans for artisans.
Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through
State Channelising Agencies

secs.t: Area development for minorities - Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, minority concentration areas

x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.
The stated coverage includes 870 minority concentration blocks and 321 towns, and has been extended to all districts, including 112 Aspirational Districts.
Eighty percent of PMJVK funds go to education, health and skills.
The allocation for women under PMJVK is stated to be
33-40 percent

secs.t: Denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes - SEED scheme, Idate Commission

x: SEED was launched in 2022 with an outlay of Rs 200 crore, an income criterion below Rs 2.5 lakh, and provisions for coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing.
Only
Rs 69.3 crore
was spent in five years, against the stated Rs 200 crore outlay, reportedly because States did not issue DNT certificates.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh BC and minority welfare - BC corporations, minority finance corporation, Imams and Muezzins honorarium

x: The AP Backward Classes are stated to comprise 138 communities organised into Groups A-E.
G.O. 1065 of August 2026 provides for
33.33 percent
BC reservation in urban local body polls.
The Assembly resolved to seek
33 percent
BC seats in legislatures.
The EWS department brings together the Reddy, Kamma, Kapu, Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vysya and EBC corporations.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: NSFDC was established in 1989 for Scheduled Castes, NBCFDC in 1992 for Backward Classes, NSTFDC in 2001 for Scheduled Tribes, and NMDFC serves minorities.
Jains were notified as a minority in 2014, the adviser’s resignation occurred in March 2026, Harjit Singh Grewal became NCM Chairperson in July 2026, and the NCSC review began in August 2026.

rows.title: Rights of workers and migrants - labour codes, unorganised sector, e-Shram, inter-state migrant workers

secs.t: Social security schemes → benefit, age, contribution; state worker pension schemes

x: NPS-Traders is intended for traders, shopkeepers and self-employed persons whose annual turnover does not exceed ₹1.5 crore.
PMJJBY and Atal Pension Yojana were launched in 2015, followed by PM-SYM in March 2019 and NPS-Traders in September 2019.
Membership of EPFO, ESIC or government-funded NPS, and being an income-tax payer, excludes eligibility.

secs.t: Unorganised Workers Social Security Act 2008, NCEUS, informal workforce

x: The 2008 Act established a
National Social Security Board
and listed welfare schemes in Schedule I.
Schedule I includes the National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana and RSBY, among others.
The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector was set up in 2004 and chaired by
Arjun Sengupta
The NCEUS report estimated that about
of Indians lived on under ₹20 a day.

secs.t: Earlier social protection schemes → launch year and target group

x: All four statements correctly describe RSBY, including its launch year, beneficiaries, ₹30,000 hospitalisation cover and later subsumption in AB-PMJAY.
Swavalamban was designed for unorganised workers joining
NPS-Lite
, with government co-contribution.

National Database of Unorganised Workers
, abbreviated as NDUW.

PMSBY, PMJJBY and PM-SYM
through the integrated welfare framework.

The definition of advertisement includes

resides or works
, subject to the applicable jurisdictional requirements.

Jago Grahak Jago is the flagship awareness campaign of the Department of Consumer Affairs and Jagriti is its mascot.

geography

domestic politics and regional pressures
affect foreign policy.
The 1962 war
led to a stronger realist orientation within India's strategic culture, alongside the continuing ideas of autonomy and restraint.

secs.t: Doctrines → leader

x: Nehruvian idealism is associated with Nehru, the Indira Doctrine with Indira Gandhi, the Gujral Doctrine with I.K. Gujral and strategic autonomy with all Prime Ministers since 1947.
The Gujral Doctrine of 1996 emphasised
non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours, non-interference and peaceful settlement
Strategic autonomy has continued through different phases: non-alignment during the Cold War and issue-based alignment or multi-alignment today.

secs.t: Core principles - anti-colonialism, anti-apartheid, disarmament, peaceful settlement, Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam

x: India opposed the NPT because it considered the division between nuclear-weapon states and non-nuclear-weapon states
discriminatory
India's principle favours peaceful settlement without force and supports strengthening the United Nations and other multilateral bodies.
India's G20 theme in 2023 was '
One Earth, One Family, One Future
', reflecting the idea of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.

secs.t: Institutions of foreign policy-making - MEA, NSC, NSA, Standing Committee

The Indian Council of World Affairs was founded in 1943 under
Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru
The correct order is the founding of ICWA in 1943, the Asian Relations Conference in 1947, establishment of the NSC in 1998, and the ICWA Act in 2001.

China stressed

as the framework for India-China ties during the Modi-Xi meeting referred to in the current context.
Taking Kashmir to the United Nations has been criticised as part of the debate over the limitations and consequences of idealist foreign-policy choices.

rows.title: Phases of Indian foreign policy - Nehruvian era, 1971-1991, post-Cold War, post-1998, contemporary multi-alignment

The IPKF operated in Sri Lanka from 1987 to 1990 under the India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987.
The 1987 India-Sri Lanka Accord was associated with Rajiv Gandhi and Sri Lankan President J.R. Jayewardene.

, under the Glenn Amendment, Japan and others imposed sanctions after the nuclear tests.

The Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver was granted to India on
6 September 2008
; the 123 Agreement followed in October 2008.

secs.t: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

x: The 1946–1962 phase is described as
optimistic non-alignment
, marked by idealism, Panchsheel, NAM, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism.
The Nehruvian phase emphasised Panchsheel, non-alignment, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism; it did not involve
formal alignment with a Cold War military bloc
The 1962–1971 phase was described as
realism and recovery
, including defence build-up, the 1965 war, Tashkent and refusal to sign the NPT.

secs.t: Post-Cold War shifts - Look East, economic diplomacy, West Asia

x: The 1991–1998 phase focused on
safeguarding strategic autonomy
after the collapse of the USSR and the 1991 economic crisis.
The Look East Policy was launched in 1991–1992 under Prime Minister
P.V. Narasimha Rao
and brought India closer to ASEAN.
The Gujral Doctrine advocated goodwill towards neighbouring countries without expecting immediate reciprocity.

secs.t: Contemporary multi-alignment - Quad, SCO, BRICS, Act East, Neighbourhood First, G20

x: India's response to the emerging multipolarity since 2008 is
issue-based alignment
, under which partnerships vary according to the issue involved.
The India-UK CETA was signed during the Prime Minister's UK visit in
July 2025
The correct sequence is Quad formation in 2007, Act East upgrade in 2014, India's full SCO membership in 2017, and Quad revival in 2017.

secs.t: Prime Ministers → signature foreign policy initiative

x: Nehru is associated with non-alignment and Panchsheel; Indira Gandhi with the Indo-Soviet Treaty and Bangladesh 1971; Rajiv Gandhi with the India-Sri Lanka Accord and IPKF; and P.V. Narasimha Rao with Look East and economic diplomacy.
The Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh 1971, Simla and Pokhran-I are all associated with Indira Gandhi's foreign-policy record.
Panchsheel, along with non-alignment and Commonwealth membership, is associated with
Jawaharlal Nehru

secs.t: Terms → meaning

x: Strategic autonomy is the freedom to assess each issue on its merits without joining military blocs; it is not the same as neutrality.
Multi-alignment means engaging rival powers simultaneously, such as through the Quad and BRICS/SCO, to maximise national interest.
Issue-based coalitions are partnerships selected according to the issue, such as
security cooperation with the United States and energy and defence cooperation with Russia
, rather than fixed alliances.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The phases indicate a movement from idealism towards realism and from non-alignment towards multi-alignment, with strategic autonomy remaining the underlying constant.
Both statements are true, but the reason describes issue-based coalition-building; it does not by itself fully explain the broader historical continuity of strategic autonomy across all phases.
The USSR tilt in 1971 and the closer US relationship after 2005 are cited in debates about whether external partnerships compromise strategic autonomy.

China lifted its technical hold

rows.title: Plurilateral groupings - G20, G7, BRICS, QUAD, I2U2, IBSA, BASIC, Colombo Security Conclave

secs.t: G7/G8 - members, "not a member", G8 to G7, outreach, PGII

x: Japan
is one of the seven G7 members, along with the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy and Canada.
The EU attends G7 proceedings, Russia joined in 1997–98 to form the G8, and its participation was suspended in 2014 after the Crimea crisis.
The G7 launched PGII in Germany in 2022 as an infrastructure plan and a counter to the Belt and Road Initiative.

secs.t: G20 - origin, first summit, members, troika, India's presidency

x: The G20 was established on 26 September 1999 as a forum of
finance ministers and central bank governors
, following the Asian Financial Crisis.
India's G20 presidency used the theme “
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future
The Johannesburg Declaration revised the goal to reduce the gender gap in labour-force participation by
25 percent
by 2030 from 2012 levels.

secs.t: BRICS - members, expansion, chair, first summit, NDB and CRA

x: Egypt
was among the countries included in the 2024 BRICS expansion, along with Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE.
The New Delhi Declaration included support for
restoring the WTO Appellate Body
, along with UNSC expansion, IMF/WB quota reform, West Asia de-escalation and zero tolerance on terrorism.
The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement, created in 2014, has a liquidity pool of
100 billion dollars

secs.t: Grouping → members and India's status

x: I2U2
comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the United States.
BASIC comprises Brazil, South Africa, India and
China
, whereas IBSA comprises India, Brazil and South Africa.
The Quad comprises India, the United States, Japan and Australia, not China.
At SB64 in Bonn, India aligned with G77 plus China, LMDC and BASIC.

secs.t: Grouping share of world GDP, trade, population

x: Exam angle: UKPSC 2024 - "BRICS = 46% of global trade" was the wrong statement; "first summit 2009 in Russia" is correct.
The expanded BRICS grouping accounts for more than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and approximately 50% of the world's population.
In 2011, BRICS accounted for about 20% of global GDP but only
of IMF votes.

secs.t: Quad - origin, revival, summits, initiatives

x: The Quad's precursor was the 2004 Tsunami Core Group; the first Quad meeting took place in 2007, and the grouping was revived in 2017.
The Quad initiatives include the Quad Vaccine Partnership, the Critical and Emerging Technologies group and IPMDA.
IPMDA stands for
Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness
and was launched in 2022 under the Quad framework.

secs.t: IBSA and BASIC

x: The IBSA Trust Fund became operational in 2004, is managed by UNOSSC and finances projects in least developed countries.
India proposed an IBSA Digital Innovation Alliance involving UPI and CoWIN, along with an NSA-level dialogue.
India and Brazil set the aim of doubling bilateral trade to
30 billion dollars

secs.t: Colombo Security Conclave - members, observers, pillars

x: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a maritime trilateral among India, Sri Lanka and Maldives.

Maritime safety and security corresponds to the maritime domain; trafficking and organised crime to transnational criminal activity; cyber security and critical infrastructure to digital and vital infrastructure protection; and HADR to humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit and secured the New Delhi Declaration by consensus despite
the Iran-UAE conflict
during 12–14 September 2026.
BRICS is criticised for lacking a coherent identity: Russia, China and Iran are associated with an “anti-West” orientation, whereas India, Brazil and South Africa are described as “non-West.”.

rows.title: Export control and security regimes - NPT, CTBT, NSG, MTCR, Wassenaar, Australia Group, FATF, IAEA

secs.t: FATF - HQ, grey and black lists, India's evaluation, APG

x: The FATF secretariat is situated in
Paris
and is associated with the OECD.
A call for action characterises the black list, not merely the grey list.
India's mutual evaluation, adopted in June 2024, placed it in the category of
regular follow-up
The APG is a
FATF-style regional body
, and India is a member of it.

secs.t: Nuclear deals and arms-control treaties → parties

x: The JCPOA involved Iran, the P5+1—United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, China and Germany—and the European Union.
The CCW concerns inhumane conventional weapons and India is party to all five protocols.
The United States and Israel struck Iran's nuclear sites in June 2025, while Iran's Parliament weighed NPT exit in March 2026.

secs.t: IAEA - HQ, safeguards, Additional Protocol, Iran/North Korea

x: Rafael Grossi, the IAEA Director General, expressed concern over hits on Iran's nuclear sites and chaired the NSG in 2016.
The India-Canada deal provides
10,000 tonnes
of uranium under IAEA safeguards for India's pressurised heavy water reactors during 2027–2035.
The separation plan identified civilian facilities for IAEA safeguards, thereby enabling NSG members to supply nuclear fuel while excluding military facilities.

secs.t: NPT and CTBT - nuclear-weapon states, India's objections, RevCons

x: The NPT was signed in 1968, entered into force in 1970, was extended indefinitely in 1995, and recognises only the five NPT nuclear-weapon states.
India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests.
Because decisions are based on consensus, a single state can block an outcome at an NPT Review Conference.

secs.t: Chemical and biological weapons - CWC, BWC, OPCW

x: The CWC was signed in 1993 and entered into force in 1997.
India is a party to the CWC and completed the declaration and destruction of its chemical-weapons stockpile in 2009.
The OPCW is headquartered at
The Hague
and implements the CWC.
The OPCW's organs include the Conference of States Parties, Executive Council and Technical Secretariat.

secs.t: NSG - origin, size, waiver, opposition

x: The NSG was formed in 1975, popularly known as the London Club, in response to India's 1974 Pokhran-I test.
The NSG is voluntary and consensus-based and has 48 members.
The 2008 waiver permits civil nuclear trade and the import of uranium and reactors by India.

secs.t: Regime → year, members, subject

x: The NPT dates from 1968 and entered into force in 1970, the CTBT from 1996, the NSG from 1975 and the MTCR from 1987.
The MTCR control threshold specified here is 500 kg over a range of 300 km, relating to missiles and drones.
The Wassenaar Arrangement, established in 1996 with 42 members, controls
conventional arms and dual-use goods
and is based in Vienna.

secs.t: TPNW, FMCT and nuclear-weapon-free zones - India's position

x: India did not sign the TPNW and has stated that the treaty adds nothing to customary law.
India supports negotiation of the FMCT at the Conference on Disarmament, provided it is universal, verifiable, non-discriminatory and does not cap existing stocks.
Tlatelolco concerns Latin America, Rarotonga the South Pacific, Bangkok Southeast Asia and Pelindaba Africa.
The Treaty of Semipalatinsk establishes the nuclear-weapon-free-zone framework for
Central Asia

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The identified 2026 developments include New START's expiry, debate over Iran's NPT exit, and India's securing of long-term uranium from Canada and Australia.
India’s description as a de facto responsible nuclear state is linked to its NFU doctrine, export controls and entry into three of the four regimes referred to.
The criticism of unequal treatment is directly linked to the absence of disarmament deadlines for recognised nuclear powers while they may modernise their arsenals.

rows.title: India in UN peacekeeping; development partnership and lines of credit; diaspora policy; soft power

secs.t: UN peacekeeping missions → host country, India's rank, all-women FPU

x: The listed present deployments include the Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, Abyei, Lebanon and the Golan Heights;
Haiti
is not included in that list.
UNMISS is in South Sudan, India is its largest troop contributor with 1,775 troops, and 210 Indian peacekeepers received the UN Medal in August 2026.

secs.t: Peacekeeping principles, Centre for UN Peacekeeping

x: Exam angle: statement questions on use of force and who withdraws a mission; mission-host-period matching.
The three principles are consent of the parties, impartiality, and no use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate.
The
UN Security Council
creates and terminates peacekeeping missions through resolutions, while the Department of Peace Operations manages them.
Resolution 2823 (2026) strengthens accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers, commonly known as Blue Helmets.

secs.t: Diaspora policy - Singhvi Committee, PBD, OCI, Samman

x: The Singhvi Committee recommended Pravasi Bharatiya Divas and a status similar to dual citizenship.
The 18th PBD was held in Bhubaneswar from 8 to 10 January 2025 with the theme “
Diaspora's Contribution to a Viksit Bharat
The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is the highest honour for overseas Indians and is conferred by the President at PBD.

secs.t: Diaspora data - largest diaspora, remittances, Telugu diaspora

x: The
United Arab Emirates
had approximately 3.5 million Indians in the cited December 2025 data.
Indian-origin people became Australia's largest immigrant-born community after overtaking the UK-born community for the first time.

secs.t: Soft power - ICCR, Festival of India, Yoga Day, Nalanda, Buddhist circuit

x: The first Festival of India was held in the United Kingdom in 1982, the next editions in the USA and France in 1985–86, and a later edition in the USSR in 1987–88.
The Buddhist circuit and Buddha Purnima events use India's
shared Buddhist heritage
as an instrument of soft power.

secs.t: Development partnership - DPA, ITEC, EXIM Bank LoCs, grant projects

x: ITEC was launched on 15 September 1964 as a training-based capacity-building programme, and e-ITEC is its online form.
The EXIM Bank extends concessional Lines of Credit to foreign governments, enabling them to import Indian goods and services.
The Salma Dam and Parliament building are in Afghanistan; Metro Express is in Mauritius; and the Indian Housing Project is in Sri Lanka.

secs.t: HADR operations → country

x: Operation Maitri was conducted in response to the Nepal earthquake in 2015.
Operation Kaveri was associated with the Sudan evacuation in April 2023.
Dost concerned the Türkiye and Syria earthquakes; Kaveri concerned Sudan; Ajay concerned Israel; and Ganga concerned Ukraine.
The Vande Bharat Mission facilitated worldwide COVID-19 repatriation in 2020.

secs.t: Vaccine Maitri and DPI diplomacy

x: Vaccine Maitri refers to India’s
supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries
and was launched in January 2021.
The India Stack referred to in DPI diplomacy includes Aadhaar, UPI and DigiLocker.

secs.t: Scholarships and training - ICCR, Study in India, e-ITEC

x: ICCR scholarships and ITEC/e-ITEC training are soft-power instruments that build goodwill through education, capacity building and people-to-people links.
Study in India is a Ministry of Education programme launched in 2018 to attract foreign students.
ICCR scholarships are a soft-power instrument for engagement with foreign nationals.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Liberia was the location of
the first all-women Formed Police Unit
in UN peacekeeping.
The reported figure was 210 UN Medals for Indian peacekeepers serving in UNMISS.
Recognition of a diaspora community or its contribution is not the same as strategic alignment with the host country.
The diaspora may be portrayed as
a liability
in Australian domestic political debates.

rows.title: India's energy and maritime diplomacy; connectivity projects (Chabahar, INSTC, IMEC)

secs.t: Maritime diplomacy - SAGAR, IFC-IOR, Djibouti Code, naval exercises

x: SAGAR aims to make India a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and is viewed as countering China's String of Pearls strategy.
MAHASAGAR was introduced in 2025, extends SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and Global South, and SHANTI is framed as a subsequent Bay of Bengal maritime-security framework.
MILAN is hosted by the Indian Navy, its 2022 and 2024 editions were at Visakhapatnam, and AIKEYME's first edition was held at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, in 2025.

secs.t: Connectivity projects → countries and route

x: The India-Middle East-Europe Corridor was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in
September 2023
The listed IMEC participants are India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the European Union, France, Germany, Italy and the United States.
The newer initiative involves
Armenia, Iran and India
and promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor.

secs.t: Energy diplomacy - pipelines, crude sources, SPR, LNG

x: All three statements are correct: about half of crude imports pass through Hormuz, the UAE is the fourth-largest supplier, and it is the only country stated to store oil in India’s SPR.
India holds an Energy Dialogue with OPEC, engages the International Energy Forum and the International Energy Agency, and obtains uranium from Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

secs.t: Chabahar - access, operator, contract, sanctions

x: Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia without relying on Pakistan and also links into the INSTC.
India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal through India Ports Global Ltd, or IPGL.
The MEA said the terminal was not damaged, while the Chabahar-Zahedan railway and Farzad-B gas field remained stalled, with US sanctions forming the main divergence.

secs.t: IONS; Indian Ocean militarisation and foreign bases

x: IONS is a voluntary forum covering maritime security, maritime domain awareness and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.
Djibouti hosts China’s first overseas base, established in 2017, and the US Camp Lemonnier.
The sinking of
IRIS Dena
by the United States in 2026 was described as challenging India’s net security provider claim.

secs.t: Energy groupings - ISA, OSOWOG, GBA, IEA

x: One Sun One World One Grid is identified as a flagship initiative associated with the
International Solar Alliance
India engages with OPEC through an Energy Dialogue and also works with the International Energy Forum and the IEA.
The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 during
India’s G20 presidency
The Global Biofuels Alliance has
32 countries and 14 international organisations
as the stated participants.

secs.t: Ports abroad and strategic access → country

x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Colombo West is in Sri Lanka, Chabahar in Iran, Sittwe in Myanmar and Duqm in Oman.
Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang
are identified as India’s counters to China’s BRI.

secs.t: UNCLOS, India-Bangladesh arbitration, Deep Ocean Mission

x: The continental shelf may extend up to
350 nautical miles
from the baseline under the stated framework.
The 2014 PCA award gave Bangladesh approximately
19,467 sq km
out of the 25,602 sq km disputed area.
Samudrayaan is part of the Deep Ocean Mission and concerns deep-sea mining and the study of polymetallic nodules.

secs.t: AP role - Eastern Naval Command, IFR, AP ports

x: The Eastern Naval Command is headquartered at Visakhapatnam and faces the Bay of Bengal.
President Droupadi Murmu reviewed the fleet from the Presidential Yacht INS Sumedha.
Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three
Strategic Petroleum Reserves

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated comparison is a thin Indian SPR buffer of 9.5 days against the IEA’s 90-day benchmark.
Stalled Iran projects under US sanctions and disruption around Hormuz are identified as current challenges affecting India’s diplomacy.
India’s IONS chairship and command of
CTF-154
are highlighted as current developments.
The shipbuilding package is valued at Rs 69,725 crore and includes a Maritime Development Fund of Rs 25,000 crore.

secs.t: Border management - Department of Border Management; border guarding forces

x: The ITBP was raised in 1962 and operates along the high-altitude China border between Karakoram Pass and Jachep La.
The Army guards both the LoC with Pakistan and the LAC with China, while the Navy has overall maritime security.
The BSF jurisdiction in Punjab and West Bengal was extended from 15 km to
50 km
inside the international border.

secs.t: Security operations → region and purpose

x: Operation Cactus was conducted in the
Maldives
in 1988 to reverse a coup attempt.
Operation Sadbhavana involves Army civic action, popularly described as a hearts-and-minds effort, in Jammu and Kashmir.
All three statements are correct: Cactus was conducted in 1988, Blue Star concerned the Golden Temple, and Sadbhavana is a civic-action effort in J&K.

secs.t: Insurgent and terror groups → base and founder; Manipur

x: ULFA is based in Assam, NSCN in Nagaland, Lashkar-e-Taiba in Pakistan and the People's War Group in Andhra Pradesh.
The People's War Group was founded by
Kondapalli Seetharamaiah
The People's War Group merged into the CPI (Maoist) in 2004.
The conflict in Manipur has primarily been between the
Meitei and Kuki
communities since May 2023.

secs.t: Anti-terror and security laws → year; major attacks → year

x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, and Section 113 defines a terrorist act.
The Mumbai serial blasts occurred in
March 1993
and involved 13 blasts with more than 250 deaths.
The correct sequence is Rajiv Gandhi assassination in 1991, Mumbai serial blasts in 1993, Coimbatore blasts in 1998 and Parliament attack in 2001.

secs.t: Left Wing Extremism and AP - Greyhounds, AOB

x: The Greyhounds, Andhra Pradesh’s special anti-Naxal force, were raised in 1989.
The Greyhounds are based at
Anandapuram in Visakhapatnam
The Greyhounds have sharply reduced Naxal activity in Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
The Andhra-Odisha Border is abbreviated as
AOB
The concept focuses on developing areas cleared of LWE to prevent the resurgence of extremism.

secs.t: Chief of Defence Staff

x: The post of Chief of Defence Staff was created in
December 2019
The CDS is not the Chairman of the UPSC.
The CDS is the military adviser to the
Nuclear Command Authority
The age limit for the Chief of Defence Staff is
65 years

secs.t: Security agencies → parent ministry / location

x: Mahesh Dixit
, an Andhra Pradesh cadre officer of the 1993 IPS batch, was appointed as the head of the Intelligence Bureau in June 2026.
The National Security Guard is popularly known as the
Black Cats
and is a counter-terror force under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
The NSG played a key role in the response to the 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks.

secs.t: Cross-border linkages - drug crescents, terror financing, FICN

x: Hawala, money laundering, black money, FICN and narcotics are all identified as channels or instruments linked with terror financing.
The National Counter-Terrorism Policy provides a common SOP for States, addresses online radicalisation and envisages wider use of NATGRID.
The Indus Waters Treaty has been in abeyance since
23 April 2025
, subject to Pakistan ending cross-border terrorism.

secs.t: Land and coastal borders - lengths, CIBMS, VVP, coastal security

x: The correct order is Bangladesh (4,096.7 km), China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km) and Nepal (1,751 km).
CIBMS is a technology-based smart-fencing system intended for the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders.
Viksit VVP Phase I covers Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Ladakh.
The Navy has overall responsibility, the Coast Guard operates in territorial waters, and coastal police operate in shallow waters.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: PRAHAAR is associated with the 2026 intelligence-led, whole-of-government counter-terrorism approach, not the 1988 SPG legislation.
Greyhounds, the AOB, and the ASR and Manyam districts are all identified in the Andhra Pradesh internal-security context.
The Andhra Pradesh cadre officer heads the IB, which is an internal intelligence agency under the MHA; RAW is the external intelligence agency under the Cabinet Secretariat.

sub: Group-II S3-44: Social security programmes - pensions, insurance, health coverage, PDS

secs.t: Health programmes → objective and launch year

x: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health assurance of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
Ayushman Arogya Mandir aims to provide comprehensive primary care through about 1.5 lakh upgraded Health and Wellness Centres.
PM-ABHIM covers district critical-care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories, BSL-3 laboratories and pandemic preparedness.
Janani Suraksha Yojana provides cash assistance for institutional delivery under the NHM and is 100 per cent centrally sponsored.

secs.t: Scheme → objective and launch year (matching)

x: The
Ujjwala
scheme, providing free LPG connections to BPL women, was launched at Ballia in 2016.

secs.t: Education programmes → objective

x: Operation Blackboard was launched to provide
minimum facilities in primary schools
, particularly in educationally backward areas.
PM-Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free and guarantor-free loans to students admitted to top-quality higher educational institutions.
Samagra Shiksha covers education from
pre-school to Class 12
and merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.
NIPUN Bharat aims to achieve foundational literacy and numeracy by
Grade 3

secs.t: Food security and nutrition - NFSA, POSHAN, ONORC

x: The Ministry of
Women and Child Development
is the nodal ministry for POSHAN Abhiyaan.
POSHAN Abhiyaan brings together ICDS, NHM and Swachh Bharat to address stunting, under-nutrition, anaemia and low birth weight.
Mission Poshan 2.0 focuses on
diet diversity, fortification and millets
One Nation One Ration Card enables NFSA beneficiaries to access ration benefits anywhere in India.

secs.t: Scheme → nodal ministry / agency; AP Aarogyasri

x: Dr NTR Vaidya Seva covers approximately
1.43 crore families and 3,257 procedures
through cashless care.
The Universal Health Policy provides free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh for every citizen, while poor persons receive treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
The budget allocations were ₹222 crore for 108 ambulance services, ₹128 crore for 104 services and ₹4,000 crore for the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.

secs.t: Sanitation and drinking water - SBM, NAMASTE, ISC, JJM

x: NAMASTE profiles workers, provides PM-JAY coverage, training with a ₹3,000 stipend and PPE.
The new phase of NAMASTE covers 500 AMRUT cities and includes Emergency Response Sanitation Units and PMKVY training.
Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana was launched in 2007, Swachh Bharat Mission in 2014, Jal Jeevan Mission in 2019 and eShram in 2021.

secs.t: Housing - PMAY-G, PMAY-U, Housing for All, RAY

x: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin was restructured from
Indira Awaas Yojana
The PMAY-U components include in-situ slum redevelopment, credit-linked subsidy, affordable housing in partnership and beneficiary-led construction.
Registration of houses in women's names gives PMAY the character of a
gender-budget scheme
Rajiv Awas Yojana aimed at creating
a slum-free India
and was subsumed into PMAY-U in 2015.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - target group, cover, eligibility basis, implementing authority, senior citizen expansion

x: PM-JAY was launched at Ranchi in September 2018, was earlier called the National Health Protection Scheme, and subsumed RSBY of 2008.
PM-JAY provides cashless and paperless cover of
₹5 lakh per family
per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.
PM-JAY uses SECC 2011 deprivation criteria, comprising six rural and eleven urban occupational criteria.
PM-JAY targets the bottom 40 per cent, approximately 10.74 crore poor and deprived families, especially rural and poor households.

secs.t: Pension schemes - NPS, APY, PM-SYM, PM-KMY, NPS-Traders

x: All four statements correctly describe NPS, including its defined-contribution character, PRAN, the two tiers and the additional ₹50,000 deduction under Section 80CCD(1B).
APY covers unorganised workers with a bank account; PM-SYM covers unorganised workers earning up to ₹15,000 monthly; PM-KMY covers small and marginal farmers; NPS-Traders covers eligible traders.
APY was launched on 9 May 2015, replaced Swavalamban, covers entry ages 18–40 and has government support extended to FY 2030–31.
The spouse receives
50 per cent of the pension
as family pension under PM-SYM, PM-KMY and NPS-Traders.

secs.t: PDS and food security - TPDS evolution, special schemes for the poorest and destitute elderly, NFSA 2013, ONORC

x: The correct sequence is wartime rationing in the 1940s, FCI and Agricultural Prices Commission in 1965, RPDS in June 1992, and TPDS in June 1997.
Antyodaya Anna Yojana, introduced among the special schemes of 2000, targets
the poorest of the poor
and provides 35 kg per household per month.
ONORC operates throughout the country, with 99.9 per cent Aadhaar seeding, 79.8 crore NFSA beneficiaries and 81.35 crore people receiving free grain under the reported figures.

secs.t: NSAP components and state pension schemes for workers and artisans

x: NSAP gives effect to
Article 41
of the Directive Principles, relating to public assistance in cases including old age, sickness and disablement.
IGNOAPS covers BPL elderly persons, IGNWPS widows, IGNDPS persons with at least 80 per cent disability, and NFBS follows the specified breadwinner-age condition.
Mukhyamantri Vishwakarma Pension Yojana is a
Rajasthan
scheme for workers, street vendors and folk artists at the age of 60.

secs.t: ESI and EPF - establishments covered, wage ceiling, contribution rates, benefits

x: EPF generally covers establishments with 20 or more employees, and the normal contribution rate is 12% each from the employee and employer.
The revised ceiling is expected to add more than
51 lakh employees
to mandatory EPFO coverage.
The principal EPFO-linked benefits are provident fund accumulation, pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme and insurance under EDLI.

secs.t: Social security schemes - launch year chronology

x: NSAP was launched in 1995, Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Annapurna in 2000, Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana in 2007, and NPS for government staff in 2004.
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and Atal Pension Yojana were launched on 9 May 2015.
UPS and NPS Vatsalya
are listed under 2025. e-Shram was launched in 2021, PM-JAY in 2018 and PMSBY and PMJJBY in 2015.

secs.t: Code on Social Security 2020 - gig and platform workers, e-Shram, unorganised workers

x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 merged nine laws, including laws relating to EPF, ESI, maternity benefit, gratuity and unorganised workers' social security.
The
National Social Security Board
recommends social-security schemes for gig and platform workers under the framework.
The 2024 One-Stop Solution links up
15 schemes
for the benefit of e-Shram registrants.

secs.t: Social security concepts - social insurance vs social assistance, ILO minimum standards convention

x: NSAP, NFSA and PM-JAY
are non-contributory, tax-funded and means-tested forms of social assistance.
The proposed Universal Social Protection Floor covers health, maternity, disability, old age and basic income.

ILO Convention No. 102 lays down minimum standards for nine branches, including medical care, sickness, unemployment, old age, employment injury, family, maternity, invalidity and survivors' benefits.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposal seeks convergence of PMAY with JJM, SBM, rooftop solar and Ujjwala.
The EPFO will not reopen the higher-pension window, while 4.4 lakh demand letters have been issued.
Insurance penetration was reported at 3.7%, while insurance density rose to USD 97 in FY25.
The share of persons aged 60 years and above is projected to increase from 10.1% to 14.9% during
